Because after the verb in an affirmative imperative, me becomes moi.
questions.explanation: In the affirmative imperative the pronoun goes after the verb with a hyphen, and me becomes moi (lesson 05): Prête-moi, Ouvre-moi. In the negative it stays me, before the verb: Ne me prête pas ta plume.

questions.stem: Complete the line from Au clair de la lune (I have no fire any more): Ma chandelle est morte, je n'ai ___ de feu.
questions.explanation: Ne … plus = no longer, not any more (lesson 17), and after it du feu becomes de feu.

questions.stem: In "Sur le pont d'Avignon, l'on y danse", what does "y" stand for?
questions.explanation: Y replaces a place introduced by a preposition such as à or sur (lesson 07): on danse sur le pont → on y danse. L'on is an older, elegant form of on.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this song map.

image.alt: A song map with no labels. Top: the title Au clair de la lune above a music staff with eleven notes and the words under them. Bottom: five boxes for Sur le pont d'Avignon: Sur le pont d'Avignon, Les beaux messieurs, Sur le pont d'Avignon, Les belles dames, Sur le pont d'Avignon. Five parts are numbered.

questions.explanation: 1 the title (le titre), 2 the notes: the tune (la mélodie), 3 the words under the notes (les paroles), 4 the part that comes back three times, Sur le pont d'Avignon: the refrain, 5 Les beaux messieurs, a couplet whose words change (next time: les belles dames).

questions.stem: Who wrote the words of Le Temps des cerises, and when?
questions.explanation: Jean-Baptiste Clément wrote the words in 1866, and Antoine Renard set them to music in 1868. The song was later tied to the Paris Commune of 1871. Adolphe Adam made Sur le pont d'Avignon famous in 1853.

questions.stem: Which of these are futur simple forms? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Serons and seront come from être (stem ser-), auront from avoir (aur-), and sifflera from siffler (infinitive + -a). Étaient is the imparfait of être, chante the present.

questions.stem: Why does the song say "Quand nous en serons au temps des cerises" and not "Quand nous en sommes …"?
choices: Because after quand, French uses the futur when the time is in the future.
Because quand is always followed by the futur.
Because the song is too old for the present tense.
questions.explanation: The time is in the future, so French uses the futur after quand, where English uses the present ("when we get to"; lesson 13). Quand is not always followed by the futur: Quand j'étais petit… looks back.

questions.stem: Match each singer to a fact from the lesson.
choices: from Sète, sang alone with his guitar
wrote Göttingen after a concert there in 1964
wrote the music of Le Temps des cerises
questions.explanation: Piaf (1915–1963) was la Môme Piaf, the kid sparrow; Brassens (1921–1981) came from Sète; Brel (1929–1978) was Belgian; Barbara (1930–1997) wrote Göttingen in 1964. The music of Le Temps des cerises is by Antoine Renard.

questions.stem: "Sifflera bien mieux le merle moqueur." Which sentence says the same in ordinary word order?
choices: Le merle moqueur sifflerait bien mieux.
Le merle moqueur siffle bien mieux.
Le merle moqueur a sifflé bien mieux.
Le merle moqueur sifflera bien mieux.
questions.explanation: Songs and poems may put the subject after the verb. In ordinary order: le merle moqueur sifflera bien mieux, still in the futur. Sifflerait is the conditionnel, siffle the present, a sifflé the passé composé.

questions.stem: Put the story of Le Temps des cerises in time order.
choices: Antoine Renard sets them to music.
The Paris Commune is crushed in the Semaine sanglante.
Clément publishes the song with a dedication to Louise, a nurse.
questions.explanation: The words date from 1866 and the music from 1868; the Commune ended in May 1871; the dedication to Louise, whom Clément met on 28 May 1871, appears in 1882.

questions.stem: What does "Je n'ai plus de feu" mean in Au clair de la lune?
choices: I no longer have any fire.
questions.explanation: Ne … plus = no longer (lesson 17). The singer's candle has gone out, so there is no light any more. Never would be ne … jamais, only ne … que.

questions.stem: In French, the lyrics of a song are les ___.
questions.explanation: Les paroles (plural, feminine) are the words of a song. Les mots are words in general.

questions.stem: A song that looks back at childhood and the past is full of ___.
questions.explanation: La nostalgie is longing for the past. Such songs often use the imparfait (Quand j'étais petit…). Le rythme is the beat, le micro the microphone, le tube a hit.

questions.stem: When did the Lumière brothers give their first public screening for a paying audience, at the Grand Café in Paris?
questions.explanation: It was Saturday 28 December 1895, in the Salon indien of the Grand Café on the boulevard des Capucines: ten films of under a minute each. 20 September 1946 is the first Cannes festival.

questions.stem: What is Georges Méliès best known for?
choices: Le Voyage dans la Lune (1902) and its camera tricks
questions.explanation: Méliès, a magician who ran the Théâtre Robert-Houdin, made about 500 films in his studio at Montreuil, full of tricks and early special effects; Le Voyage dans la Lune (1902) is the most famous. À bout de souffle is Godard's (1960).

questions.stem: Put each event on the timeline of French cinema.

image.alt: A timeline of French cinema from 1890 to today with year marks every 25 years and five numbered dots, at 1895, 1902, 1946, 1959 and 1976. The events are not named.

choices: Méliès : Le Voyage dans la Lune
questions.explanation: 1895 the Lumière screening, 1902 Le Voyage dans la Lune, 1946 the first Cannes festival (planned for 1939), 1959 the Nouvelle Vague (Les Quatre Cents Coups at Cannes), 1976 the first César ceremony.

questions.stem: Which sentence about the Cannes festival is true?
choices: It was planned for September 1939, but the war stopped it; the first one opened in 1946.
It began in 1895 with the Lumière brothers.
It began in 1976, together with the César.
It has been held every September since 1939.
questions.explanation: The first festival was planned for 1–20 September 1939 and cancelled when the Second World War broke out; it finally opened on 20 September 1946, and has been held in May since 1952.

questions.stem: Match each cinema term to its meaning.
choices: the original language with French subtitles
questions.explanation: VO = version originale, VOST = version originale sous-titrée, VF = version française (doublée). In practice a VO showing in France is usually subtitled too; VOST says so explicitly. A silent film is un film muet.

questions.stem: Which of these describe the Nouvelle Vague? Select all that apply.
choices: shooting in the streets rather than in studios
huge budgets and big studio sets
directors such as Truffaut, Godard and Varda
questions.explanation: The Nouvelle Vague of the late 1950s left the studios for the streets, with light cameras, small teams and small budgets: Truffaut, Godard, Varda and others. Big studio sets are what they reacted against, and silent films belong to Méliès's time.

questions.stem: Complete with a relative pronoun: C'est une comédie ___ fait rire toute la salle.
questions.explanation: The gap needs a subject for "fait" (the comedy makes people laugh), so qui (lesson 10).

questions.stem: Malik est le personnage ___ je préfère.
questions.explanation: Je is the subject of préfère, and the gap is its object (je préfère ce personnage), so que. Qui would be a subject; où is for place and time; dont needs a verb with de (12h1).

questions.stem: Le village ___ se passe l'histoire est magnifique.
questions.explanation: A place, so où: the story takes place in the village. After où the subject (l'histoire) often follows a short verb. Que would need a direct object, qui a subject in the gap.

questions.stem: The ending disappointed you. Choose the right word: "La fin est ___."
questions.explanation: The thing that disappoints is décevant(e), and la fin is feminine: décevante. Déçu(e) describes the person who is disappointed: je suis déçu(e).

questions.stem: Put the parts of a short review in the order the lesson recommends.
choices: A short summary in the present, without the ending
What you liked and liked less, with reasons
questions.explanation: Start with the facts, summarise without giving away the end, give your opinion with reasons, and finish with a recommendation (Je le recommande à …) and a mark.

questions.stem: What is true of a synopsis?
choices: It is in the passé simple, like a tale.
It is in the futur, because the film is coming out.
It tells the whole story, ending included.
It is a short summary in the present that stops before the end.
questions.explanation: Un synopsis (masculine) summarises the plot (l'intrigue) in the present: Lucie perd son travail, elle retourne au village… and keeps the ending secret.

questions.stem: Build the end of the review: "It's one of the best films of the year."
questions.explanation: C'est un des meilleurs films de l'année: meilleur is the comparative of bon (never plus bon), and after a superlative French uses de (lesson 09).

questions.stem: Who or what are the César awards named after?
choices: the sculptor César, who designed the trophy
the first actor to win one
questions.explanation: The trophy, a block of compressed metal, was designed by the sculptor César (César Baldaccini), and the awards are named after him. The first ceremony was on 3 April 1976.

questions.stem: Kate writes: "Ma famille me manque." What does she mean?
questions.explanation: With manquer, what you miss is the subject: ma famille me manque = I miss my family (literally, my family is missing to me). "My family misses me" would be je manque à ma famille.

questions.stem: Back in Cork, Kate writes "I miss Lyon already". Which is right?
choices: Je me manque de Lyon déjà.
questions.explanation: Lyon is the subject, and Kate is the indirect object me before the verb: Lyon me manque. The English order (je manque Lyon) is the classic mistake.

questions.stem: Match each numbered month to what happened in Kate's year.

image.alt: Kate's year as a strip of twelve months from September to August with no labels: a suitcase in September, a key in October, a bank card in February, mountains and a lake in May, an open book in June and a plane in August. Six months are numbered.

questions.explanation: September: arrival; October: the room in a flat-share; February: the cash machine swallows her card; May: the weekend in Annecy with Léa; June: the last day at the bookshop; August: back in Cork. Kate went home for Christmas in December, which has no number.

questions.stem: Kate writes to a landlord she doesn't know. How does she begin?
questions.explanation: A formal e-mail to someone you don't know opens with Madame, Monsieur, and closes with a formal formula or Cordialement. Salut and Coucou are for friends; Bises is a closing for friends and family.

questions.stem: In "Pourriez-vous me dire si la chambre est encore disponible ?", what is "pourriez-vous"?
choices: the conditionnel, for a polite request
questions.explanation: Pourriez is the conditionnel of pouvoir: the future stem pourr- + the imparfait ending -iez (lesson 14). The futur would be pourrez, the imparfait pouviez, the present pouvez.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct French? Select all that apply.
choices: Je voudrais savoir quand je pourrais la visiter.
Je voudrais savoir quand est-ce que je peux la visiter.
Pourriez-vous me dire si la chambre est libre ?
Pourriez-vous me dire est-ce que la chambre est libre ?
Je me demande combien coûtent les charges.
questions.explanation: In an indirect question the question word stays (quand, combien), a yes/no question uses si, and there is no est-ce que and no inversion of the pronoun (lesson 19). Inverting a noun subject after combien (combien coûtent les charges) is normal.

questions.stem: Hugo: "Et du lait, il y en a encore ?" Kate: "Non, il n'y ___ a plus."
questions.explanation: En replaces du lait (lesson 07), and with il y a it gives il y en a; in the negative, il n'y en a plus (no more).

questions.stem: Kate writes about her flatmates: "Hugo et Mathilde m'ont très bien ___."
questions.explanation: The direct object m' (Kate, a woman) comes before avoir, so the participle agrees with it: accueillie (lesson 08). It doesn't agree with the subject Hugo et Mathilde, because the auxiliary is avoir.

questions.stem: Put the events of Kate's year in order.
choices: Kate arrive à Lyon et dort dans une auberge de jeunesse.
Elle écrit pour une chambre en colocation.
Elle rentre à Cork pour Noël.
Un distributeur avale sa carte bancaire.
Elle passe un week-end à Annecy avec Léa.
Elle fait ses adieux à ses collègues.
questions.explanation: September (arrival), October (the flat-share), December (Christmas at home), February (the card), May (Annecy) and June (the last day at the bookshop).

questions.stem: In "Comme l'agence était fermée, je n'ai pas pu la récupérer", what does "comme" express?
questions.explanation: Comme at the start of the sentence gives the cause: because the branch was closed (lesson 20). The consequence follows (je n'ai pas pu…; je n'ai donc plus de carte).

questions.stem: Match each sentence from Kate's year to what it does.
left: Grâce à ma conseillère, j'ai eu une nouvelle carte.
Je rentrerai à Cork le 22 décembre.
choices: a good result and its cause
questions.explanation: Si on + imparfait is a suggestion (lesson 22); grâce à gives the cause of a good result (20); j'aimerais is a wish in the conditionnel (14); the futur gives a plan (13).

questions.stem: "Il y a un an, je n'osais pas commander un café ; aujourd'hui, je lis des romans !" Which tenses does Kate use, and why?
choices: The imparfait for how things used to be, and the present for now
The passé composé for one event, and the futur for a plan
The passé simple, because it is a story
The conditionnel for a wish, and the present for a fact
questions.explanation: Osais is the imparfait: how she was a year ago. Lis is the present: how she is now. Il y a un an = a year ago (lesson 03).

questions.stem: Build Kate's sentence: "I will never forget the Saturday customers."
questions.explanation: Je n'oublierai jamais les clients du samedi: ne and jamais go around the conjugated verb (lesson 17), here a futur (n'oublierai). Pas would make ne … pas jamais, which is wrong.

questions.stem: Kate's first day: "Le premier jour, il ___ et je ne comprenais rien."
questions.explanation: The weather is the background of that day, like je ne comprenais rien: imparfait, il pleuvait (lessons 01–02). A plu would be a single event, pleut the present, pleuvra the futur.

questions.stem: Complete with the imparfait of "finir": "Quand j'étais petit, je ___ toujours mes devoirs avant le dîner."
questions.explanation: The stem comes from "nous finissons" without -ons: finiss-, + -ais for je: "je finissais". "Finais" builds the stem from the infinitive; "finissait" is the il/elle form; "finirais" is the conditionnel (lesson 14), not a past tense.

questions.stem: Where does the imparfait stem of "prendre" come from?
questions.explanation: Every imparfait except être starts from the nous present without -ons: nous prenons → pren- → je prenais. The infinitive and the je form both give "prend-", which produces the wrong form *prendais.

questions.stem: What is the imparfait of "être" with "nous"?
questions.explanation: Être is the only verb with its own imparfait stem, ét-, plus the normal ending -ions: "nous étions". "Sommions" wrongly starts from "nous sommes"; "êtions" has a circumflex that the imparfait doesn't have; "étons" has the wrong ending.

questions.stem: Choose the correct spelling: "Quand il était petit, il ___ beaucoup de chocolat." (manger)
questions.explanation: -ger verbs keep the e before a, so the g stays soft: "il mangeait". "Mangait" would be read with a hard g; "mangeais" is the je/tu form; "mangeat" is not an imparfait ending.

questions.stem: Choose the correct imparfait: "Au lycée, nous ___ l'anglais et l'espagnol." (étudier)
questions.explanation: The stem is étudi- (from "nous étudions") and the nous ending is -ions, so the imparfait has two i's: "nous étudiions". "Étudions" is the present; "étudiaient" is the ils/elles form.

questions.stem: Why is the imparfait used in "Le samedi, je jouais au foot avec mes copains"?
choices: It describes a habit: something that happened every Saturday.
It tells one event that happened on one Saturday.
It describes something that is about to happen.
It gives the weather on a Saturday.
questions.explanation: "Le samedi" (with le) means "on Saturdays", every Saturday, so this is a habit in the past: the imparfait ("I used to play"). One event on one Saturday would be "samedi, j'ai joué".

questions.stem: Complete the description: "Ma grand-mère ___ les cheveux blancs et elle ___ toujours un chapeau."
questions.explanation: A description of how someone looked and what they always wore is background, so both verbs are imparfait: "avait … portait". "A eu … a porté" tells events, not a description; "était les cheveux blancs" uses the wrong verb (hair takes avoir); "porte" is present.

questions.stem: What does "autrefois" mean?
choices: in the past, in the old days
questions.explanation: "Autrefois" means "in the past, formerly": "Autrefois, il y avait une boulangerie ici." "Later" is "plus tard" and "sometimes" is "parfois".

questions.stem: A French child of 13 usually goes to…
questions.explanation: Le collège is for ages 11 to 15 (sixième to troisième). L'école maternelle is 3 to 6, le lycée 15 to 18, and l'université comes after the bac. Remember: le collège is not a college.

questions.stem: Your French friend says: "Mon fils entre au collège en septembre." How old is her son, most likely?
questions.explanation: Children start le collège (in sixième) at about 11. At about 6 they start l'école élémentaire (CP), at about 15 le lycée, and at about 18 they finish the lycée.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu te souviens ___ ton premier jour d'école ?"
questions.explanation: "Se souvenir" needs "de" before the thing remembered: "se souvenir de quelque chose". "Tu te souviens de ton premier jour d'école ?" — Do you remember your first day at school?

questions.stem: Read: "Quand j'avais huit ans, j'habitais à Lille. Le mercredi, il n'y avait pas d'école, alors j'allais chez ma grand-mère. Elle préparait des crêpes et on regardait des dessins animés." What did the writer usually do on Wednesdays?
questions.explanation: "Le mercredi … j'allais chez ma grand-mère": on Wednesdays (a habit, imparfait) the writer went to the grandmother's. There was no school that day; the grandmother made the pancakes (crêpes); the writer already lived in Lille.

questions.stem: Write the imparfait of "faire": "Quand j'étais petite, je ___ du piano le mardi."
questions.explanation: Nous faisons → stem fais- → "je faisais". Note the pronunciation: "fuh-zè". "Quand j'étais petite, je faisais du piano le mardi." — When I was little I used to play the piano on Tuesdays.

questions.stem: Write the imparfait of "être": "À l'école, nous ___ très bavards."
questions.explanation: Être has the stem ét- in the imparfait: "nous étions". "À l'école, nous étions très bavards." — At school we were very talkative.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "When I was little, I lived in Lyon."
questions.explanation: "Quand j'étais petit, j'habitais à Lyon." Both verbs are imparfait: a description of a time in your life. The capital Q and the comma after "petit" show where the parts go.

questions.stem: Match each verb to its imparfait (je form).
questions.explanation: Each comes from the nous present: nous avons → avais, nous allons → allais, nous voyons → voyais, nous buvons → buvais. "Boivais" starts from "ils boivent" and "voirais" from the infinitive.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Quand j'étais petit, j'avais un chien.
Il faisait beau et les enfants jouaient dehors.
Nous mangions à la cantine tous les jours.
Elle commencait l'école à huit heures.
questions.explanation: The first three are correct imparfaits (avais, faisait, jouaient, mangions: no e before i). The last needs a cedilla before a: "elle commençait".

questions.stem: Name each stage of French school.

image.alt: Four steps rising from left to right, marked with ages 3–6, 6–11, 11–15 and 15–18, with a numbered marker on each step.

questions.explanation: Maternelle 3–6, primaire (élémentaire) 6–11, collège 11–15, lycée 15–18. L'université comes after the lycée; la crèche is a day nursery for babies.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in this school playground.

image.alt: A school playground: a woman in front of the school, a girl holding a small doll, a ball between two boys, a school bag on a bench, and the playground ground, each with a numbered marker.

questions.explanation: The primary-school teacher is la maîtresse (a man would be le maître); the girl holds une poupée; the boys play with un ballon; the school bag is un cartable; the playground is la cour. There is no board (le tableau) or pen (le stylo) in the picture.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je ___ quand le téléphone a sonné."
questions.explanation: The sleeping was going on when the phone interrupted it: the interrupted action is in the imparfait, "je dormais". The interruption ("a sonné") is in the passé composé.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il ___ nuit et il faisait froid quand nous sommes arrivés."
questions.explanation: Night and cold describe the scene when the event (we arrived) happened: background, imparfait: "il faisait nuit". "A fait" would make the darkness an event; "fait" and "fera" are present and future.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Pendant je faisais la cuisine, le chat a mangé le poisson.
Pendant que je fais la cuisine, le chat a mangé le poisson.
Pendant que je faisais la cuisine, le chat a mangé le poisson.
Pendant que je faisais la cuisine, le chat a mangeait le poisson.
questions.explanation: "Pendant que" (while) + the imparfait for what was going on, then the passé composé for the event. "Pendant" alone can't introduce a verb; "je fais" (present) clashes with the past event; "a mangeait" mixes two tenses.

questions.stem: In "Je dormais quand le téléphone a sonné", why is "a sonné" in the passé composé?
choices: It's the event that interrupts what was going on.
questions.explanation: The phone ringing is a single event that cuts into the sleeping, so it takes the passé composé. The sleeping is the background (imparfait).

questions.stem: Which word usually introduces an event in the passé composé?
questions.explanation: "Tout à coup" (suddenly) announces something that happens: "Tout à coup, j'ai entendu un bruit." "D'habitude" and "autrefois" go with habits, and "pendant que" with an action in progress (imparfait).

questions.stem: "Il a fait beau toute la semaine." Why the passé composé here?
choices: It sums up a whole finished period.
It describes the background to another event.
It's a habit that kept repeating.
questions.explanation: With "toute la semaine", the speaker looks back at a closed period and sums it up: passé composé. As background to an event on one day, it would be "il faisait beau".

questions.stem: How do you ask "What happened?"
questions.explanation: Se passer (to happen) takes être, and the thing that happened is the subject, so French uses "qu'est-ce qui": "Qu'est-ce qui s'est passé ?" (or "Qu'est-ce qui est arrivé ?"). "Qu'est-ce que" is for the object; "a passé" uses the wrong auxiliary and drops the se.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il s'est cassé ___ jambe au ski."
questions.explanation: With a reflexive verb and a body part, French uses the article, not a possessive: "Il s'est cassé la jambe." The se already shows whose leg it is. "Le" and "son" have the wrong gender (la jambe).

questions.stem: In "Le voleur a volé mon sac", "voler" means…
questions.explanation: "Voler" has two meanings, "to steal" and "to fly". With a thief (le voleur) and a bag, it's "to steal": The thief stole my bag.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Our car broke down"?
choices: Notre voiture a tombé en panne.
Notre voiture est cassée en panne.
Notre voiture est tombée en panne.
questions.explanation: "Tomber en panne" takes être, like tomber, and the participle agrees with "voiture": "est tombée". "A tombé" uses the wrong auxiliary; "tombait" would mean it kept breaking down (a habit); "cassée en panne" isn't French.

questions.stem: Read: "Samedi dernier, il faisait très froid. Je rentrais à pied du travail quand j'ai glissé sur la neige. Je suis tombé et je me suis cassé le bras. Un homme m'a aidé et il a appelé une ambulance. J'ai eu de la chance : il était médecin !" Why was the writer lucky?
choices: The man who helped him was a doctor.
questions.explanation: "J'ai eu de la chance : il était médecin !" — I was lucky: he was a doctor! The text says it was very cold, he fell and he broke his arm.

questions.stem: Read: "Samedi dernier, il faisait très froid. Je rentrais à pied du travail quand j'ai glissé sur la neige. Je suis tombé et je me suis cassé le bras. Un homme m'a aidé et il a appelé une ambulance. J'ai eu de la chance : il était médecin !" Which verb describes the background?
questions.explanation: "Je rentrais à pied" (I was walking home) is what was going on when the events happened: imparfait. Slipping, falling and calling are events in the passé composé.

questions.stem: Put each verb in the right tense: "Nous ___ (regarder) la télé quand l'orage ___ ___ (commencer)."
questions.explanation: We were watching TV (in progress: imparfait "regardions") when the storm started (event: passé composé "a commencé"). "Nous regardions la télé quand l'orage a commencé."

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "While I was waiting for the bus, I saw an accident."
questions.explanation: "Pendant que j'attendais le bus, j'ai vu un accident." Pendant que + imparfait for the action in progress, then the event in the passé composé.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: La tempête is a storm with strong wind; l'orage a thunderstorm; la panne a breakdown; le témoin a witness; le bruit a noise. Luck is la chance and a cloud is le nuage.

questions.stem: Read: "Il faisait nuit et j'étais fatigué. Soudain, le téléphone a sonné. J'ai répondu." Which verbs give the background? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Il faisait nuit" and "j'étais fatigué" set the scene (imparfait). The phone ringing and the answer are events in the passé composé.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things and people in this stormy street.

image.alt: A stormy street: a dark cloud with lightning, wind lines bending a tree, a broken-down car with steam, a man running with a handbag, a police officer behind him, and a man at a bus stop pointing, each with a numbered marker.

questions.explanation: 1 le nuage (cloud), 2 le vent (wind), 3 la panne (the car has broken down), 4 le voleur (the thief with the bag), 5 le policier (police officer), 6 le témoin (the witness pointing). There is no snow (la neige) in the picture; la chance (luck) isn't a thing you can see.

questions.stem: How do you say "I have lived in Paris for five years" (and still do)?
choices: J'habite à Paris depuis cinq ans.
J'ai habité à Paris depuis cinq ans.
J'habite à Paris pendant cinq ans.
J'ai habité à Paris il y a cinq ans.
questions.explanation: Something that started in the past and is still true: depuis + present. English "have lived" tempts you into the passé composé, but "j'ai habité … depuis" is wrong; "pendant" is for a closed period; "il y a" means ago.

questions.stem: How do you say "I came to France three years ago"?
choices: Je suis venu en France depuis trois ans.
Je suis venu en France il y a trois ans.
Je viens en France il y a trois ans.
Je suis venu en France trois ans il y a.
questions.explanation: "Ago" is il y a + time, before the time, with the passé composé for the event: "il y a trois ans". "Depuis" would need the present and a situation still going on.

questions.stem: Complete: "J'ai vécu à Berlin ___ deux ans : de 2015 à 2017."
questions.explanation: A closed period in the past (from 2015 to 2017, now over) takes pendant: "J'ai vécu à Berlin pendant deux ans." Depuis is for something still going on; dans is for the future; en is for the time something takes.

questions.stem: Complete: "Le train part ___ dix minutes. Dépêche-toi !"
questions.explanation: Dans + time = in (from now): the train leaves ten minutes from now. "En dix minutes" would be the time something takes ("in ten minutes' time" is dans).

questions.stem: Complete: "J'ai fait le trajet ___ trois heures : c'est rapide !"
questions.explanation: En + time = how long something takes: I did the journey in three hours. Dans would mean three hours from now; depuis needs something still going on; à partir de means "from … on".

questions.stem: Which question asks specifically for a length of time, not a starting point?
choices: Depuis combien de temps tu habites ici ?
Quand est-ce que tu es arrivé ?
questions.explanation: "Depuis combien de temps … ?" asks how long (answer: depuis trois ans). "Depuis quand … ?" asks for the starting point (depuis 2021), though in speech it's often used for both. The other two ask when.

questions.stem: "Ça fait deux ans que je travaille ici." means…
choices: I worked here two years ago.
I'll work here in two years.
I worked here for two years, but not any more.
I've been working here for two years (and still am).
questions.explanation: Ça fait + time + que + present = for (still going on), like depuis: "Je travaille ici depuis deux ans."

questions.stem: Complete: "___ qu'elle est à la retraite, elle voyage beaucoup."
questions.explanation: Before a whole clause (a subject and verb), use "depuis que": "Depuis qu'elle est à la retraite …" — Since she retired, she has been travelling a lot. "Ça fait" and "il y a" need a length of time before que; "en" can't introduce a clause.

questions.stem: How do you read "le XXIe siècle"?
questions.explanation: Centuries are read as ordinals: XXI → vingt et unième (with "et", like vingt et un). "Le vingt et un siècle" uses the plain number, which French doesn't do for centuries.

questions.stem: "Dès 7 heures du matin, il y avait du monde." means…
choices: Until 7 a.m., there were lots of people.
At about 7 a.m., there was nobody.
From as early as 7 a.m., there were lots of people.
questions.explanation: "Dès" means "from (as early as)", stressing that it's early. "Until" is jusqu'à; "about" is vers or environ.

questions.stem: "Il a pris sa retraite l'année dernière." means…
choices: He took his pension money last year.
He went back to work last year.
questions.explanation: "Prendre sa retraite" is "to retire": he retired last year. "Être à la retraite" is "to be retired".

questions.stem: Read: "Paul est né en 1980 à Nantes. Il a fait ses études à Paris, puis il s'est installé à Bordeaux en 2008. Il s'est marié en 2010. Il travaille dans une banque depuis 2012." Which statement is true?
choices: He has worked in a bank since 2012 and still does.
He no longer works in a bank.
questions.explanation: "Il travaille dans une banque depuis 2012": depuis + present, so he still works there. He moved to Bordeaux in 2008 and married in 2010; he studied in Paris.

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "J'apprends le français ___ trois ans." (I've been learning French for three years.)
questions.explanation: Still going on, so depuis + present: "J'apprends le français depuis trois ans." You could also say "Ça fait trois ans que j'apprends le français."

questions.stem: Write "durer" in the present: "Le film ___ deux heures." (The film lasts two hours.)
questions.explanation: "Durer" is a regular -er verb: "le film dure deux heures". It is mostly used with a thing as subject.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "I've been waiting for an hour!"
questions.explanation: "Ça fait une heure que j'attends !" Ça fait + length of time + que + present.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Ça fait trois ans que j'habite ici.
J'ai habité ici depuis trois ans.
questions.explanation: Depuis works with a date or a length of time, + present. "Ça fait … que" works only with a length of time, never a date. "J'ai habité ici depuis …" wrongly uses the passé composé for something still true.

questions.stem: Each line shows one time expression. Name them.

image.alt: Five timelines with a dashed line marking now: a point in the past; a bar from that point up to now with an arrow going on; a closed bar in the past; a short bracketed span; and a dashed arrow from now to a point in the future. Each has a numbered marker.

questions.explanation: Il y a = a point in the past (ago). Depuis = from that point up to now and still going on. Pendant = a closed period with a beginning and an end. En = the time something takes. Dans = a point in the future, counted from now.

questions.topic: Venir de and être en train de
questions.stem: How do you say "I've just eaten"?
questions.explanation: The passé récent is venir in the present + de + infinitive: "Je viens de manger." "Je suis venu de manger" puts venir in the passé composé; "je viens manger" means "I'm coming to eat"; "je vais manger" is "I'm going to eat".

questions.topic: Venir de and être en train de
questions.stem: How do you say "She's cooking right now (she's in the middle of it)"?
choices: Elle est en train de cuisiner.
questions.explanation: Être en train de + infinitive: "Elle est en train de cuisiner." Don't forget de; French has no "is cooking" form with -ant; "elle vient de cuisiner" means she has just cooked.

questions.topic: Venir de and être en train de
questions.stem: Complete: "Le film est sur le point ___ commencer."
questions.explanation: "Être sur le point de" + infinitive = to be about to: "Le film est sur le point de commencer."

questions.topic: Venir de and être en train de
questions.stem: Complete: "Je viens ___ lever." (I've just got up.)
questions.explanation: The reflexive pronoun stays with the infinitive and matches the subject: je → me. "Je viens de me lever." "Se" is the infinitive's dictionary form, not the right person; "de" can't be left out.

questions.topic: Venir de and être en train de
questions.stem: Which sentence is wrong?
choices: Je suis en train de faire la vaisselle.
Il est en train de dormir.
Je suis en train d'avoir une voiture.
Nous sommes en train de manger.
questions.explanation: "Être en train de" is for an action in progress, not a state like having something: say "J'ai une voiture." The other three are actions happening right now.

questions.topic: Venir de and être en train de
questions.stem: "Le train vient de partir." means…
choices: The train is coming from Paris.
The train is about to leave.
The train is going to leave.
questions.explanation: Venir de + infinitive = to have just done: the train has just left. "About to leave" is "est sur le point de partir" and "going to leave" is "va partir".

questions.topic: Venir de and être en train de
questions.stem: "J'étais en train de passer l'aspirateur quand on a sonné." What happened?
choices: I vacuumed after the doorbell rang.
I was about to start vacuuming.
Someone rang the doorbell while I was vacuuming.
questions.explanation: "J'étais en train de" (imparfait) = I was in the middle of. The doorbell (passé composé, "on a sonné") interrupted the vacuuming, like the interrupted action of lesson 02.

questions.stem: Which chore uses the verb "passer"?
questions.explanation: "Passer l'aspirateur" = to vacuum. The others use faire: faire la vaisselle, faire les courses, faire le ménage.

questions.stem: "Faire la lessive" means…
questions.explanation: La lessive is the laundry (and the washing powder). The dishes are la vaisselle, the shopping les courses, and ironing is repasser.

questions.stem: Complete with "ranger" in the present: "Nous ___ notre chambre tous les samedis."
questions.explanation: Like manger, ranger keeps the e before o so the g stays soft: "nous rangeons". "Rangons" would be read with a hard g; "rangeions" mixes in the imparfait; "rangez" is the vous form.

questions.stem: Complete with "nettoyer" in the present: "Il ___ la salle de bains."
questions.explanation: -yer verbs change y to i before a silent e: "il nettoie" (but "nous nettoyons"). "Nettoye" keeps the y before the silent e; "nettoit" uses a wrong ending; "nettoyes" is a wrong tu form.

questions.topic: Venir de and être en train de
questions.stem: Read: "— Tu peux m'aider ? — Pas maintenant, je suis en train de repasser. — Et après ? — Après, je vais faire les courses." What is the second person doing right now?
questions.explanation: "Je suis en train de repasser" = I'm ironing right now. The shopping is for later: "je vais faire les courses" (futur proche).

questions.topic: Venir de and être en train de
questions.stem: Complete with the passé récent: "Les enfants ___ ___ ranger leur chambre." (The children have just tidied their room.)
questions.explanation: Venir in the present (ils viennent) + de + infinitive: "Les enfants viennent de ranger leur chambre."

questions.topic: Venir de and être en train de
questions.stem: Put the words in order: "I'm about to go out."
questions.explanation: "Je suis sur le point de sortir." Être (conjugated) + sur le point de + infinitive.

questions.stem: Match each chore to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Vaisselle = dishes, lessive = laundry, courses = shopping, aspirateur = vacuum cleaner, repasser = to iron. "To water" is arroser and "to do DIY" is bricoler.

questions.topic: Venir de and être en train de
questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Je viens de finir mes devoirs.
Elle est en train de se préparer.
questions.explanation: The first three use the present of venir or être, de, and the reflexive pronoun that matches the subject (se for elle, nous for nous). "Je suis venu de manger" puts venir in the passé composé: the passé récent is "je viens de manger".

questions.stem: Name the numbered things and chores in this house.

image.alt: A cut-away house with numbered markers on a fridge, an oven, a washing machine, a person vacuuming upstairs, a person washing dishes at the sink, and a person in the garden with a watering can.

questions.explanation: 1 le frigo, 2 le four, 3 la machine à laver (round door), 4 passer l'aspirateur, 5 faire la vaisselle at the sink, 6 arroser (water) the garden. Nobody is ironing (repasser) or doing DIY (bricoler).

questions.stem: In the memoir, why does Thomas write "Le soir, Mamie allumait un feu" but "Mamie a allumé des bougies"?
choices: The fire was every evening; the candles were one night, during the storm.
The first sentence is more polite.
The fire is in the present and the candles in the past.
There is no difference in meaning.
questions.explanation: Same verb, different job: the imparfait "allumait" with "le soir" is a habit; the passé composé "a allumé" is one action on the night of the storm.

questions.stem: Which phrase from the text starts a single event?
choices: Le soir, quand il faisait frais
Un été, l'été de mes dix ans
questions.explanation: "Un été" (one summer) breaks the routine and introduces one story told in the passé composé. "Le soir", "de temps en temps" and "le jeudi" all mark habits.

questions.stem: "Je m'endormais souvent avant la fin de l'histoire." means…
choices: I fell asleep once before the end of the story.
I'm falling asleep before the end of the story.
I often fell asleep before the end of the story.
I had fallen asleep before the end of the story.
questions.explanation: Imparfait + souvent = a habit: I often used to fall asleep. One time would be "je me suis endormi"; "had fallen asleep" would be the plus-que-parfait "je m'étais endormi".

questions.stem: Which tense is "elle avait perdu une partie de sa mémoire"?
questions.explanation: Avoir in the imparfait (avait) + a past participle (perdu) = plus-que-parfait: "she had lost". The imparfait alone would be "elle perdait".

questions.stem: "Quand je suis arrivé à la gare, le train était déjà parti." What happened first?
choices: Both happened at the same moment.
questions.explanation: "Était parti" is the plus-que-parfait: the train had left before I arrived. So the train left first.

questions.stem: "Peu à peu" means…
questions.explanation: "Peu à peu" = little by little, gradually. "From time to time" is de temps en temps; "a few years later" is quelques années après.

questions.stem: In careful French, complete: "Je me rappelle ___ odeur de la maison."
questions.explanation: Se rappeler takes a direct object, with no de: "Je me rappelle l'odeur." (With se souvenir you need de: "Je me souviens de l'odeur.") You will hear "se rappeler de" in speech, but it's considered careless.

questions.stem: What is the imparfait of "rire" with "nous"?
questions.explanation: Stem ri- (from "nous rions") + -ions = "nous riions", with two i's like "nous étudiions". "Nous rions" is the present and "nous rirons" the future.

questions.stem: In the text, why didn't Thomas like going down to the cellar?
choices: He was afraid of the dark.
questions.explanation: "Je n'aimais pas descendre à la cave : j'avais peur du noir." The cellar was cold and damp, not hot.

questions.stem: During the storm, what did Mamie bring back from the attic?
questions.explanation: "Elle est montée au grenier et elle est revenue avec un vieux jeu de cartes." She had already lit the candles; the blankets were in the children's den.

questions.stem: Write "se cacher" in the imparfait: "L'après-midi, nous nous ___ dans la cabane."
questions.explanation: A habit, so imparfait: nous cachons → cach- + -ions = "nous nous cachions".

questions.stem: Put the parts of this short memory in a logical order.
choices: Quand j'étais petit, je passais mes étés à la mer.
Le matin, nous allions toujours à la plage.
Un jour, mon frère s'est perdu sur la plage.
Aujourd'hui, on rit quand on raconte cette histoire.
questions.explanation: A memoir opens with time and place (quand j'étais petit), describes the habits (le matin, toujours), breaks the routine with one event (un jour + passé composé) and closes in the present (aujourd'hui).

questions.stem: Match each time link to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Peu à peu = gradually; de temps en temps = now and then; quelques années après = a few years later; ce soir-là = that evening (one evening). "Every evening" is le soir or tous les soirs; "before" is avant.

questions.stem: Which verbs are in the plus-que-parfait? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Avoir in the imparfait + a participle: "avions construit", "avait perdu". "Riait" is the imparfait alone and "ai compris" is the passé composé.

questions.stem: How do you read "le XIXe siècle"?
questions.explanation: XIX = 19, read as an ordinal: dix-neuvième (neuf → neuvième, with v). "Le dix-neuf siècle" uses a plain number.

questions.stem: In which century is the year 1789?
questions.explanation: First two digits + 1: 17 + 1 = 18, so le XVIIIe (dix-huitième) siècle. The 1700s are the 18th century.

questions.stem: How do you say "Louis XIV"?
questions.explanation: Kings use plain numbers, except "Premier" for the first: Louis Quatorze, but François Premier.

questions.stem: How do you say "in the sixties"?
questions.explanation: Decades: dans les années + number, with no s or apostrophe after the number: "dans les années 60" (soixante).

questions.stem: When did women in France vote for the first time?
choices: in the municipal elections of 29 April 1945
questions.explanation: The ordinance of 21 April 1944 gave women the right to vote and stand for election; they first used it in the municipal elections of 29 April 1945.

questions.stem: What did the law of 20 June 1936 give employees?
choices: two weeks of paid holiday a year
five weeks of paid holiday a year
questions.explanation: The 1936 law gave employees at least two weeks (15 days) of paid holiday, les congés payés, after a year in the same workplace. Today it is five weeks.

questions.stem: "En 1914, la France était un pays de paysans." Why "était" and not "a été"?
choices: It's a habit of one person.
It describes the situation at the time (background).
questions.explanation: What France was like in 1914 is a description, so imparfait. The dated event that follows is in the passé composé: "En août 1914, la guerre a commencé."

questions.stem: At the changeover, 1 € = 6,55957 F. About how much were 100 francs in euros?
questions.explanation: Francs to euros: divide. 100 ÷ 6,55957 = 15,2449…, so 15,24 €. "655,96" multiplies instead of dividing.

questions.stem: Which date is a public holiday in France for the end of the Second World War in Europe?
questions.explanation: The war in Europe ended on 8 May 1945. 11 November marks the 1918 armistice; 14 July is the national holiday; 25 August 1944 is the liberation of Paris (not a national holiday).

questions.stem: When did euro coins and notes arrive in France?
questions.explanation: The euro became the currency for banks and prices on 1 January 1999; coins and notes followed on 1 January 2002. Francs were accepted until 17 February 2002.

questions.stem: Write the ordinal: "le XXe siècle" is read "le ___ siècle".
questions.explanation: Vingt + -ième = vingtième: le vingtième siècle, the 20th century.

questions.stem: Put these events in time order, earliest first.
questions.explanation: 1914–1918, then 1936, then 1945 (first vote), 1958 (Fifth Republic) and 1999–2002 (the euro).

questions.stem: Match each year to its event.
questions.explanation: 1918: armistice; 1936: les congés payés; 1958: la Ve République; 2002: euro coins and notes. The Revolution began in 1789 and women first voted in 1945.

questions.stem: Name the event at each numbered point on the timeline.

image.alt: A timeline from 1910 to 2010 with unlabelled bars and dots; numbered markers at 1914–1918, 1936, 1958, 1968 and 1999–2002.

questions.explanation: 1914–1918: la Première Guerre mondiale; 1936: les congés payés; 1958: la Ve République; 1968: Mai 68; 1999–2002: l'euro. The French Revolution (1789) is not on this timeline.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Au XXe siècle, la vie a beaucoup changé.
Dans les années 80, ma mère habitait à Paris.
Dans le XXe siècle, il y a eu deux guerres mondiales.
En les années 60, mon père était étudiant.
questions.explanation: Centuries take au (au XXe siècle); decades take dans les (dans les années 80). "Dans le XXe siècle" and "en les années 60" are wrong.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu connais Marc ? — Oui, je ___ connais."
questions.explanation: "Marc" is one man and the direct object of "connaître", so "le": "Je le connais." "La" is feminine, "les" plural, and "lui" is for verbs with à (lesson 6).

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu regardes la télé ? — Non, je ne ___ regarde pas."
questions.explanation: "La télé" is feminine, so "la": "Je ne la regarde pas." "L'" is only used before a vowel or mute h, and "regarde" starts with r. "Le" is masculine; "lui" is an indirect pronoun.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'm going to invite them"?
questions.explanation: With aller + infinitive, the pronoun goes before the infinitive, because it is the object of "inviter": "Je vais les inviter." Not before "vais", and never after the verb. "Leur" is wrong because "inviter quelqu'un" takes a direct object.

questions.stem: How do you say "Help me!" to a friend?
questions.explanation: In an affirmative command the pronoun goes after the verb with a hyphen, and "me" becomes "moi": "Aide-moi !"

questions.stem: How do you say "Don't look at him!" to a friend?
questions.explanation: In a negative command the pronoun goes back before the verb, with no hyphen, and "ne … pas" goes around both: "Ne le regarde pas !" The hyphen form "Regarde-le !" is only for the affirmative.

questions.stem: Replace "le bus" with a pronoun: "J'attends le bus."
questions.explanation: "Attendre" takes a direct object in French (no "for"), so the pronoun is "le", elided to "l'" before the vowel: "Je l'attends." "Lui" is for verbs with à, and the pronoun never goes after the verb in a statement.

questions.stem: What does "On se voit demain ?" mean?
choices: Did we see each other yesterday?
questions.explanation: "Se voir" is reciprocal: "to see each other". "On se voit demain ?" (literally "Do we see each other tomorrow?") is the everyday way to suggest meeting. The verb is in the present, so it isn't about yesterday.

questions.stem: You want to tell a good friend "I like you" (as a friend). What do you say?
questions.explanation: With a person, "aimer" means to love; "aimer bien" softens it to "to like": "Je t'aime bien." "Je t'aime" is "I love you". "Je te plais" means "you like me" (lesson 6), and "Je l'aime bien" is about someone else.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu aimes ton nouveau quartier ? — Oui, je ___ beaucoup."
questions.explanation: "Le quartier" is masculine, so the pronoun is "le", and it elides before the vowel of "aime": "Je l'aime beaucoup." "Le aime" and "la aime" forget the elision (and "la" is the wrong gender); "lui" is indirect.

questions.stem: Complete with the present of "croire": "Mes parents ne me ___ pas."
questions.explanation: The present of "croire" is crois, crois, croit, croyons, croyez, croient. The y appears only in "nous croyons, vous croyez". "Croyent" and "croivent" are common mistakes; "croyons" is the "nous" form.

questions.stem: Léa writes to Sarah: "Hugo est un peu jaloux. Quand je vois mes amis, il m'appelle toutes les heures. Mais je l'aime, et on se réconcilie toujours après nos disputes." What does Léa say about Hugo?
choices: He calls her very often when she is with her friends.
She doesn't love him any more.
questions.explanation: "Il m'appelle toutes les heures" = he calls me every hour, when she sees her friends. She says "je l'aime" (I love him) and that they always make up after their arguments, so they do argue.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake?
questions.explanation: "Chercher" means "to look for": no preposition in French. Say "Je cherche mes lunettes" (and "Je les cherche"). The other three are correct: attendre, écouter and aider take a direct object.

questions.stem: Which verbs take a direct object in French, with no preposition before the person or thing? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Attendre, chercher and écouter take a direct object even though English uses "for" or "to": "J'attends Paul, je cherche mes clés, j'écoute la radio" (so le, la, les). "Téléphoner" takes à + person: "Je téléphone à Paul" (lui, lesson 6).

questions.stem: Type the missing pronoun: "Tu connais mes parents ? — Oui, je ___ connais bien."
questions.explanation: "Mes parents" is plural, so "les": "Je les connais bien." — Yes, I know them well.

questions.stem: Turn this command into one with a pronoun for "la photo": "Regarde la photo !" → "___ !"
questions.explanation: In an affirmative command the pronoun goes after the verb with a hyphen: "Regarde-la !" ("La photo" is feminine.)

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "We're going to invite them on Saturday."
questions.explanation: "Nous allons les inviter samedi." The pronoun "les" belongs to "inviter", so it goes just before the infinitive, not before "allons".

questions.stem: Match each sentence to its meaning.
questions.explanation: "La" is her, "le" him, "les" them. "Se" with a plural subject is reciprocal: "Ils se connaissent" = they know each other. "They know me" would be "Ils me connaissent".

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu téléphones à ta mère ? — Oui, je ___ téléphone ce soir."
questions.explanation: "Téléphoner" takes à + person, so the pronoun is indirect: "lui", for a man or a woman. "La" would be a direct object; "leur" is plural.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu écris à tes grands-parents ? — Oui, je ___ écris souvent."
questions.explanation: "Écrire à" + several people → "leur": "Je leur écris souvent." The pronoun "leur" never takes -s ("leurs" is the possessive "their"). "Les" is direct; "lui" is singular.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu appelles Paul ce soir ? — Oui, je ___ appelle."
questions.explanation: "Appeler quelqu'un" takes a direct object (no à), so the pronoun is "le", elided before the vowel: "Je l'appelle." "Lui" is the classic mistake, because "téléphoner à" takes "lui".

questions.stem: Complete: "Marie m'aide beaucoup. Je ___ remercie."
questions.explanation: "Remercier quelqu'un" takes a direct object, with no à: "Je la remercie." "Lui" is the trap: you only use it with "dire merci à": "Je lui dis merci."

questions.stem: How do you say "I like this song" with "plaire"?
questions.explanation: With "plaire", the thing you like is the subject and you are the indirect object: "Cette chanson me plaît" (literally, this song pleases me). "Je plais" means "I am liked / I please".

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu penses à ta sœur ? — Oui, ___"
questions.explanation: "Penser à" + a person keeps à and takes a stressed pronoun: "Je pense à elle" (ta sœur is a woman). "Je lui pense" is wrong: penser à doesn't take lui or leur. "À lui" would be about a man.

questions.stem: How do you say "Write to me!" to a friend?
questions.explanation: Affirmative command: the pronoun goes after the verb with a hyphen, and "me" becomes "moi": "Écris-moi !"

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'm not going to answer them"?
choices: Je ne leur vais pas répondre.
Je ne vais pas leur répondre.
Je ne vais pas les répondre.
Je ne vais leur pas répondre.
questions.explanation: "Répondre à" takes an indirect pronoun ("leur"), and with aller + infinitive the pronoun goes before the infinitive. "Ne … pas" goes around "vais": "Je ne vais pas leur répondre."

questions.stem: What does "Il ne décroche pas" mean?
questions.explanation: "Décrocher" is to pick up the phone, so "Il ne décroche pas" = he isn't answering. To hang up is "raccrocher", to call back "rappeler", and a busy line is "C'est occupé".

questions.stem: Your friend says: "Allô ? Je ne t'entends pas bien, je suis dans le métro !" What is the best reply?
choices: D'accord, je lui rappelle plus tard.
D'accord, je te rappelle plus tard.
questions.explanation: "Je te rappelle plus tard" = I'll call you back later. "Rappeler quelqu'un" takes a direct object, and here the person is "you" (te). "Je lui rappelle" is wrong (direct verb, and it isn't "you"); "ça me plaît" and "je te décroche" make no sense here.

questions.stem: Complete: "Les enfants ? Je ___ donne ___ cadeaux ce soir."
questions.explanation: The first word is the pronoun "to them": always "leur", never with -s. The second is the possessive "their" before a plural noun: "leurs cadeaux". So "Je leur donne leurs cadeaux."

questions.stem: Lucas texts his sister: "Coucou Chloé ! Papa ne m'a pas rappelé. Je lui ai laissé un message sur son répondeur ce matin. Tu peux lui téléphoner ce soir ? Et ne dis rien à maman !" What does Lucas ask Chloé to do?
choices: Leave a message on Lucas's voicemail.
Tell their mother about the call.
questions.explanation: "Tu peux lui téléphoner ce soir ?" — "lui" is Papa, the person in the sentences before. "Ne dis rien à maman" means "don't tell Mum anything".

questions.stem: In which sentences is "lui" correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Je lui attends devant le cinéma.
Je lui remercie pour le cadeau.
questions.explanation: Téléphoner, montrer and sourire take à + person, so "lui" is right. "Attendre" and "remercier" take a direct object: "Je l'attends", "Je le / la remercie".

questions.stem: Replace "à mes parents" with a pronoun: "Je parle à mes parents." → "Je ___ parle."
questions.explanation: "Parler à" + several people → "leur", with no -s: "Je leur parle."

questions.stem: Turn the command into one with a pronoun for "à Julie": "Téléphone à Julie !" → "___ !"
questions.explanation: "Téléphoner à" takes the indirect pronoun "lui" (for a woman too), placed after the verb with a hyphen in an affirmative command: "Téléphone-lui !"

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "Can you show me your photos?"
questions.explanation: "Tu peux me montrer tes photos ?" The pronoun "me" belongs to "montrer" (montrer quelque chose à quelqu'un), so it goes before the infinitive.

questions.stem: Does the verb take a direct object (le, la, les) or an indirect one (lui, leur) for a person? Match each verb.
questions.explanation: Appeler, remercier and aider take the person directly (je l'appelle, je la remercie, je l'aide). Téléphoner and répondre take à + person (je lui téléphone, je leur réponds). "Y" is for à + a thing or place, not a person.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things on the phone screens.

image.alt: Two phone screens. Left: an incoming call from Maman with a red button and a green button. Right: a list of missed calls from Maman, a green call-back button and a voicemail notice with one new message. Numbers mark the green button, the red button, the call-back button, the voicemail symbol and the phone's frame.

questions.explanation: The green button is for picking up (décrocher), the red one for hanging up (raccrocher). After a missed call you can call back (rappeler) or listen to your voicemail (le répondeur). The whole device is le portable. "Occupé" (engaged) and "laisser" (to leave) are not on the screens.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu vas à la piscine ? — Oui, j'___ vais."
questions.explanation: "À la piscine" is à + a place, so "y": "J'y vais." With "aller" French needs the "y"; "Oui, je vais" alone sounds unfinished.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu veux du fromage ? — Oui, j'___ veux bien."
questions.explanation: "Du fromage" is a partitive (some cheese), so "en": "J'en veux bien." "Le" would mean "the cheese" (le fromage), and "y" replaces à + a thing or a place.

questions.stem: How do you answer "Tu as combien de frères ?" if you have two brothers?
questions.explanation: With a number, "en" replaces the noun and the number stays at the end: "J'en ai deux." French needs both: "J'ai deux" has no pronoun, and "J'en ai" loses the number.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il y a des œufs dans le frigo ? — Non, ___"
questions.explanation: "Il y a" + "en" is always "il y en a", and the negative wraps "ne … pas" around "y en a": "Il n'y en a pas." Y comes before en.

questions.stem: You say "Go ahead!" to a friend you call "tu". What do you say?
questions.explanation: The command of "aller" for tu is "va", but it gets an s back before "y" so the two vowels link with a z sound: "Vas-y !" (said "va-zi"). With vous it is "Allez-y !"

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu penses à ton grand-père ? — Oui, ___"
questions.explanation: After "penser à", a person takes à + a stressed pronoun: "Je pense souvent à lui." "Y" is for things and places ("Tu penses à ton examen ? J'y pense"), and "penser à" never takes "lui". (You may hear "j'y pense" about a person in casual speech, but careful French avoids it.)

questions.stem: Complete: "Il faut combien de farine ? — Il ___ faut trois cents grammes."
questions.explanation: The noun follows a quantity ("trois cents grammes de farine"), so "en" replaces "de farine" and the quantity stays: "Il en faut trois cents grammes."

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'm going to buy some"?
questions.explanation: "En" goes before the infinitive it belongs to: "Je vais en acheter." It never goes before "vais", and it only follows the verb in an affirmative command ("Achètes-en !").

questions.stem: What does "Coupez les carottes en tranches" mean?
questions.explanation: "Couper" is to cut, and "une tranche" is a slice, so "couper en tranches" is to slice. To cook is "faire cuire", to mix "mélanger".

questions.stem: Which sentence means "My father cooks (makes the meals) every Sunday"?
choices: Mon père cuit tous les dimanches.
Mon père se cuit tous les dimanches.
Mon père cuisine tous les dimanches.
Mon père fait cuit tous les dimanches.
questions.explanation: "Cuisiner" is to cook in the sense of making meals. "Cuire" is what the food does ("le riz cuit"), or "faire cuire" + the food ("il fait cuire le riz"), so "Mon père cuit" would mean the father is cooking in the oven!

questions.stem: Look at the recipe card. After you add the carrots and the water, how long do they cook?

image.alt: A recipe card for carrot and lemon soup for four people, 35 minutes, with a list of ingredients and five steps.
image.caption: Soupe de carottes au citron

questions.explanation: Step 3 says "Ajoutez les carottes et l'eau. Faites cuire 25 minutes." The 5 minutes in step 2 are for the onion and garlic, and 35 minutes is the time for the whole recipe.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I ate half of the cake"?
choices: J'ai mangé la moitié du gâteau.
J'ai mangé la moitié le gâteau.
questions.explanation: "La moitié" is a noun, so it takes "de": "la moitié du gâteau" (de + le = du). "Demi" is used before a noun with a hyphen and an article ("un demi-citron"), not like this.

questions.stem: In which answers is "en" used correctly? Select all that apply.
choices: Tu as une voiture ? — Oui, j'en ai une.
Tu vas à Paris ? — Oui, j'en vais.
Tu bois du café ? — Non, je n'en bois pas.
Tu viens de la gare ? — Oui, j'en viens.
questions.explanation: "En" replaces a noun after a number (une voiture → j'en ai une), a partitive (du café → je n'en bois pas) and de + a place (de la gare → j'en viens). "À Paris" is à + a place, so it takes "y": "J'y vais."

questions.stem: Type the missing pronoun: "Tu vas souvent au marché ? — Oui, j'___ vais le samedi."
questions.explanation: "Au marché" is à + a place, so "y": "J'y vais le samedi."

questions.stem: Type the missing pronoun: "Tu as des enfants ? — Oui, j'___ ai trois."
questions.explanation: "Des enfants" after a number becomes "en", and the number stays: "J'en ai trois."

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "There are twelve of them."
questions.explanation: "Il y en a douze." "Il y a" becomes "il y en a" ("y" before "en"), and the number goes at the end.

questions.stem: Which pronoun would replace the words after the verb? Match each sentence to its pronoun.
questions.explanation: À + a place or a thing → y (j'y vais, j'y pense). A partitive or a noun after a number → en (j'en mange, j'en achète trois). À + a person → lui (je lui parle). "Le" would replace a definite direct object ("le pain").

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in the kitchen.

image.alt: A kitchen counter with a saucepan on the hob, a frying pan, a paper bag, a bottle of yellow oil, a salt cellar, a lemon, an onion and a head of garlic. Numbers mark the saucepan, the frying pan, the bag, the bottle, the lemon and the onion.

questions.explanation: The deep pan with a lid on the hob is la casserole; the flat one with a long handle is la poêle (said "pwal"). The bag holds la farine, the bottle l'huile. The yellow fruit is le citron and the brown bulb l'oignon. The garlic (l'ail) is in the picture but has no number.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu as vu le film ? — Oui, je ___"
questions.explanation: In the passé composé the pronoun goes before the auxiliary, and "le" elides before "ai": "Je l'ai vu."

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu as parlé à Julie ? — Non, ___"
choices: je ne lui ai pas parlée.
je ne lui ai pas parlé.
questions.explanation: "Parler à" takes "lui". "Ne" goes before the pronoun and "pas" after the auxiliary: "Je ne lui ai pas parlé." There is no agreement with "lui", because it is an indirect object.

questions.stem: Complete with "écrire": "La lettre ? Je l'ai ___ hier."
questions.explanation: "L'" stands for "la lettre", a feminine direct object placed before the verb, so the participle agrees: "Je l'ai écrite." You can hear it: the t is pronounced.

questions.stem: Complete with "envoyer": "Ma sœur ? Je lui ai ___ un message."
questions.explanation: "Lui" is an indirect object, and the direct object ("un message") comes after the verb, so there is no agreement: "Je lui ai envoyé un message."

questions.stem: Complete with "mettre": "Les photos ? Je les ai ___ sur le site."
questions.explanation: "Les" stands for "les photos", feminine plural, placed before the verb, so the participle of "mettre" (mis) takes -es: "Je les ai mises sur le site."

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I couldn't repair it"?
choices: Je n'ai pas pu réparer le.
Je n'ai le pas pu réparer.
Je n'ai pas pu lui réparer.
Je n'ai pas pu le réparer.
questions.explanation: The pronoun belongs to "réparer", so it goes before the infinitive, even when "pouvoir" is in the passé composé: "Je n'ai pas pu le réparer." "Réparer" takes a direct object, so not "lui".

questions.stem: Complete with "acheter": "Des pommes ? J'en ai ___ deux kilos."
questions.explanation: "En" is not a direct object pronoun like "les", so the participle doesn't agree (that is the usual rule): "J'en ai acheté deux kilos."

questions.stem: Complete: "Ton sac ? Tu ___ trouvé ?"
questions.explanation: The pronoun goes before the auxiliary and elides before "as": "Tu l'as trouvé ?" (Did you find it?)

questions.stem: What does "Quelqu'un a rapporté votre portefeuille" mean?
questions.explanation: "Rapporter" is to bring back or return an item, so someone handed the wallet in. "To steal" is "voler", "to repair" "réparer", "to report" (to the police) "déclarer".

questions.stem: At the repair shop: "Vous avez la facture ?" Which answer is correct?
questions.explanation: "L'" = "la facture" (feminine), a direct object before the verb, so the participle agrees: "je l'ai apportée". "Lui" is indirect, and "les" is plural.

questions.stem: Read the message: "Bonjour, votre montre est réparée. Elle est encore sous garantie, donc la réparation est gratuite. Vous pouvez la récupérer à partir de jeudi. N'oubliez pas votre reçu." (gratuite = free) What must the customer bring?
questions.explanation: "N'oubliez pas votre reçu" = don't forget your receipt. The repair is free (still under guarantee), and "la récupérer" means collecting the watch, so the customer doesn't bring it.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: With avoir the participle never agrees with the subject, and "ses clés" comes after the verb, so: "Marie a perdu ses clés." With the pronoun it would be "Marie les a perdues" (agreement with les). "Leur" is indirect.

questions.stem: Which sentences are written correctly? Select all that apply.
choices: Ma mère ? Je lui ai téléphonée.
Les clés ? Je les ai retrouvées.
questions.explanation: The participle agrees with a direct object that comes before it: "je l'ai prise" (la valise), "je les ai retrouvées" (les clés). There is no agreement with "lui" (je lui ai téléphoné), with "en" (j'en ai mangé), or when the object comes after the verb (j'ai ouvert la porte).

questions.stem: Type the missing words (pronoun, auxiliary and participle): "Tu as vu Léa ? — Oui, je ___ hier."
questions.explanation: "Léa" is a woman and the direct object; the pronoun "la" elides to "l'" before "ai", and the participle agrees with it: "Je l'ai vue hier."

questions.stem: Rewrite with a pronoun for "à mes parents": "J'ai téléphoné à mes parents." → "Je ___ ___ téléphoné."
questions.explanation: "Téléphoner à" + several people → "leur", placed before the auxiliary: "Je leur ai téléphoné." No agreement: "leur" is indirect.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "I didn't buy any."
questions.explanation: "Je n'en ai pas acheté." "Ne" and the pronoun "en" stay together before the auxiliary, "pas" follows the auxiliary, and the participle comes last.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to the right form of the participle.
questions.explanation: "La porte" (feminine) → ouverte; "le livre" (masculine) → lu; "mes amies" (feminine plural) → invitées. With "lui" there is no agreement → écrit.

questions.stem: Name the numbered objects at the lost-property office.

image.alt: A lost-property office under the sign Objets trouvés. On the shelf: a red booklet, a bunch of keys and a case with two earbuds. On the counter: a brown wallet, a small pink coin purse with a clasp, and a watch. Each object has a number.

questions.explanation: The red booklet is le passeport, the bunch of keys les clés, the case with two earbuds les écouteurs. On the counter: the wallet for notes and cards is le portefeuille, the little purse for coins le porte-monnaie, and la montre.

questions.stem: Name each part of the sentence "Je ne l'ai pas vu."

image.alt: The sentence Je ne l'ai pas vu split into six boxes, Je, ne, l', ai, pas and vu, with a bracket over ne … pas and a dashed frame around l' and ai. A number is under each box.

questions.explanation: "Je" is the subject, "l'" the object pronoun, "ai" the auxiliary avoir, "vu" the past participle, and "ne … pas" wraps the pronoun and the auxiliary together. There is no infinitive or article in this sentence ("l'" here is a pronoun, not the article).

questions.stem: Replace both objects: "Je donne les clés à Inès." → "Je ___ donne."
questions.explanation: "Les clés" = les (column 2) and "à Inès" = lui (column 3). Le, la, les come before lui, leur: "Je les lui donne."

questions.stem: Replace "son vélo": "Paul me prête son vélo." → "Il ___ prête."
questions.explanation: "Me" is in column 1 and comes before "le" (column 2): "Il me le prête." — He lends it to me.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il y a du café ? — Oui, ___"
questions.explanation: "Y" (column 4) always comes before "en" (column 5): "Il y en a."

questions.stem: Which is the standard way to say "Give it to me!" to a friend?
questions.explanation: In an affirmative command the direct object comes first, then the person: "Donne-le-moi !" "Donne-moi-le" is heard in casual speech but counted as a mistake, and the statement order "me le" belongs before the verb, not in a command.

questions.stem: Which is the standard way to say "Give me some!" (vous)?
questions.explanation: "En" always comes last, and "moi" becomes "m'" before "en": "Donnez-m'en !"

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I didn't tell him (it)"?
choices: Je ne lui l'ai pas dit.
Je ne l'ai pas lui dit.
Je n'ai pas le lui dit.
Je ne le lui ai pas dit.
questions.explanation: The pair "le lui" (column 2 then 3) stays together before the auxiliary, and "ne … pas" goes around the pair and the auxiliary: "Je ne le lui ai pas dit."

questions.stem: Complete with "donner": "Les clés ? Je te les ai ___."
questions.explanation: "Les" = "les clés", a feminine plural direct object before the verb, so the participle agrees: "données". "Te" (to you) is indirect here and doesn't affect the agreement.

questions.stem: A friend asks "Tu as dit le secret à Paul ?" In casual speech the answer is "Oui, je lui ai dit." What does it mean?
questions.explanation: In relaxed speech "le" is often dropped before "lui": "je lui ai dit" stands for "je le lui ai dit" (I told it to him). The full form is the one to write.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Don't give it to them!"?
questions.explanation: A negative command uses the statement order, before the verb and without hyphens: "le" (column 2) then "leur" (column 3), inside "ne … pas": "Ne le leur donne pas !"

questions.stem: Read: "Julie : Ma perceuse ? Tu la lui as prêtée ? — Karim : Non, je l'ai rangée dans le placard." What did Karim do with the drill?
choices: He put it away in the cupboard.
He gave it back to Julie.
questions.explanation: "Je l'ai rangée dans le placard" = I put it away in the cupboard ("ranger" = to put away). "Non" answers the question "Did you lend it to him?"

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Te le", "me les" and "y en" follow the order me/te → le/la/les → lui/leur → y → en. "Lui le" should be "le lui" (Je le lui prête), and "en lui" should be "lui en" (Elle lui en parle).

questions.stem: Replace both objects with pronouns: "Je montre la photo à mes parents." → "Je ___ ___ montre."
questions.explanation: "La photo" = la (column 2), "à mes parents" = leur (column 3): "Je la leur montre."

questions.stem: Replace "le livre" with a pronoun: "Rends-moi le livre !" → "___ !"
questions.explanation: In an affirmative command the direct object comes first: "Rends-le-moi !"

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "I'm going to show it to you."
questions.explanation: "Je vais te le montrer." The pair "te le" (column 1 then 2) goes before the infinitive it belongs to.

questions.stem: Match the flatshare objects to their English names.
questions.explanation: La perceuse = drill, l'échelle = ladder, le tire-bouchon = corkscrew, la rallonge = extension lead. A hair dryer is le sèche-cheveux.

questions.stem: Inès says: "Ma mère vit avec Marc depuis trois ans. Mon beau-père est très sympa." Who is "mon beau-père" here?
questions.explanation: "Beau-père" means stepfather or father-in-law. Here Inès is talking about her mother's partner, Marc, so he is her stepfather.

questions.stem: Léo has the same mother as Inès but a different father. For Inès, Léo is…
questions.explanation: A brother who shares one parent with you is "un demi-frère" (half-brother). "Le beau-frère" is a brother-in-law.

questions.stem: When was the PACS (pacte civil de solidarité) created?
questions.explanation: The PACS was created by the law of 15 November 1999. 2013 is the year marriage opened to couples of the same sex, and since 2017 the PACS has been registered at the town hall or with a notary.

questions.stem: According to INSEE, about what share of families with children under 18 were single-parent families in France in 2020?
questions.explanation: INSEE gives 24.7 % in 2020, about a quarter, up from 12 % in 1990. About 9 % were blended families and about 66 % "traditional" families.

questions.stem: Complete with "se parler": "Ils se sont ___ hier soir."
questions.explanation: "Parler à quelqu'un" takes an indirect object, so "se" is indirect here and the participle doesn't agree: "Ils se sont parlé."

questions.stem: Complete with "se rencontrer": "Elles se sont ___ en 2015."
questions.explanation: "Rencontrer quelqu'un" takes a direct object, so "se" is direct and the participle agrees with it: feminine plural, "rencontrées".

questions.stem: What is the plural of "la demi-sœur"?
questions.explanation: "Demi" before a hyphen never changes; only the noun takes -s: "les demi-sœurs".

questions.stem: A teenager says: "Je suis en garde alternée." What does it mean?
choices: I live with each parent in turn.
I look after my little brother.
I live alone with my mother.
questions.explanation: "La garde alternée" is shared custody: the child lives with each parent in turn, often one week each.

questions.stem: In 2024 there were 248,174 marriages and 197,176 PACS in France (INSEE). Which sentence is true?
choices: There were more PACS than marriages.
There were about twice as many marriages as PACS.
There were almost four PACS for every five marriages.
There were about as many PACS as divorces.
questions.explanation: 197,176 ÷ 248,174 ≈ 0.79, so about 4 PACS for every 5 marriages. The figures say nothing about divorces.

questions.stem: Which sentences have the correct participle? Select all that apply.
choices: Nous nous sommes mariés. (a man and a woman)
questions.explanation: "Téléphoner à" is indirect: no agreement (se sont téléphoné). "Voir quelqu'un" is direct: agreement (se sont vues). "Se marier" agrees with the subject; a man and a woman → masculine plural (mariés). "Écrire à" and "sourire à" are indirect, so "se sont écrit" and "se sont souri", with no ending.

questions.stem: Put "se marier" in the passé composé: "Léa et Sami ___ ___ ___ en 2023."
questions.explanation: Verbs with "se" take être, and "se marier" agrees with the subject. Léa and Sami are a woman and a man, so masculine plural: "Léa et Sami se sont mariés en 2023."

questions.stem: Type the missing word: shared custody is "la garde ___".
questions.explanation: "La garde alternée": the children live with each parent in turn.

questions.stem: This is Inès's family. Name the numbered people from Inès's point of view.

image.alt: A family tree. Mamie and Papi at the top, joined by a line that goes down to Claire. Middle row: Sophie and Antoine as a couple, a dashed line (separated) from Antoine to Claire, and Claire and Marc as a couple. Bottom row: Zoé below Sophie and Antoine, Inès below Antoine and Claire, and Léo below Claire and Marc. Numbers mark the line joining Mamie and Papi, Sophie, Claire, Marc, Zoé and Léo.

questions.explanation: Mamie and Papi are Inès's grandparents (les grands-parents). Claire is her mother; Marc, her mother's partner, is her stepfather (le beau-père); Sophie, her father's partner, is her stepmother (la belle-mère). Zoé shares her father and Léo shares her mother, so they are her half-sister and half-brother (la demi-sœur, le demi-frère).

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "They met at university."
questions.explanation: "Ils se sont rencontrés à la fac." The pronoun "se" comes before the auxiliary "être", and "rencontrés" agrees because "se" is the direct object (rencontrer quelqu'un).

questions.stem: Match the family words to their meanings.
questions.explanation: Monoparentale = one parent with the children; recomposée = a couple with at least one child from an earlier relationship; le conjoint = spouse, the official word on forms; les petits-enfants = grandchildren (grandparents are les grands-parents).

questions.stem: Complete: "La banlieue est ___ calme que le centre-ville." (quieter)
questions.explanation: Before an adjective, "more" is plus: plus calme que. "plus de" goes before a noun (plus de bruit), "autant" is for nouns and verbs, and "meilleur" is the comparative of bon only.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "This cake is better than the other one"?
choices: Ce gâteau est plus bon que l'autre.
Ce gâteau est meilleur que l'autre.
Ce gâteau est plus meilleur que l'autre.
Ce gâteau est meilleure que l'autre.
questions.explanation: Better = the comparative of bon (good), which is meilleur; it agrees with gâteau (masculine): meilleur. "Plus bon" doesn't exist as a comparative, "plus meilleur" says "more" twice, and "meilleure" is feminine.

questions.stem: Complete: "Elle chante ___ que moi." (She sings better than me.)
questions.explanation: How she sings is an adverb (bien), and its comparative is mieux, which never changes. "Meilleur(e)" is the comparative of the adjective bon. "Plus bien" doesn't exist.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il y a ___ bruit en ville qu'à la campagne."
questions.explanation: Before a noun, "more" is plus de, with no article: plus de bruit. "Plus" alone goes before adjectives and adverbs, and "aussi" is for adjectives and adverbs (as … as).

questions.stem: Complete: "Lyon n'a pas ___ habitants que Paris." (as many inhabitants as)
questions.explanation: With a noun, "as many / as much" is autant de, which becomes autant d' before a vowel or mute h: autant d'habitants. "Aussi" goes with adjectives and adverbs, and "autant" needs de before a noun.

questions.stem: Complete: "C'est la rue ___ animée de la ville." (the liveliest street)
questions.explanation: Animé follows the noun, so the article comes twice: la rue la plus animée. Rue is feminine, so la plus, not le plus. "Plus de" is for nouns.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "It's the biggest museum in France"?
choices: C'est le plus grand musée en France.
C'est le musée plus grand de France.
C'est le plus grand musée de France.
C'est le grand musée le plus de France.
