questions.explanation: "In" after a superlative is de: le plus grand musée de France. Grand normally goes before the noun, so one article is enough. "Le musée plus grand" lacks the second article (le musée le plus grand would be correct), and "en France" is the usual mistake.

questions.stem: Complete: "Mon frère est plus âgé que ___."
questions.explanation: After que in a comparison, French uses a stressed pronoun: plus âgé que moi, que toi, que lui. "Je" and "me" can only stand next to a verb.

questions.stem: What does "Le village est moins cher que la ville" mean?
choices: The village is cheaper than the town.
The village is more expensive than the town.
The village is as expensive as the town.
The town is cheaper than the village.
questions.explanation: Moins cher que = less expensive than, so cheaper than. "More expensive" would be plus cher, and "as expensive" aussi cher.

questions.stem: Before the noun, "propre" means "own". What does "ma propre chambre" mean?
questions.explanation: Before the noun, propre means own: ma propre chambre = my own bedroom. After the noun it means clean: une chambre propre = a clean bedroom.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ce film est ___ que l'autre. Il est vraiment nul !" (nul = rubbish)
questions.explanation: The speaker thinks the film is rubbish, so it is worse: pire (or plus mauvais). "Meilleur", "mieux" and "aussi bien" all say it is at least as good as the other one, which doesn't fit "vraiment nul".

questions.stem: Complete: "Il travaille ___ que moi." (as much as me)
questions.explanation: To compare how much people do something, put autant after the verb: il travaille autant que moi. "Aussi" goes before adjectives and adverbs, and "autant de" before a noun.

questions.stem: Read the advert: "À louer : appartement de 3 pièces dans un immeuble moderne, en banlieue. Plus grand et moins cher que les appartements du centre-ville. Quartier calme et sûr. Gare à 10 minutes." Which statement is true?
choices: The flat is cheaper than flats in the town centre.
The flat is in the town centre.
The area is lively and noisy.
The flat is smaller than flats in the centre.
questions.explanation: Moins cher que les appartements du centre-ville = cheaper than flats in the centre. It is en banlieue (in the suburbs), the area is calme et sûr (quiet and safe), and it is plus grand (bigger). (À louer = for rent.)

questions.stem: Complete with the comparative of "bon": "Ta soupe est ___ que la soupe du restaurant."
questions.explanation: Bon becomes meilleur, and it agrees with soupe (feminine): meilleure. "Plus bonne" is wrong.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "It's the most peaceful village in the region."
questions.explanation: C'est le village le plus tranquille de la région. Tranquille follows the noun, so the article comes twice (le village le plus tranquille), and "in" after a superlative is de.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct French? Select all that apply.
choices: Il y a plus de pollution qu'avant.
Ce restaurant est plus bon que l'autre.
C'est la ville la plus animée de la région.
Mon frère est plus grand que je.
questions.explanation: "Elle parle mieux que moi", "Il y a plus de pollution qu'avant" and "C'est la ville la plus animée de la région" are correct. "Plus bon" must be meilleur, and after que you need the stressed pronoun: plus grand que moi.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to the word that fills the gap.
left: Ce vin est ___ que l'autre. (good → better)
Il n'y a pas ___ de touristes ici. (as many)
Le métro est ___ rapide que le bus. (as … as)
questions.explanation: Meilleur is the comparative of the adjective bon (the wine is good); mieux the comparative of the adverb bien (you dance well). With a noun, "as many" is autant de; with an adjective, "as … as" is aussi … que. "Plus bon" doesn't exist, and pire means worse.

questions.stem: Name the numbered places in this landscape.

image.alt: A landscape with six numbered places: tall blocks of flats on the left, small houses beside them, a hill in the middle, a river at the bottom of the valley, a farm house on the right and a field of wheat in front of it.

questions.explanation: 1 is a block of flats (l'immeuble), 2 the small houses of the suburbs (la banlieue), 3 a hill (la colline), 4 the river in the valley (la rivière), 5 the farm (la ferme) and 6 the wheat field (le champ). There is no beach or lake.

questions.stem: Complete: "J'ai une amie ___ habite à Lyon."
questions.explanation: A verb (habite) follows the gap, so the antecedent une amie is the subject: qui. Que is for the object (a subject follows it), and où for a place or time.

questions.stem: Complete: "C'est le site ___ j'utilise tous les jours."
questions.explanation: A subject (j') follows the gap: le site is the object of utiliser (j'utilise ce site), so the relative is que. Qui would need a verb next.

questions.stem: Complete: "C'est la ville ___ je suis né."
questions.explanation: Je suis né dans cette ville: the town is the place where it happened, so où. You can't be born the town (que), and quand isn't a relative pronoun after a noun.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je me souviens du jour ___ je suis arrivé en France."
questions.explanation: After a time noun (le jour, l'année, le moment), French uses où for "when": le jour où je suis arrivé. "Le jour quand" is the typical English-speaker mistake.

questions.stem: Complete: "L'appli ___ il a téléchargée est gratuite."
questions.explanation: A subject (il) follows, so que, and que becomes qu' before a vowel: qu'il. "Que il" is never written. Qui would need a verb straight after it.

questions.stem: Complete: "Les photos que j'ai ___ sont très belles." (prendre)
questions.explanation: Que stands for les photos (feminine plural) and comes before the verb, so the participle of avoir agrees with it: les photos que j'ai prises. Here you can even hear the agreement: prises ends in a z sound ("preez").

questions.stem: Which is correct for "the friend who lives in Lyon"?
questions.explanation: A verb follows, so qui, and qui never elides: qui habite. A qu' before a vowel is always que, which would need a subject after it.

questions.stem: What does "Ça sert à quoi ?" mean?
questions.explanation: Servir à = to be used for. Ça sert à quoi ? = What is it for? The answer uses ça sert à + infinitive: Ça sert à charger le portable.

questions.stem: How do you say "the film I saw"?
questions.explanation: English can leave "that" out; French never leaves que out. Le film is the object of voir, so que, not qui.

questions.stem: Complete: "Pour écrire un texte sur l'ordinateur, on utilise ___."
questions.explanation: You type on the keyboard: le clavier. The charger (le chargeur) charges the battery, the printer (l'imprimante) prints, and le mot de passe is a password.

questions.stem: Complete: "C'est toi qui ___ le chargeur ?"
questions.explanation: The verb after qui agrees with the antecedent, here toi: c'est toi qui as … (as with tu as). "A" is the il/elle form.

questions.stem: What does "C'est Léa qui a le mot de passe" mean?
choices: Léa is the one who has the password.
questions.explanation: C'est … qui puts one person in the spotlight: it's Léa (and nobody else) who has the password.

questions.stem: Read the message: "Salut Hugo ! Tu peux m'envoyer le lien du site où tu as acheté ta tablette ? Je cherche une tablette qui n'est pas trop chère. Merci ! Inès" What does Inès want?
choices: the link to the website where Hugo bought his tablet
a tablet that Hugo doesn't want any more
questions.explanation: Le lien du site où tu as acheté ta tablette = the link to the website where you bought your tablet. She is looking for a tablet that isn't too expensive, but she doesn't ask for Hugo's.

questions.stem: Complete with qui, que or où: "C'est l'imprimante ___ ne marche pas."
questions.explanation: A verb (ne marche pas) follows; the ne belongs to the verb. The printer is the subject, so qui.

questions.stem: Complete with qui, que or où: "C'est le café ___ on va le samedi."
questions.explanation: On va dans ce café: it's the place where you go, so où.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "The password I use doesn't work."
questions.explanation: Le mot de passe que j'utilise ne marche pas. The relative clause (que j'utilise) comes straight after its antecedent, in the middle of the sentence.

questions.stem: Which sentences use the relative pronoun correctly? Select all that apply.
choices: C'est le livre que je lis.
C'est un homme qui travaille ici.
Le jour où il est parti, il pleuvait.
La fille qui je connais est sympa.
questions.explanation: "Le livre que je lis" (a subject follows), "un homme qui travaille" (a verb follows) and "le jour où" (a time) are correct. "Qu'est grande" needs qui (qui est grande), and "qui je connais" needs que (que je connais).

questions.stem: Name the numbered things on this desk.

image.alt: A desk with six numbered things: a screen in the middle, a keyboard in front of it, a mouse on the right of the keyboard, a printer on the right, a tablet on the left and a plug at the end of a cable on the far left.

questions.explanation: 1 is the screen (l'écran), 2 the keyboard (le clavier), 3 the mouse (la souris), 4 the printer (l'imprimante), 5 the tablet (la tablette) and 6 the charger, plugged in and connected to the phone (le chargeur). There is no key or pen.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Le mot de passe = password, le lien = link, le fichier = (computer) file, télécharger = to download, enregistrer = to save (or record). To print is imprimer.

questions.stem: Which pronoun replaces "la robe" in "Quelle robe ? ___-ci ou ___-là ?"
questions.explanation: Robe is feminine singular, so celle: celle-ci ou celle-là ? Celui is masculine, ceux and celles are plural.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ce ne sont pas mes clés, ce sont ___ de Paul."
questions.explanation: Les clés is feminine plural, so celles: celles de Paul (Paul's). Ceux is masculine plural.

questions.stem: Complete: "C'est ton sac ? — Oui, c'est ___."
questions.explanation: Sac is masculine singular, so le mien. La mienne would be for a feminine noun, and mon needs a noun after it.

questions.stem: Complete: "Paul cherche sa clé. Tu as ___ ?" (his)
questions.explanation: The pronoun agrees with the thing owned (clé, feminine), not with Paul: la sienne. Le sien would be for a masculine noun, and sa needs a noun.

questions.stem: Complete: "Notre maison est petite ; ___ est immense." (theirs)
questions.explanation: Maison is feminine singular: la leur. Les leurs is plural, and leur only takes -s in the plural.

questions.stem: Which is the possessive pronoun "ours" for a masculine noun?
questions.explanation: The pronoun has a circumflex: le nôtre (said with a closed o, "noht"). Notre without a circumflex is the determiner (notre maison).

questions.stem: You point at a thing in a shop and don't know its name. You say: "Je voudrais ___, s'il vous plaît."
questions.explanation: With no noun to agree with, use ça. Celui and celle never stand alone (celui-ci, celle-là would work), and lequel is a question word.

questions.stem: How do you say "a leather jacket"?
questions.explanation: Materials take en + noun with no article: une veste en cuir. (Une veste de cuir is also possible, but never with an article.)

questions.stem: Complete: "C'est à qui, ce parapluie ? — C'est ___."
questions.explanation: Être à + a stressed pronoun says who something belongs to: c'est à moi. The other way is c'est le mien.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ma valise est trop ___ ! Je ne peux pas la porter."
questions.explanation: If you can't carry it, it's heavy: lourde (feminine of lourd). Légère is light, douce soft, ronde round.

questions.stem: What does "une bague en argent" mean?
questions.explanation: L'argent is money, but also silver, the metal: en argent = (made of) silver. A gold ring is une bague en or.

questions.stem: Sarah asks "Malik, ton sac est de quelle marque ?" and Malik answers "Le mien ? Il n'a pas de marque. C'est celui de mon frère !" Whose bag is Malik carrying?
choices: his own, from a famous brand
questions.explanation: Celui de mon frère = my brother's (celui stands for le sac). It has no brand (il n'a pas de marque).

questions.stem: Complete: "Les gâteaux ? Ceux que j'ai ___ sont sur la table." (acheter)
questions.explanation: Que stands for ceux, which stands for les gâteaux (masculine plural), and it comes before the verb, so the participle agrees: achetés.

questions.stem: Complete with the right form of "mine": "Ce ne sont pas tes clés, ce sont ___."
questions.explanation: Clés is feminine plural, so les miennes. (Les miens would be for a masculine plural noun.)

questions.stem: Match each noun to the demonstrative pronoun that replaces it.
questions.explanation: The pronoun takes the gender and number of the noun: le pull → celui, la veste → celle, les gâteaux → ceux, les chaussures → celles. Cela is for a thing with no noun.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Celui-ci", "celle de Marie" and "Ça me plaît" are correct. Celui never stands alone, and the pronoun le nôtre needs its circumflex.

questions.stem: What is each numbered object made of? Each one is made of a different material.

image.alt: A shop shelf with six numbered objects: on the top shelf a brown wooden bowl, a grey box and a light blue bottle with a cap; on the bottom shelf a brown handbag, a pink knitted jumper and a yellow ring on a small stand.

questions.explanation: 1 the bowl is wooden (en bois), 2 the box metal (en métal), 3 the bottle plastic (en plastique), 4 the bag leather (en cuir), 5 the knitted jumper wool (en laine) and 6 the ring gold (en or). Materials take en with no article.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "Your car is faster than mine."
questions.explanation: Ta voiture est plus rapide que la mienne. La mienne agrees with voiture (feminine); it comes after que like any other noun.

questions.stem: Which is the adverb from "doux" (gentle)?
questions.explanation: Take the feminine (douce) and add -ment: doucement. The e of douce stays.

questions.stem: Which is the adverb from "évident" (obvious)?
questions.explanation: Adjectives in -ent change to -emment (said "a-MAHN"): évident → évidemment. Adjectives in -ant change to -amment (courant → couramment).

questions.stem: Complete: "Il parle ___ français."
questions.explanation: How he speaks needs an adverb: bien. Bon is the adjective (un bon livre), and meilleur is its comparative.

questions.stem: Complete: "Elle est très ___ : elle travaille tout le temps."
questions.explanation: Someone who works all the time is hard-working: travailleuse (feminine of travailleur). Paresseuse is lazy, égoïste selfish, inquiète worried.

questions.stem: Which sentence is natural French for "I slept well"?
questions.explanation: Short common adverbs like bien go between avoir and the participle: j'ai bien dormi. Bon is an adjective.

questions.stem: How do you say "I'm bored"?
questions.explanation: To be bored is s'ennuyer: je m'ennuie. Je suis ennuyeux means "I'm boring". Je suis ennuyé means "I'm bothered" (embarrassed by a problem).

questions.stem: Complete: "Le TGV est un train très ___."
questions.explanation: After être you need an adjective: rapide. Vite and rapidement are adverbs (il va vite), and "vitement" doesn't exist.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ma mère est ___ : il est minuit et mon frère n'est pas rentré."
questions.explanation: A mother whose son isn't home at midnight is worried: inquiète (feminine of inquiet).

questions.stem: Complete: "Les deux voisines sont ___."
questions.explanation: En colère is a phrase and never changes: elle est en colère, elles sont en colère.

questions.stem: What does "Elle parle couramment trois langues" mean?
questions.explanation: Couramment (from courant) means fluently. Often is souvent, quickly vite or rapidement.

questions.stem: Which adverb is spelled wrongly?
questions.explanation: Gentil is an exception: gentiment (no l). Vraiment, poliment and facilement follow the rule: an adjective ending in a vowel + -ment.

questions.stem: Complete: "C'est un collègue ___ : il fait toujours son travail à l'heure."
questions.explanation: Someone who always does his work on time is reliable: sérieux. In French, sérieux about work is a compliment.

questions.stem: Read: "Lucas est un élève curieux. Il pose beaucoup de questions et il lit vraiment bien. Mais en maths, il fait ses exercices trop vite." What is the teacher's criticism?
choices: He does his maths exercises too fast.
He is lazy in every subject.
questions.explanation: Trop vite = too fast, in maths. He asks a lot of questions (beaucoup de questions) and reads really well (vraiment bien).

questions.stem: Write the adverb made from "complet" (complete).
questions.explanation: Feminine complète + -ment: complètement. The grave accent of the feminine stays.

questions.stem: Translate into French: "I'm bored." (Start with je.)
questions.explanation: S'ennuyer: je m'ennuie. The y becomes i before the silent ending -e. (Je suis ennuyeux = I'm boring.)

questions.stem: Match each adjective to its adverb.
questions.explanation: Vrai ends in a vowel: vraiment. Sérieux takes the feminine: sérieusement. Courant: -ant → -amment. Bon is irregular: bien. Mal is the adverb of mauvais.

questions.stem: Which adverbs are spelled correctly? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Lentement, rapidement and évidemment are correct. Gentil gives gentiment, and courant gives couramment, with mm.

questions.stem: How does each person feel? Name the numbered faces.

image.alt: Five numbered faces: 1 smiling, 2 sad with a tear, 3 red with frowning eyebrows, 4 worried with raised eyebrows, a wavy mouth and a drop of sweat, 5 smiling with eyes closed and chin up, wearing a medal.

questions.explanation: 1 is happy (content), 2 sad (triste), 3 angry (en colère), 4 worried (inquiet) and 5 proud of his medal (fier). Paresseux and généreux describe character, not a feeling on a face.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "He answered politely."
questions.explanation: Il a répondu poliment. A -ment adverb that says how something was done usually goes after the participle in the passé composé.

questions.stem: Complete: "C'est le livre ___ je parle."
questions.explanation: Parler de: je parle de ce livre. De + the antecedent becomes dont. "Que" would need a verb with no preposition (le livre que je lis).

questions.stem: Complete: "Voici l'outil ___ j'ai besoin."
questions.explanation: Avoir besoin de: j'ai besoin de cet outil → l'outil dont j'ai besoin. "L'outil que j'ai besoin" is a very common mistake.

questions.stem: Complete: "J'ai un ami ___ le père est pilote." (whose father)
questions.explanation: Le père de cet ami → dont le père. Dont + noun = whose, and the noun keeps its article (dont le père, never dont son père).

questions.stem: Complete: "___ me plaît, c'est le calme."
questions.explanation: After the gap comes me plaît: me is an object pronoun, so there's no subject; "the thing" is the subject, so ce qui. Qu'est-ce qui asks a question.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ j'aime, c'est la mer."
questions.explanation: A subject (j') follows, so "the thing" is the object of aimer: ce que (ce qu' before a vowel). Qu'est-ce que asks a question, and que alone needs an antecedent.

questions.stem: What does "C'est un roman dont j'ai oublié le titre" mean?
choices: It's a novel whose title I've forgotten.
It's a novel I forgot to read.
It's a novel I've forgotten about.
It's a novel with no title.
questions.explanation: Dont + le titre = whose title. The word order after dont stays normal: dont j'ai oublié le titre.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: J'ai une amie dont son frère habite à Paris.
J'ai une amie que le frère habite à Paris.
J'ai une amie qui le frère habite à Paris.
J'ai une amie dont le frère habite à Paris.
questions.explanation: Dont already means "of whom", so the noun keeps le, not a possessive: dont le frère. Neither que nor qui can mean "whose".

questions.stem: Complete: "C'est la maison ___ mes parents ont achetée."
questions.explanation: Acheter takes a direct object (acheter la maison) and a subject (mes parents) follows: que. The participle agrees: achetée.

questions.stem: Complete: "Prends ___ tu veux."
questions.explanation: There's no noun: you mean "what(ever)", and a subject (tu) follows, so ce que.

questions.stem: What does "Je ne peux pas me passer de mon portable" mean?
choices: I can't do without my phone.
questions.explanation: Se passer de = to do without. (Se passer alone, lesson 2, means to happen.)

questions.stem: Complete with dont, ce qui or ce que: "C'est un jour ___ je me souviens très bien."
questions.explanation: Se souvenir de: je me souviens de ce jour → un jour dont je me souviens.

questions.stem: Complete with dont, ce qui or ce que: "___ est difficile, c'est la prononciation."
questions.explanation: A verb (est) follows, so "the thing" is the subject: ce qui.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to the relative pronoun that fills the gap.
left: C'est la maison ___ est au coin.
questions.explanation: Rêver de → dont. Grandir dans la maison (a place) → où. A verb follows → qui. Adorer takes a direct object and a subject follows → que.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Le livre dont je parle est super.
L'outil que j'ai besoin est cassé.
Le roman dont j'en parle est long.
questions.explanation: "Le livre dont je parle", "Ce qui m'intéresse" and "Prends ce que tu veux" are correct. Avoir besoin de needs dont (l'outil dont j'ai besoin), and dont already contains the de, so no en.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "Here is the ring my grandmother was proud of."
questions.explanation: Voici la bague dont ma grand-mère était fière. Être fier de → dont, straight after the antecedent, then the normal order subject + verb.

questions.stem: According to INSEE's figures for 1 January 2023, which commune has the most inhabitants?
questions.explanation: Paris: 2 103 778, then Marseille 886 040, Lyon 519 127 and Toulouse 514 819.

questions.stem: Complete with the 2023 figures (Marseille 886 040, Lyon 519 127): "Marseille a ___ habitants que Lyon."
questions.explanation: Marseille has more people: plus de + noun, with d' before a vowel or mute h: plus d'habitants.

questions.stem: How many arrondissements does Lyon have?
questions.explanation: Lyon has 9, Marseille 16 and Paris 20.

questions.stem: Complete: "Paris est ___ la plus grande ville de France." (by far)
questions.explanation: By far = de loin. Très can't go before a superlative, and plus is already in la plus grande.

questions.stem: What does "le surnom" mean?
questions.explanation: Le surnom is a false friend: it's a nickname (la cité phocéenne for Marseille). A surname is le nom de famille.

questions.stem: The commune of Marseille covers about 240 km², Paris about 105 km². Which sentence is right?
choices: Marseille est plus de deux fois plus grande que Paris.
Marseille est deux fois plus grande de Paris.
Marseille est plus grande deux fois que Paris.
Marseille est moins grande que Paris.
questions.explanation: 240 ÷ 105 ≈ 2.3, so more than twice as big: plus de deux fois plus grande que. "Than" is always que, and deux fois goes before plus.

questions.stem: Which commune covers the largest area on the map?
choices: They are all about the same.
questions.explanation: Marseille covers about 240.6 km², Toulouse 118.3, Paris 105.4 and Lyon 47.9, because Marseille's boundary includes hills, beaches and the calanques.

questions.stem: What is a métropole in this lesson?
choices: one district of Paris with its own town hall
a group of communes around a big city that work together on transport, housing and roads
the historic centre of a city
the underground railway of a city
questions.explanation: A métropole groups communes around a city (the Métropole de Lyon, the Métropole du Grand Paris, Aix-Marseille-Provence). A numbered district of Paris, Lyon or Marseille is an arrondissement.

questions.stem: Which city is nicknamed "la cité phocéenne"?
questions.explanation: Marseille was founded around 600 BC by Greek sailors from Phocaea (Phocée), hence la cité phocéenne.

questions.stem: How does French usually write the number 2,103,778?
questions.explanation: French separates groups of three digits with a space and uses a comma for decimals: 2 103 778, 105,4 km².

questions.stem: Complete (Lyon 519 127, Marseille 886 040): "Lyon a ___ habitants que Marseille."
questions.explanation: Lyon has fewer people: moins de + noun, d' before a vowel: moins d'habitants.

questions.stem: Match each city to a fact from the lesson.
choices: founded by Greek sailors about 600 BC
historic site on UNESCO's list since 1998
grew about 1.2 % a year from 2017 to 2023
questions.explanation: Paris has 20 arrondissements; Marseille was founded by Greek sailors from Phocaea around 600 BC; the Historic Site of Lyon was listed by UNESCO in 1998; INSEE gives Toulouse about +1.2 % a year from 2017 to 2023.

questions.stem: Name the numbered cities on this map of mainland France.

image.alt: A simplified outline map of mainland France with four numbered dots: 1 in the north, 2 in the east, 3 on the Mediterranean coast in the south-east, 4 in the south-west.

questions.explanation: 1 is Paris (north, on the Seine), 2 Lyon (east), 3 Marseille (on the Mediterranean) and 4 Toulouse (south-west). Lille is in the far north and Bordeaux on the Atlantic side, west.

questions.stem: Which of these statements from the guide are opinions or reputations rather than checked facts? Select all that apply.
choices: Paris est plus stressant que les autres villes.
Marseille a été fondée vers 600 avant Jésus-Christ.
Lyon est la capitale de la gastronomie.
Paris est la ville la plus peuplée de France.
Marseille est plus détendu que Paris.
questions.explanation: Stress, "capital of gastronomy" and being relaxed are reputations: the guide marks them with disent ses visiteurs, pour beaucoup de Français and dit-on. The founding date and Paris's population are checked facts.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "Lyon is less populated than Marseille."
questions.explanation: Lyon est moins peuplé que Marseille. Moins + adjective + que, as in lesson 9.

questions.stem: What is the present participle of "faire"?
questions.explanation: Nous faisons → fais- → faisant. Fait is the past participle.

questions.stem: What is the gérondif of "être"?
questions.explanation: Être is one of three irregular present participles: étant (avoir → ayant, savoir → sachant). Été is the past participle.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je prends mon petit-déjeuner ___ la radio."
questions.explanation: Two things at once, same subject: en + present participle, en écoutant. Without en it isn't a gérondif, and en is never followed by an infinitive.

questions.stem: What does "On apprend en pratiquant" mean?
choices: You learn and then you practise.
questions.explanation: The gérondif says how: en pratiquant = by practising.

questions.stem: Which sentence breaks the same-subject rule (the speaker is the one who arrived)?
choices: J'ai vu Paul en sortant du métro.
En arrivant, le chien m'a regardé.
Il a progressé en écoutant des podcasts.
questions.explanation: The gérondif refers to the subject of the main verb, so "En arrivant, le chien m'a regardé" says that the dog arrived. Say "Quand je suis arrivé, le chien m'a regardé."

questions.stem: How do you say "I like reading"?
questions.explanation: After aimer, French uses an infinitive: j'aime lire. Not every English -ing is a gérondif.

questions.stem: Join "Marie lit." and "Son frère fait la cuisine." into one sentence.
choices: Marie lit en faisant la cuisine son frère.
En faisant la cuisine, Marie lit.
Marie lit en son frère faisant la cuisine.
Marie lit pendant que son frère fait la cuisine.
questions.explanation: There are two subjects, so a gérondif is impossible: use pendant que. "En faisant la cuisine, Marie lit" would mean Marie cooks.

questions.stem: What is the present participle of "commencer"?
questions.explanation: Nous commençons → commenç- → commençant: the ç keeps the c soft before a.

questions.stem: What does "le trajet" mean in "Le trajet en bus dure quarante minutes"?
questions.explanation: Le trajet is the journey from one place to another. The bus journey takes forty minutes.

questions.stem: Write the gérondif of "savoir".
questions.explanation: Savoir is irregular: sachant, so the gérondif is en sachant.

questions.stem: Complete with the gérondif of "prendre": "Je lis le journal ___ le métro."
questions.explanation: Nous prenons → pren- → prenant: en prenant le métro (while taking the metro).

questions.stem: In which of these sentences would French use a gérondif? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "While she works" (en travaillant), "by listening" (en écoutant) and "while driving" (en conduisant) are gérondifs. "I hate waiting" is je déteste attendre, and "thanks for helping me" merci de m'avoir aidé or merci pour ton aide.

questions.stem: Match each infinitive to its present participle.
questions.explanation: Avoir is irregular (ayant). The others come from the nous form: buvons → buvant, mangeons → mangeant, lisons → lisant. Avant means before, and boivant mixes the ils stem with -ant.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "When I arrived at the station, I saw Paul."
questions.explanation: En arrivant à la gare, j'ai vu Paul. The gérondif and the main verb share their subject (je): I arrived and I saw.

questions.stem: Complete with the futur simple of prendre: "Demain, nous ___ le train de 8 heures."
questions.explanation: Prendre is an -re verb, so it drops its final e: prendr- + -ons = "nous prendrons". "Prendrerons" keeps the e, "prenons" is the present, and "prendront" is the ils form.

questions.stem: Which is the futur simple of aller for je?
questions.explanation: Aller has the irregular future stem ir-: "j'irai". "J'aurai" is the futur of avoir, and "j'irais" (with an s) is the conditionnel of aller, lesson 14. "Allerai" doesn't exist.

questions.stem: Complete: "Quand je ___ grand, je serai pilote."
questions.explanation: After quand, when the action is in the future, French uses the futur where English uses the present ("When I grow up"): "Quand je serai grand". "Je suis" would be English logic; "serais" is the conditionnel.

questions.stem: Which is the futur simple of prévoir for ils?
questions.explanation: Prévoir is built on voir in the present (ils prévoient), but its futur is regular: prévoir + -ont = "ils prévoiront". It does not copy voir's verr- (so not "prévront"). "Ils prévoient" is the present.

questions.stem: Complete with the futur simple of appeler: "Je t'___ ce soir."
questions.explanation: Spelling-change -er verbs build the futur on the je present + r: j'appelle → j'appellerai, with the double l. "Appellerais" (with s) is the conditionnel.

questions.stem: Complete with the futur simple of être: "Mes amis ___ en retard."
questions.explanation: Être has the stem ser-, and ils takes -ont: "ils seront". "Serons" is the nous form, "seraient" the conditionnel and "sont" the present.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Plus tard, elle deviendra une infirmière.
questions.explanation: Devenir has the future stem deviendr- (like venir → viendr-), and like être it takes no article before a job: "elle deviendra infirmière".

questions.stem: A weather forecast says: "Demain, il pleuvra sur la Bretagne." What is "pleuvra"?
choices: the futur simple of pleurer (to cry)
the futur simple of pleuvoir (to rain)
questions.explanation: Il pleut → il pleuvra (stem pleuvr-), the futur simple; forecasts are a classic place for it. The conditionnel would be "pleuvrait", the passé composé "il a plu", and pleurer gives "il pleurera".

questions.stem: What does "Il viendra sûrement" usually mean?
questions.explanation: Viendra is the futur of venir. Despite its look, sûrement usually means "very probably" in everyday French: a little less than "for sure".

questions.stem: Read: "Le programme de samedi : à dix heures, nous visiterons le musée. À midi, nous mangerons au restaurant du port. L'après-midi, chacun fera ce qu'il veut. Le soir, nous prendrons le bateau de 19 heures pour rentrer." What will happen in the afternoon?
choices: They will have lunch at the port.
Everyone will be free to do what they want.
They will take the boat home.
questions.explanation: "L'après-midi, chacun fera ce qu'il veut" = in the afternoon each person will do what they want. The museum is at ten, lunch at noon and the boat in the evening. (chacun = each one, lesson 18)

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: At the start of a sentence, use "peut-être que" (with a hyphen; que becomes qu' before il). Without the hyphen, "peut être" means "can be". Peut-être can also follow the verb: "Il viendra peut-être".

questions.stem: Complete: "Quand il ___, je prends toujours le bus."
questions.explanation: Here quand means "every time": it is a habit (je prends toujours), so the present stays: "Quand il pleut". The futur after quand is only for an action in the future.

questions.stem: What does "Elle a réalisé son rêve" mean?
choices: She told everyone about her dream.
She had the same dream again.
She made her dream come true.
questions.explanation: Réaliser un rêve, un projet = to make it happen, to achieve it. (For "realise" in the sense of understand, careful French says se rendre compte.)

questions.stem: Type the futur simple of faire: "Demain, nous ___ les courses."
questions.explanation: Faire has the irregular stem fer- + -ons: "nous ferons" (said "fuh-RON").

questions.stem: Type the futur simple of acheter: "Demain, j'___ des fleurs."
questions.explanation: J'achète + r + -ai = "j'achèterai": the è of the present stays in the whole futur.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "When I have time, I'll write to you."
questions.explanation: French uses the futur after quand for a future action: "Quand j'aurai le temps, je t'écrirai." (j'aurai = futur of avoir; t' = to you before the verb.)

questions.stem: Match each verb to its future stem.
questions.explanation: These stems are irregular but the endings are the usual -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont: je serai, j'aurai, j'irai, je saurai, je verrai. Sav- is the imparfait stem of savoir (je savais).

questions.stem: Which future stem goes in each numbered empty space on the wheel?

image.alt: A wheel of twelve verbs with their future stems. Six segments show the stems: envoyer enverr-, venir viendr-, devenir deviendr-, pouvoir pourr-, vouloir voudr-, devoir devr-. Six segments have a number instead of a stem: être, avoir, aller, faire, savoir and voir.

questions.explanation: être → ser-, avoir → aur-, aller → ir-, faire → fer-, savoir → saur-, voir → verr-. "Av-" and "fais-" are imparfait stems (j'avais, je faisais), not future stems.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct futur simple? Select all that apply.
choices: Nous irons à Paris en mai.
Tu feras la vaisselle ce soir.
questions.explanation: "Nous irons", "ils pourront" and "tu feras" use the irregular stems ir-, pourr- and fer-. Prévoir gives "je prévoirai", and pleuvoir gives "il pleuvra".

questions.stem: Which is the conditionnel of vouloir for je?
questions.explanation: Future stem voudr- + the imparfait ending -ais = "je voudrais" (I would like). "Je voudrai" is the futur, "je voulais" the imparfait, and -ait is the il ending.

questions.stem: Complete with the conditionnel of aimer: "Mes parents ___ partir en Grèce."
questions.explanation: Infinitive aimer + the ils ending -aient = "aimeraient". "Aimeront" is the futur, "aimaient" the imparfait (no r), and "aimerions" the nous form.

questions.stem: You arrive at a hotel without a booking. Which question is the most polite?
choices: Je veux une chambre pour ce soir.
Vous auriez une chambre pour ce soir ?
Donnez-moi une chambre pour ce soir.
Vous avez eu une chambre pour ce soir ?
questions.explanation: The conditionnel (vous auriez = would you have) softens the request. "Je veux" and the imperative "Donnez-moi" sound blunt, and "vous avez eu" is a passé composé that doesn't make sense here.

questions.stem: Complete: "À ta place, je ___ en juin."
questions.explanation: "À ta place" (if I were you) is followed by the conditionnel: partir → partir- + -ais = "je partirais". "Partirai" is the futur.

questions.stem: How do you say "You should book" to a friend?
questions.explanation: Advice uses the conditionnel of devoir: "tu devrais" + infinitive, with no de. "Tu devras" is the futur (you will have to).

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I would do the shopping"?
questions.explanation: "Would" = conditionnel: fer- + -ais = "je ferais". "Je ferai" (no s) is the futur (I will do), "je faisais" the imparfait (I was doing / used to do).

questions.stem: What is "une location"?
choices: a rental (a flat, a house or a car you rent)
questions.explanation: False friend: une location is a rental (une location de voiture = a car hire). "A location" is un endroit or un lieu, and a booking is une réservation.

questions.stem: The receptionist says: "Désolé, l'hôtel est complet." What does she mean?
choices: The hotel is closed for the season.
The hotel has just been renovated.
questions.explanation: Complet (feminine complète) = full, no room left. "Breakfast is included" would be "le petit-déjeuner est compris".

questions.stem: Look at the booking page. How much do two nights in the double room cost?

image.alt: A booking page for the invented Hôtel des Trois Mouettes in Saint-Malo, 14 to 16 August, 2 nights, 2 adults. Chambre double, vue sur la mer, 98 euros a night, disponible. Chambre familiale (4 personnes), 135 euros a night, complet. Chambre simple, 72 euros a night, disponible. Petit-déjeuner compris, climatisation, Wi-Fi gratuit, annulation gratuite jusqu'à 48 h avant l'arrivée.

questions.explanation: The double room is 98 € per night (98 € / nuit), and the stay is 2 nights: 2 × 98 = 196 €. 270 € would be two nights in the family room, which is complet anyway; 144 € is two nights in the single room.

questions.stem: Look at the booking page. Which room can't you book for 14–16 August?

image.alt: A booking page for the invented Hôtel des Trois Mouettes in Saint-Malo, 14 to 16 August, 2 nights, 2 adults. Chambre double, vue sur la mer, 98 euros a night, disponible. Chambre familiale (4 personnes), 135 euros a night, complet. Chambre simple, 72 euros a night, disponible. Petit-déjeuner compris, climatisation, Wi-Fi gratuit, annulation gratuite jusqu'à 48 h avant l'arrivée.

questions.explanation: The family room is marked "Complet" (fully booked). The double and single rooms are "Disponible" (available).

questions.stem: You want to know whether breakfast is included. What do you ask?
questions.explanation: Compris = included. Complet means full, annulé means cancelled, and disponible means available, which asks whether you can have breakfast at all, not whether it is in the price.

questions.stem: How do you say "I'm going to visit my grandmother"?
choices: Je vais visiter à ma grand-mère.
Je vais rendre visite à ma grand-mère.
Je vais rendre visite ma grand-mère.
Je vais faire la visite de ma grand-mère.
questions.explanation: Visiter is for places (visiter un musée). For a person, French says rendre visite à quelqu'un, with à.

questions.stem: What does "On pourrait aller à la plage" mean?
choices: We'll be able to go to the beach.
We could go to the beach.
We were able to go to the beach.
We can't go to the beach.
questions.explanation: Pourrait is the conditionnel of pouvoir (pourr- + -ait): "could", here a suggestion. "We'll be able to" would be the futur, on pourra.

questions.stem: Type the conditionnel of pouvoir: "___-vous m'aider, s'il vous plaît ?"
questions.explanation: Pouvoir has the stem pourr- + the vous ending -iez: "Pourriez-vous …?" (Could you …?)

questions.stem: Type the conditionnel of avoir: "Est-ce que vous ___ une chambre double ?"
questions.explanation: Avoir has the future stem aur- + the vous ending -iez: "vous auriez" (would you have).

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "Would it be possible to pay by card?"
questions.explanation: "Ce serait possible de + infinitive ?" is a polite way to ask: serait is the conditionnel of être.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to what it does.
questions.explanation: All four use the conditionnel: pourriez-vous (could you), j'aimerais (I'd like), tu devrais (you should), on pourrait (we could). A promise would usually be in the futur: Je t'appellerai.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things at the hotel.

image.alt: A hotel reception with numbered markers: the front desk, a key on the desk, an open book on the desk, a backpack on the floor, an air-conditioning unit on the wall and a window showing the sea and a boat.

questions.explanation: 1 la réception (the desk), 2 la clé, 3 le guide (the open guidebook), 4 le sac à dos, 5 la climatisation, 6 la vue (the sea view through the window). The suitcase (la valise) has no number, and there is no swimsuit.

questions.stem: Which forms are in the conditionnel? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Conditionnel = future stem + -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient: je voudrais, vous devriez, il faudrait. "Nous ferons" and "tu auras" have futur endings.

questions.stem: Complete: "S'il ___ beau demain, on ira à la plage."
questions.explanation: With a real condition, the si clause is in the present, even when the result is in the future: "S'il fait beau demain, on ira …". Never the futur after si (= if).

questions.stem: Complete the advice: "Si tu es fatigué, ___ !"
questions.explanation: Affirmative imperative of se reposer: the verb without its s (tu reposes → repose) + hyphen + toi: "repose-toi".

questions.stem: What does "Il ne faut pas fumer ici" mean?
choices: You don't have to smoke here.
questions.explanation: Il ne faut pas always forbids: "you must not". "You don't have to" is tu n'es pas obligé(e) de or ce n'est pas la peine de.

questions.stem: How do you say "You don't have to come" (it's up to you)?
choices: Tu n'es pas obligé de venir.
questions.explanation: Tu n'es pas obligé(e) de + infinitive = you don't have to. "Il ne faut pas venir" and "Tu ne dois pas venir" usually mean you must not come.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: S'il pleut, je reste à la maison.
Si il pleut, je reste à la maison.
S'elle pleut, je reste à la maison.
Si il pleuvra, je reste à la maison.
questions.explanation: Si drops its i only before il and ils: s'il, s'ils (but si elle, si on). And the si clause takes the present, not the futur.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il vaut mieux ___ avant un examen."
questions.explanation: Il vaut mieux is followed directly by the infinitive, with no de: "Il vaut mieux dormir" (It's better to sleep).

questions.stem: Complete: "Le médecin m'a conseillé ___ du sport."
questions.explanation: Conseiller à quelqu'un de + infinitive: "Il m'a conseillé de faire du sport." Here m' is the "à quelqu'un" (to me).

questions.stem: How do you say "Don't worry!" to a friend?
questions.explanation: In the negative imperative the pronoun goes back before the verb and has no hyphen: ne + t' + inquiète + pas. (Inquiète-toi is the affirmative form.)

questions.stem: "Si tu veux maigrir, mange moins de sucre." What does maigrir mean?
questions.explanation: Maigrir (a finir verb: je maigris, nous maigrissons) = to lose weight; grossir = to put on weight.

questions.stem: In the reading "Dix conseils pour être en forme", what should you do if you are stressed?
choices: go to the gym every day
questions.explanation: Tip 9: "Si vous êtes stressé, prenez dix minutes pour vous détendre." (se détendre = to relax). Tip 5 actually warns against a too-strict diet.

questions.stem: Julien says: "Si tu fais un peu de sport, tu dormiras mieux." Why is "dormiras" in the futur?
choices: Because si is always followed by the futur.
It is a result in the future of a condition in the present.
Because it is a polite request.
questions.explanation: Si + present (tu fais) → futur (tu dormiras) for a future result. The futur goes in the main clause, never after si itself.

questions.stem: Someone apologises for being late and you answer "Ce n'est pas grave." What do you mean?
questions.explanation: Grave = serious (an illness, a problem); "Ce n'est pas grave" is the everyday way to say it doesn't matter, never mind.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je ne me ___ pas très bien aujourd'hui."
questions.explanation: Se sentir is like partir: je me sens, tu te sens, il se sent. "Sent" is the il form.

questions.stem: Type the right form of être: "Si tu ___ fatigué, repose-toi."
questions.explanation: Si + present: "si tu es fatigué". The present, not the futur (seras), after si.

questions.stem: Type the missing word: "Il ___ mieux partir tôt." (It's better to leave early.)
questions.explanation: Il vaut mieux + infinitive = it's better to. Vaut comes from valoir; you only need it in this phrase.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "If it rains, we'll stay at home."
questions.explanation: Si + il = s'il; si + present (pleut), then the futur (restera). With si first, a comma separates the two parts.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to its meaning.
left: Tu n'es pas obligé de dormir.
questions.explanation: Il faut = you need to; il ne faut pas = you must not; tu n'es pas obligé de = you don't have to; tu devrais (conditionnel of devoir) = you should.

questions.stem: Ma semaine santé: name the healthy habit in each numbered picture.

image.alt: A weekly planner from lundi to dimanche with a picture for each day and numbers from mardi to dimanche: a dumbbell, a plate with vegetables and fish, a tooth, a crossed-out cigarette, a tube of sun cream under the sun, and a person stretching on a mat.

questions.explanation: 1 (mardi) la salle de sport, 2 un repas équilibré, 3 le dentiste, 4 arrêter de fumer, 5 la crème solaire, 6 se détendre. Lundi (sleep) has no number.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Si elle veut, elle peut venir.
Si tu auras le temps, appelle-moi.
Si ils viennent, on mangera ensemble.
Si tu as fini, tu peux partir.
questions.explanation: Correct: s'il + present → futur; si elle + present → present; si + passé composé (something finished) → present. Wrong: "si tu auras" (no futur after si: si tu as le temps) and "si ils" (s'ils).

questions.stem: Complete with the passé composé of pleuvoir: "Hier, il ___ pendant trois heures."
questions.explanation: Pleuvoir has the irregular participle plu and takes avoir: "il a plu". "Pleuvra" is the futur and doesn't fit hier.

questions.stem: Complete with the futur simple of faire: "Demain, il ___ beau."
questions.explanation: Faire has the future stem fer- (one r): "il fera beau". Weather verbs always stay in the il form.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il est important ___ trier le verre."
questions.explanation: Il est + adjective + de + infinitive: "Il est important de trier".

questions.stem: Your friend asks "Trier les déchets ?" You answer: "Oui, ___ important."
questions.explanation: When nothing follows the adjective (it refers back to what was said), only c'est works: "Oui, c'est important." Il est important needs de + infinitive after it.

questions.stem: What does a sign saying "Baignade interdite" mean?
questions.explanation: Interdit = forbidden; it agrees with la baignade (swimming), so it is interdite. Similar signs: Interdit de fumer, Stationnement interdit.

questions.stem: Complete with jeter: "Je ___ les bouteilles dans la colonne à verre."
questions.explanation: Jeter doubles its t before a silent ending: je jette, tu jettes, il jette, ils jettent (but nous jetons). "Jettes" is the tu form.

questions.stem: Complete with protéger: "Nous ___ la nature."
questions.explanation: In the nous form, the é stays (the ending -ons is heard) and an e keeps the g soft before o: "nous protégeons". The è is only for je, tu, il and ils (je protège).

questions.stem: Complete: "J'éteins la lumière ___ économiser l'électricité."
questions.explanation: Pour + infinitive gives the purpose: in order to save electricity.

questions.stem: "Demain, le ciel sera nuageux à Paris." What will the weather be like?
questions.explanation: Nuageux (feminine nuageuse) = cloudy, from le nuage (cloud). Sunny is ensoleillé.

questions.stem: In the notice "Notre immeuble devient plus vert", where does glass go?
choices: in the container in the street
questions.explanation: "Le verre dans le conteneur de la rue." The yellow bin is for packaging and paper, the brown bin for kitchen waste, and nothing may be left in the hall.

questions.stem: In the same notice, what will happen from 1 March?
choices: The heating will be turned off.
A brown bin for kitchen waste will be put in the courtyard.
Glass will be collected door to door.
Cardboard boxes will be allowed in the hall.
questions.explanation: "À partir du 1er mars, il y aura un nouveau bac marron dans la cour pour les déchets de cuisine." Il y aura is the futur of il y a.

questions.stem: Since 1 January 2023, what can go in the yellow bin across almost all of metropolitan France?
questions.explanation: Since 2023 the sorting rule has been the same almost everywhere: all packaging (plastic pots, trays and films included) goes in the yellow bin. Glass goes to the bottle bank, and food waste to compost or a brown bin.

questions.stem: Type the futur simple of pleuvoir: "Demain, il ___ en Bretagne."
questions.explanation: Pleuvoir has the future stem pleuvr-: "il pleuvra" (not "pleuvera").

questions.stem: Type the past participle of pleuvoir: "Hier soir, il a ___."
questions.explanation: Il pleut → il a plu (it rained).

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "It is forbidden to throw rubbish here."
questions.explanation: Il est + adjective + de + infinitive: "Il est interdit de jeter des déchets ici."

questions.stem: Match each form to its tense.
questions.explanation: Pleuvoir in four tenses: il a plu (finished event), il pleuvait (background), il va pleuvoir (aller + infinitive), il pleuvra (stem pleuvr-). The conditionnel would be il pleuvrait.

questions.stem: Look at tomorrow's map. What will the weather be at each number?

image.alt: A simplified map of France with six numbered weather symbols: a cloud over Paris, a cloud with rain near Brest, a grey cloud with lightning near Lyon, a sun near Marseille, wind lines near Bordeaux and a cloud with snowflakes in the Alps.

questions.explanation: 1 nuageux (a plain cloud, Paris), 2 de la pluie (Brest), 3 un orage (lightning, Lyon), 4 ensoleillé (Marseille), 5 du vent (Bordeaux), 6 de la neige (the Alps). No symbol shows a flood or a heatwave.

questions.stem: In a common sorting system, what goes in each numbered container? (Colours vary from town to town.)

image.alt: Four numbered containers with items above them: a yellow bin with a plastic bottle, a can and a cardboard box; a green bottle bank with a glass bottle and a jar; a brown bin with vegetable peelings; a grey bin with a bin bag.

questions.explanation: 1 les emballages et le papier (yellow bin), 2 le verre (bottle bank), 3 les déchets de cuisine (brown bin), 4 les ordures ménagères (everything else). Medicines go back to the pharmacy, not in any of these.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Il est possible recycler ce sac.
Ici, on ne jette pas le verre dans la poubelle.
questions.explanation: Correct: il est + adjective + de + infinitive; c'est + adjective + de in speech; on for rules. Wrong: "possible recycler" needs de; weather verbs never take ils (il pleut).

questions.stem: Complete: "Si j'___ riche, j'achèterais un voilier."
questions.explanation: In an imaginary condition, the si clause takes the imparfait: "si j'étais". The conditionnel (j'achèterais) goes in the other half, never after si.

questions.stem: Complete: "Si tu habitais à Paris, tu ___ au musée tous les week-ends."
questions.explanation: Si + imparfait (habitais) → conditionnel: ir- + -ais = "tu irais". "Tu iras" is the futur, which goes with si + present.

questions.stem: Which sentence talks about an imaginary situation (not true now)?
choices: Si j'ai une voiture, je viendrai.
Quand j'aurai une voiture, je viendrai.
J'ai une voiture, donc je viens.
Si j'avais une voiture, je viendrais.
questions.explanation: Si + imparfait + conditionnel = imaginary: the speaker has no car. "Si j'ai une voiture" is a real possibility, and the other two talk about facts or the future.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake?
choices: Si j'avais le temps, je viendrais.
Si j'aurais le temps, je viendrais.
Je viendrais si j'avais le temps.
S'il avait le temps, il viendrait.
questions.explanation: No conditionnel after si: "Si j'avais le temps". Remember "Les si n'aiment pas les -rais". The other three are correct, in either order.

questions.stem: What does "Si j'étais toi, je prendrais le train" mean?
choices: If you were me, you'd take the train.
When I'm with you, I take the train.
If I were you, I'd take the train.
If I was taking the train, I'd see you.
questions.explanation: Si j'étais toi = if I were you, the same advice as à ta place (lesson 14), followed by the conditionnel.

questions.stem: What does "Si on allait au cinéma ?" mean?
choices: If we went to the cinema, …
How about going to the cinema?
We will go to the cinema if you want.
questions.explanation: Si on + imparfait with a question mark and no main clause is a suggestion (lesson 22), not an imaginary condition.

questions.stem: In the French Loto you choose 5 numbers out of 49 and 1 lucky number out of 10. About what is the chance of winning the jackpot?
questions.explanation: There are 1,906,884 ways to choose 5 numbers out of 49; times 10 lucky numbers = 19,068,840. 1 in 1.9 million forgets the lucky number.

questions.stem: In the reading "Et si vous gagniez au loto ?", what would Kevin really do with the money?
choices: buy a flat for his parents
questions.explanation: Kevin jokes that he would quit (je démissionnerais tout de suite ! Non, je plaisante), then says "j'achèterais un appartement pour mes parents". Sailing is Martine's dream, the charity Amina's.

questions.stem: What does "Si j'avais su, je serais venu" mean?
choices: If I had known, I would have come.
If I knew, I would come.
If I know, I will come.
questions.explanation: This is the B1 pattern for a past that didn't happen: si + plus-que-parfait (j'avais su), conditionnel passé (je serais venu). Just recognise "si j'avais su", which people say all the time.

questions.stem: Type the imparfait of avoir: "Si j'___ le temps, j'apprendrais le piano."
questions.explanation: Si + imparfait: nous avons → av- + -ais = "j'avais".

questions.stem: Type the conditionnel of faire: "Si tu gagnais au loto, qu'est-ce que tu ___ ?"
questions.explanation: Future stem fer- + -ais = "tu ferais" (what would you do?).

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "If I were rich, I would buy a boat."
questions.explanation: Si + imparfait (j'étais), comma, then the conditionnel (j'achèterais).

questions.stem: What does each sentence express?
left: S'il fait beau, on ira à la plage.
Si j'étais riche, j'achèterais un voilier.
Si on allait à la plage ?
Si tu viens, apporte du pain.
questions.explanation: Si + present = a real condition (with futur or imperative after it); si + imparfait + conditionnel = an imaginary one; si on + imparfait alone with a question mark = a suggestion.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Si j'avais le temps, je voyagerais.
Si j'aurais le temps, je voyagerais.
questions.explanation: Correct: si + imparfait with the conditionnel in the other half, in either order; si j'étais toi. Wrong: "si j'aurais" (no conditionnel after si) and "si j'étais tu" (toi).

questions.stem: Where does an empty yoghurt pot go in the common French system since 2023?
questions.explanation: Since 1 January 2023 all packaging, including plastic pots, trays and films, goes in the yellow bin almost everywhere in metropolitan France.

questions.stem: Where does an empty jam jar go?
choices: to the bottle bank (la colonne à verre)
questions.explanation: Glass goes to the bottle bank, without its lid; the metal lid can go in the yellow bin.

questions.stem: What changed on 1 January 2024?
choices: Plastic bags were banned at the checkout.
Local councils must give everyone a way to sort food waste.
All packaging went into the yellow bin.
questions.explanation: Since 1 January 2024 every council must offer a way to sort biowaste (a brown bin, collection points or compost). The bags were banned in 2016, Vélib' opened in 2007 and the yellow-bin rule dates from 2023.

questions.stem: Complete: "J'achète souvent des vêtements ___."
questions.explanation: D'occasion (second-hand) never changes: un vélo d'occasion, des vêtements d'occasion.

questions.stem: Complete: "Au marché, on trouve des produits ___."
questions.explanation: Local follows the -al → -aux pattern in the masculine plural: des produits locaux (feminine: des pommes locales).

questions.stem: What is "un vide-grenier"?
choices: an empty attic you can rent
a street sale where people sell their old things
questions.explanation: Literally an "attic-emptier": a weekend sale (often on a Sunday) in a street or village where people sell their old things; like a car-boot sale or a yard sale.

questions.stem: In the waste order that French and European law follow, what is the best thing to do?
questions.explanation: From best to least good: réduire, réutiliser, recycler, jeter. The best waste is the waste you never produce.

questions.stem: When did Paris open its shared-bike scheme, Vélib'?
questions.explanation: Vélib' opened on 15 July 2007. Lyon's Vélo'v, one of the first big schemes, opened in 2005.

questions.stem: In the debate, why is Bernard against banning cars from the town centre?
choices: He thinks the air will be dirtier.
He thinks customers won't come to the shops any more.
He thinks children will be in danger.
questions.explanation: "Les clients ne viendront plus dans nos magasins s'ils ne peuvent pas se garer." He prefers more car-sharing and public transport.

questions.stem: Type the noun that goes with gaspiller: "le ___ alimentaire" (food waste)
questions.explanation: Gaspiller (to waste) → le gaspillage (wasting): le gaspillage alimentaire = food waste.

questions.stem: Put these green milestones in France in the order they happened.
choices: no more single-use plastic checkout bags
all packaging in the yellow bin
questions.explanation: 2005 Vélo'v; 15 July 2007 Vélib'; 1 July 2016 plastic checkout bags banned; 10 February 2020 loi AGEC; 1 January 2023 all packaging in the yellow bin; 1 January 2024 food-waste sorting.

questions.stem: Name each numbered level, from best (top) to least good (bottom).

image.alt: An upside-down pyramid with four numbered levels, widest at the top: a water bottle, a reused bag, a recycling triangle and a bin. An arrow at the side goes from meilleur at the top to moins bon at the bottom.

questions.explanation: 1 réduire, 2 réutiliser, 3 recycler, 4 jeter: the order of the waste hierarchy.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Organic is bio (des produits bio), which is not one of the four words.

questions.stem: In the common system since 2023, which go in the yellow bin? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Packaging goes in the yellow bin: plastic bottles, cans (la canette) and cardboard (le carton). Glass goes to the bottle bank and an apple core to the compost.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il faut que tu ___ la vaisselle."
questions.explanation: Il faut que + subjunctive; faire is irregular: que je fasse, que tu fasses. At A2 you could say "Tu dois faire la vaisselle".

questions.stem: What is the subjunctive of partir for je?
questions.explanation: Ils partent → part- + -e = que je parte (the t is heard). "Je pars" is the present indicative.

questions.stem: How do you say "I want to leave"?
questions.explanation: When the person who wants is the person who acts, use the infinitive. The subjunctive is for wanting someone else to act: Je veux que tu partes.

questions.stem: Which form is the subjunctive of être (il)?
questions.explanation: Être: que je sois, que tu sois, qu'il soit … "Est" is the present, "sera" the futur and "serait" the conditionnel.

questions.stem: Which is a natural A2 way to say "Il faut que nous partions tôt" without the subjunctive?
questions.explanation: Devoir + infinitive (or il faut + infinitive) says the same thing. "Nous partions" alone is the imparfait (we were leaving).

questions.stem: In "Il faut que je parle", why does "parle" look like the present?
choices: Because il faut que takes the present.
For -er verbs, the je, tu, il and ils subjunctive forms look like the present.
questions.explanation: Ils parlent → parl- + -e = que je parle, the same spelling as je parle. You recognise the subjunctive by the trigger (il faut que).

questions.stem: In "Les règles de la coloc", what must you do if you invite friends?
questions.explanation: Rule 3: "Si quelqu'un invite des amis, il faut qu'il prévienne les autres." Prévienne is the subjunctive of prévenir (to let know). The quiet time in rule 4 starts at 23 heures (11 p.m.).

questions.stem: What does "On fait la vaisselle à tour de rôle" mean?
choices: We take turns doing the dishes.
We do the dishes every day.
questions.explanation: À tour de rôle = in turn, taking turns (c'est ton tour = it's your turn).

questions.stem: "Il faut que tu ailles chez le dentiste." Which verb is "ailles"?
questions.explanation: Aille, ailles, aille, allions, alliez, aillent: the subjunctive of aller. Avoir gives aie, aies, ait.

questions.stem: Use the rule (ils present − ent + ending). Which is the subjunctive of dormir? "Il faut que tu ___ huit heures."
questions.explanation: Ils dorment → dorm- + -es = "que tu dormes".

questions.stem: Say it without the subjunctive. "Il faut que je parte." = "Je dois ___."
questions.explanation: Devoir + infinitive: "Je dois partir." It means the same and is perfectly correct.

questions.stem: Put the steps for making a regular subjunctive in order.
choices: Take the ils present: ils partent.
Put que and the subject first: que tu partes.
questions.explanation: Ils form → stem → ending → que + subject. The same steps give que je dorme, qu'il écrive, que tu lises.

questions.stem: Match each subjunctive form to its infinitive.
questions.explanation: The six irregulars to recognise: être (sois), avoir (aie), aller (aille), faire (fasse), pouvoir (puisse), savoir (sache).

questions.stem: Which sentences contain a subjunctive? Select all that apply.
choices: Je veux qu'il sache la vérité.
Il faut qu'on fasse les courses.
questions.explanation: Viennes (venir), sache (savoir) and fasse (faire) are subjunctives after il faut que / vouloir que. "Il faut venir" uses the infinitive, and "je sais qu'il vient" states a fact with the indicative.

questions.stem: Complete so that it means "I don't work here any more": "Je ne travaille ___ ici."
questions.explanation: No longer, not any more = ne … plus: Je ne travaille plus ici. Pas would just mean "I don't work here", jamais "never", and rien "nothing" doesn't fit with travailler ici.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: In the passé composé personne goes after the participle: je n'ai vu personne. It never takes pas as well (je n'ai pas vu personne is a common mistake), and nothing comes between n' and the auxiliary.

questions.stem: Complete: "Personne ___ venu."
questions.explanation: When personne is the subject, ne comes straight after it and there is no pas: Personne n'est venu (nobody came). Without ne the sentence is casual speech at best; with pas it is wrong.

questions.stem: What does "Je n'ai que dix euros" mean?
choices: I no longer have ten euros.
I have more than ten euros.
questions.explanation: Ne … que means only: it is a restriction, not a negative. I don't have ten euros would be je n'ai pas dix euros; no longer would be ne … plus.

questions.stem: How do you say "There's no more coffee"?
choices: Il n'y a plus de café.
Il n'y a que de café.
Il n'y a pas plus de café.
Il n'y a plus du café.
questions.explanation: After ne … plus, du becomes de: il n'y a plus de café. Ne … que would mean only (and keeps du: il n'y a que du café). Pas and plus never go together.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je n'ai ___ idée." (I have no idea.)
questions.explanation: Aucun agrees with the noun: idée is feminine, so aucune, and the noun is singular (no -s on aucune here). Pas never goes with aucun.

questions.stem: How do you say "I didn't understand anything" in the passé composé?
questions.explanation: Rien, like pas, plus and jamais, goes before the participle: je n'ai rien compris. Only personne, aucun, que and nulle part go after it.

questions.stem: How do you say "There are two people at reception"?
choices: Il n'y a personne à l'accueil.
Il n'y a deux personnes à l'accueil.
Il y a deux personne à l'accueil.
Il y a deux personnes à l'accueil.
questions.explanation: Here personne is the noun la personne (a person), so it takes a plural -s and no ne: deux personnes. Il n'y a personne means there is nobody.

questions.stem: Read the advert: "Restaurant Le Quai cherche un serveur à temps partiel. Aucune expérience demandée. Travail le soir uniquement, du jeudi au dimanche. Salaire : 13 € de l'heure." Which statement is true?
choices: You only work in the evenings.
questions.explanation: Travail le soir uniquement = work in the evenings only. Aucune expérience demandée = no experience required; à temps partiel = part-time; du jeudi au dimanche = Thursday to Sunday, so not Monday.

questions.stem: Complete: "Elle a trouvé ___ de vendeuse dans une boulangerie."
questions.explanation: Le poste (masculine) is a position or job: un poste de vendeuse. La poste (feminine) is the post office. Le chômage is unemployment, and l'entretien (an interview) is masculine.

questions.stem: Complete the sign: "Merci de ___ fumer."
questions.explanation: Before an infinitive, ne pas stays together in front of it: Merci de ne pas fumer (thank you for not smoking). The same goes for ne plus, ne jamais, ne rien.

questions.stem: Your friend asks: "Tu as déjà travaillé dans un hôtel ?" You never have. What do you answer?
questions.explanation: Jamais alone means never. Personne answers who?, rien answers what?, and aucune needs a feminine noun to refer to.

questions.stem: In casual speech you hear: "J'ai rien compris." What does it mean?
questions.explanation: In speech French often drops ne: j'ai rien compris = je n'ai rien compris. Rien still means nothing. Write the full form yourself.

questions.stem: How do you say "Nobody answered my advert"?
choices: La personne n'a répondu à mon annonce.
Personne n'a répondu à mon annonce.
Personne n'a pas répondu à mon annonce.
questions.explanation: Personne as the subject + n' + verb, without pas. La personne is a person; je n'ai répondu à personne means I didn't answer anyone.

questions.stem: Write the missing word (nobody): "Je n'ai vu ___ au bureau."
questions.explanation: Personne goes after the participle: je n'ai vu personne au bureau.

questions.stem: Write the missing word: "Je ne fume ___." (I don't smoke any more.)
questions.explanation: No longer, not any more = ne … plus: je ne fume plus. The s of plus is silent here.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "I've never worked on Sundays."
questions.explanation: Ne before the auxiliary, jamais between the auxiliary and the participle: Je n'ai jamais travaillé le dimanche.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Le métier is a trade or profession, l'entretien a (job) interview, le salaire the pay, le stage an internship and le chômage unemployment. To apply is postuler; a meeting is une réunion.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Je ne travaille pas plus ici.
questions.explanation: Personne n'est venu (subject personne, no pas), je n'ai eu aucun problème (aucun after the participle, singular noun) and il n'a rien dit (rien before the participle) are correct. Je ne travaille pas plus ici has two second words (use plus alone). Je n'ai que de pain is wrong: ne … que keeps the article: je n'ai que du pain.

questions.stem: Name the heading of each numbered line in this job advert.

image.alt: A job advert for Le Petit Marché, a grocer's in Rennes, with five numbered blank headings. Next to them: vendeur / vendeuse; 20 heures par semaine, du mardi au samedi; 14 € brut de l'heure; aucun diplôme demandé, mais un an d'expérience dans la vente; CV et lettre avant le 30 novembre.

questions.explanation: Vendeur / vendeuse is le poste (the position); 20 heures par semaine is à temps partiel (part-time); 14 € de l'heure is le salaire; one year in sales is l'expérience; CV et lettre is la candidature (the application). Twenty hours a week isn't à temps plein (full-time), and le chômage (unemployment) isn't part of an advert.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ étudiant a un emploi du temps."
questions.explanation: Before a singular noun, use the determiner chaque. Chacun stands alone (chacun a …); tous and plusieurs need a plural noun.

questions.stem: Complete: "Les étudiantes ? ___ a choisi une matière."
questions.explanation: With no noun after it, use the pronoun: chacune (feminine, for les étudiantes), with a singular verb (a choisi). Chaque needs a noun; toutes would need a plural verb (ont choisi); quelques needs a noun.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tout le monde ___ content."
questions.explanation: Tout le monde (everyone) takes a singular verb: tout le monde est content. Sont is the classic mistake.

questions.stem: In which sentence is the s of tous pronounced?
questions.explanation: When tous stands alone as a pronoun (all of them), its s is said: ils sont tous là, "toos". Before a noun (tous les jours, tous mes amis) the s is silent.

questions.stem: How do you say "I studied all day (the whole day)"?
questions.explanation: Toute la journée = the whole day. Tous les jours means every day. Tout must agree with the feminine journée: toute.

questions.stem: Complete: "J'ai appris quelque chose ___."
questions.explanation: After quelque chose, an adjective needs de and stays masculine: quelque chose d'intéressant (de elides before a vowel).

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Plusieurs goes straight before the noun, with no article, and has the same form for masculine and feminine: plusieurs examens.

questions.stem: What does "quelquefois" mean?
questions.explanation: Quelquefois (one word) means sometimes, like parfois. A few times is quelques fois (two words); somewhere is quelque part; someone is quelqu'un.

questions.stem: Read: "À la fac, Nina a cours tous les matins sauf le mercredi. L'après-midi, elle travaille à temps partiel dans une librairie. Elle a plusieurs examens en janvier." When does Nina have classes?
questions.explanation: Tous les matins sauf le mercredi = every morning except (on) Wednesday. In the afternoons she works part-time in a bookshop.

questions.stem: How long is a licence (bachelor's degree) at a French university?
questions.explanation: La licence is bac + 3. Le master adds two more years (bac + 5); the doctorat is bac + 8; a BTS is bac + 2.

questions.stem: What does "passer un examen" mean?
questions.explanation: A false friend: passer un examen = to take (sit) an exam. To pass it is réussir un examen; to fail it is rater (informal) or échouer à.

questions.stem: What does "Certains étudiants travaillent le soir" mean?
choices: Each student works in the evening.
Some students work in the evening.
Students certainly work in the evening.
All the students work in the evening.
questions.explanation: Certains, certaines before a plural noun = some (part of a group). All would be tous les; each, chaque. Certainly is certainement.

questions.stem: Complete (a man speaking): "Je me suis ___ à un cours de français." (I signed up)
questions.explanation: S'inscrire is conjugated like écrire: the participle is inscrit, and with être it agrees (a woman writes inscrite). Inscrivé doesn't exist.

questions.stem: Where does a French lycée pupil usually eat at lunchtime?
questions.explanation: La cantine is the school canteen. Le resto U is the university canteen; le bac is an exam and l'emploi du temps the timetable.

questions.stem: Write the missing word: "___ le monde est là." (Everyone is here.)
questions.explanation: Tout le monde = everyone, with a singular verb.

questions.stem: Write the pronoun that means "each one" (feminine): "Les filles ? ___ a son livre."
questions.explanation: Alone and feminine: chacune, with a singular verb (a).

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "All my friends are at university."
questions.explanation: Tous goes before the possessive and the noun: Tous mes amis font des études.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
choices: exam at the end of the lycée
questions.explanation: Le bac ends the lycée; la licence is three years at university; le master two more years; la fac is informal for university; les devoirs is homework. The timetable is l'emploi du temps and the canteen la cantine.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Chacun a son emploi du temps.
Il a appris quelque chose de nouveau.
questions.explanation: Chaque jour (chaque + singular), j'ai plusieurs questions (plusieurs, no article), chacun a son emploi du temps (chacun alone, singular verb) and il a appris quelque chose de nouveau (de + masculine adjective) are correct. Tout le monde takes a singular verb: tout le monde est là.

questions.stem: Name the numbered subjects and activities in Léo's timetable.

image.alt: Léo's weekly timetable from lundi to vendredi with icons instead of subject names: a plus and equals sign, a speech bubble saying Hello!, a plate with a fork and knife, a globe, a football and a musical note. Six cells are numbered: five on Monday and the second lesson on Tuesday.

questions.explanation: Monday starts with les maths (plus and equals), then l'anglais (Hello!), la cantine at lunchtime (a plate), la géographie (a globe) and le sport (a football); on Tuesday from 10 h it's la musique (a note). L'histoire and les devoirs aren't shown.

questions.stem: Paul says: « Je suis fatigué. » Complete: "Paul dit ___ fatigué."
questions.explanation: Reported speech needs que (never dropped), and je becomes il because you are talking about Paul: Paul dit qu'il est fatigué. S'il is for questions (if he is).

questions.stem: Report the question « Tu viens ce soir ? »: "Elle demande ___ tu viens ce soir."
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with si (if, whether): elle demande si tu viens. Est-ce que disappears in an indirect question.

questions.stem: Report « Qu'est-ce que vous voulez ? »: "Dites-moi ___ vous voulez."
questions.explanation: Qu'est-ce que becomes ce que in an indirect question: dites-moi ce que vous voulez. Ce qui is for the subject (ce qui se passe); vous is the subject here.

questions.stem: Report « Qu'est-ce qui se passe ? »: "Je ne sais pas ___ se passe."
questions.explanation: Qu'est-ce qui becomes ce qui: je ne sais pas ce qui se passe. There is no other subject after the gap, so it's ce qui, not ce que.

questions.stem: Which indirect question is correct?
choices: Je voudrais savoir où vous habitez.
Je voudrais savoir où que vous habitez.
Je voudrais savoir où est-ce que vous habitez.
questions.explanation: In an indirect question there is no est-ce que and no inversion of a subject pronoun: où vous habitez.

questions.stem: Which is spelled correctly?
choices: Je me demande se il vient.
Je me demande si il vient.
questions.explanation: Si elides only before il and ils: s'il, s'ils. Before elle and on it stays si: si elle vient.

questions.stem: The officer says: « Patientez ! » Complete: "L'agent nous dit ___."
questions.explanation: An order is reported with dire de + infinitive: il nous dit de patienter (he tells us to wait).

questions.stem: Marc says: « Mon compte est vide. » How do you report it?
choices: Marc dit si son compte est vide.
Marc dit son compte est vide.
Marc dit que mon compte est vide.
Marc dit que son compte est vide.
questions.explanation: The account is Marc's, so mon becomes son: Marc dit que son compte est vide. Que is never dropped, and si is only for yes/no questions.

questions.stem: Read: "Bonjour, je voudrais savoir si je peux retirer de l'argent au guichet. — Oui, mais il faut une pièce d'identité." What does the customer want to know?
choices: whether he can withdraw money at the counter
whether he needs a new card
how much money is in his account
questions.explanation: Je voudrais savoir si … = I'd like to know whether …; retirer de l'argent au guichet = withdraw money at the counter. The answer: yes, with ID (une pièce d'identité).

questions.stem: A letter says: "Le délai est de dix jours." What does it mean?
choices: You have ten days to do it.
The office is closed for ten days.
You will wait ten days in the queue.
questions.explanation: Le délai is the time allowed (a deadline). A delay, something late, is le retard.

questions.stem: Where do you take out cash with your bank card?
questions.explanation: Le distributeur (de billets) is the cash machine. Le virement is a transfer, la file d'attente a queue, le délai the time allowed.

questions.stem: Complete politely: "Pourriez-vous me dire ___ ?" (where reception is)
choices: où est-ce que se trouve l'accueil
questions.explanation: Inside the polite question the indirect part has no inversion and no est-ce que: où se trouve l'accueil (a noun subject may follow a short verb). The question mark belongs to the whole sentence.

questions.stem: What does "Préviens-moi si tu es en retard" mean?
choices: Let me know if you're late.
Call me back if you're late.
Wait for me if you're late.
questions.explanation: Prévenir = to let know, to warn (not usually to prevent). Préviens-moi = let me know. Call me back is rappelle-moi.

questions.stem: In which sentence is the question mark correct?
choices: Elle demande ce que tu veux ?
Pourriez-vous me dire si la banque est ouverte ?
Je me demande où il habite ?
questions.explanation: An indirect question has no question mark unless the whole sentence is a question. Pourriez-vous me dire … ? is itself a question; the others are statements about what someone asks or wonders.

questions.stem: Report « Est-ce que tu as ton code ? »: "Il me demande ___ j'ai mon code."
questions.explanation: Yes/no question → si: il me demande si j'ai mon code.

questions.stem: Report « Qu'est-ce que tu veux ? »: "Je ne sais pas ___ tu veux." (two words)
questions.explanation: Qu'est-ce que → ce que: je ne sais pas ce que tu veux.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "I wonder if the bank is open."
questions.explanation: Se demander + si + statement order: Je me demande si la banque est ouverte.

questions.stem: Match each direct question to the word that starts its indirect version.
questions.explanation: Yes/no → si; qu'est-ce que → ce que; qu'est-ce qui → ce qui; question words like où stay. Que and qu'est-ce que never start an indirect question.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
