choices: Je voudrais savoir où tu habites.
Elle demande où est-ce que tu habites.
questions.explanation: Il dit qu'il est malade (que kept), elle demande si tu viens (si for yes/no) and je voudrais savoir où tu habites (no inversion) are correct. Il dit il est malade drops que; où est-ce que keeps est-ce que, which an indirect question drops.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in the bank.

image.alt: Inside a bank, with five numbered things: a cash machine in the wall, a bank card in front of it, a desk with a person behind it under an information sign, a counter with a glass window and a clerk, and three customers waiting in line.

questions.explanation: The machine in the wall is le distributeur; the card in front of it is la carte bancaire; the desk under the information sign is l'accueil; the counter with a glass window is le guichet; the customers waiting in line are la file d'attente. A transfer (le virement) and a parcel (le colis) aren't shown.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ le magasin était fermé, je suis rentré."
questions.explanation: Comme gives the cause at the start of the sentence. Car can't put the cause first; donc introduces a consequence; grâce à needs a noun, not a sentence.

questions.stem: Complete: "Le train est en retard ___ la neige."
questions.explanation: Before a noun (la neige) use à cause de or grâce à; for a bad result, à cause de. Parce que and car need a full sentence.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ ton aide, j'ai trouvé un emploi."
questions.explanation: A good result + a noun: grâce à (thanks to). À cause de is for bad results; car and comme need a sentence with a verb.

questions.stem: Complete: "J'appelle ___ réserver une table."
questions.explanation: Purpose with the same person: pour + infinitive (j'appelle pour réserver). Pour que needs a different subject and the subjunctive; parce que and car give a cause and need a conjugated verb.

questions.stem: Which is correct?
questions.explanation: De + le contracts to du: à cause du retard. Des would need a plural noun (des retards).

questions.stem: "Pourquoi tu appelles ?" Which answer is correct?
choices: Comme mon colis n'est pas arrivé.
Car mon colis n'est pas arrivé.
Grâce à mon colis n'est pas arrivé.
Parce que mon colis n'est pas arrivé.
questions.explanation: The answer to Pourquoi ? starts with parce que. Car can't stand alone as an answer, comme must be followed by the main sentence, and grâce à needs a noun.

questions.stem: Complete: "Vérifiez le colis avant ___."
questions.explanation: Avant de + infinitive: avant de signer (before signing). French uses the infinitive after a preposition where English uses -ing.

questions.stem: What does "en effet" mean in "Je suis mécontent. En effet, j'attends depuis trois semaines."?
questions.explanation: En effet confirms or explains what was just said: indeed, in fact. It doesn't mean in effect.

questions.stem: Read: "Madame, Monsieur, je vous écris car j'ai reçu un pull rouge au lieu du pull bleu que j'ai commandé. Je souhaite l'échanger. Cordialement, Léa." What is the problem?
questions.explanation: Au lieu du pull bleu = instead of the blue jumper: she ordered blue and got red, and wants to exchange it.

questions.stem: What does "Je me suis trompé de numéro" mean?
questions.explanation: Se tromper de + noun = to get the wrong …: se tromper de numéro, d'adresse.

questions.stem: Complete: "Le produit était cassé, ___ je l'ai renvoyé."
questions.explanation: The second half is a consequence: c'est pourquoi (that's why). Parce que and car would make sending it back the cause of the breakage; grâce à needs a noun.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il est parti sans ___." (He left without paying.)
questions.explanation: Sans + infinitive: sans payer. No de after sans, and never the -ant form here.

questions.stem: Which word means "a refund"?
questions.explanation: Le remboursement is the refund (verb rembourser). La réclamation is a complaint, la livraison the delivery and la commande the order.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ce n'est pas ma ___ !" (It's not my fault!)
questions.explanation: La faute = fault, blame: ce n'est pas ma faute. Une erreur is a mistake (and would need mon before a vowel: mon erreur).

questions.stem: Write the missing word (thanks to): "___ au service client, le problème est réglé."
questions.explanation: Grâce à + a good cause, contracted with le: grâce au service client.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je vous écris ___ demander un remboursement." (to ask, in order to ask)
questions.explanation: Purpose: pour + infinitive: je vous écris pour demander un remboursement.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "As the shop was closed, I went home."
questions.explanation: Comme gives the cause first, then the main sentence: Comme le magasin était fermé, je suis rentré.

questions.stem: Match each linking word to what it expresses.
questions.explanation: Parce que and grâce à give a cause; donc and c'est pourquoi a consequence; pour + infinitive a purpose. None of them expresses a contrast (that's mais, pourtant).

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Comme il pleuvait, on est restés.
Car il pleuvait, on est restés.
Je suis venu pour te voir.
questions.explanation: Comme first with the cause, pour + infinitive (pour te voir) and avant de + infinitive are correct. Car can't put the cause first (use comme); pour can't be followed by a conjugated verb (je t'appelle pour réserver).

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this complaint e-mail.

image.alt: A complaint e-mail with six numbers in the margin: next to the subject line Objet : Commande n° 48213 – lampe cassée; next to Madame, Monsieur,; next to the paragraph about the broken lamp and the damaged box; next to the paragraph asking for a replacement or a refund; next to Cordialement; and next to an attachment called lampe.jpg.

questions.explanation: 1 is l'objet (the subject line); 2 la formule d'appel (Madame, Monsieur,); 3 le problème (a broken lamp in a damaged box); 4 la demande (replace it or refund it); 5 la formule de politesse (Cordialement); 6 la pièce jointe (the photo). There is no phone number or date of birth.

questions.stem: In the experience section of a French CV, jobs are usually listed…
questions.explanation: The classic French CV uses reverse chronological order (antichronologique): you start with your current or last job and go back in time.

questions.stem: According to service-public.fr (checked November 2026), a photo on a CV is…
questions.explanation: Service-public.fr lists an ID photo among the things a CV may contain. There's no rule that requires or forbids it.

questions.stem: Under the Code du travail (articles L1221-6 to L1221-9), an employer may ask a candidate for information that…
choices: has a direct link with the job
questions.explanation: Questions must have a direct link with the job, to judge whether you can do it. You never have to reveal your health, a pregnancy, or your political, union or religious views.

questions.stem: What does "Actuellement étudiant en tourisme, …" mean at the start of a letter?
choices: I used to be a tourism student, …
I will soon be a tourism student, …
I am currently a tourism student, …
questions.explanation: Actuellement is a false friend: it means currently, now. Actually is en fait.

questions.stem: Which is the usual CV line for "J'ai géré les réservations"?
choices: J'ai géré les réservations, c'était bien.
questions.explanation: CV lines are short, usually built on a noun: gérer → la gestion. Full sentences with je are for the cover letter.

questions.stem: In the "vous, moi, nous" plan of a cover letter, what goes in the "nous" paragraph?
choices: what you will bring and a request for an interview
questions.explanation: Vous = the company, moi = you, nous = working together: what you will bring, and the request to meet. The address and date go above the letter.

questions.stem: Which closing suits a cover letter?
choices: Dans l'attente de votre réponse, je vous prie d'agréer, Madame, Monsieur, l'expression de mes salutations distinguées.
questions.explanation: A cover letter ends with the full formal formula, often introduced by dans l'attente de votre réponse. The others are for friends and family.

questions.stem: France Travail advises writing what you can bring in the present or the futur rather than the conditionnel. Which sentence follows that advice?
choices: Je pourrais peut-être vous aider un peu.
Mon expérience pourrait peut-être être utile.
Mon expérience serait éventuellement un atout.
Mon expérience sera un atout pour votre équipe.
questions.explanation: Sera (futur) sounds confident. The conditionnel with peut-être sounds unsure. Keep the conditionnel for polite requests: je serais heureux de vous rencontrer.

questions.stem: On a CV, what does "anglais courant" mean?
questions.explanation: Courant (for a language) = fluent. Basics are notions; mother tongue is langue maternelle.

questions.stem: Write the French for "contact details" with its article: ___
questions.explanation: Les coordonnées (feminine plural): name, address, phone, e-mail.

questions.stem: Put the parts of the cover letter in order.
choices: Mon expérience sera un atout … (working together)
questions.explanation: Subject line, opening, then vous (the company), moi (you), nous (working together), and the closing formula.

questions.stem: Match each CV heading to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Coordonnées = contact details; formation = education; compétences = skills; centres d'intérêt = interests; langue maternelle = mother tongue. A cover letter is la lettre de motivation; a recruiter is le recruteur.

questions.stem: Which sentences suit a formal application? Select all that apply.
choices: Je me permets de vous adresser ma candidature.
Je serais heureux de vous rencontrer lors d'un entretien.
questions.explanation: Je me permets de vous adresser ma candidature, vous trouverez ci-joint mon CV and je serais heureux de vous rencontrer lors d'un entretien are set formal phrases. Je veux le job is too blunt and informal; mon CV est attaché is an anglicism (say ci-joint or en pièce jointe).

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this CV.

image.alt: A one-page CV for Daniel WALSH with the section headings blanked out and numbered: 1 next to the name, address and e-mail at the top; then five blank headings above two jobs with dates, a master's course and a degree in tourism, a list of languages, software and teamwork, and football, voluntary work and travel.

questions.explanation: 1 is the top block with the name, address and e-mail: les coordonnées. Then l'expérience professionnelle (jobs with dates), la formation (the master's course and the degree), les langues, les compétences (software, teamwork) and les centres d'intérêt (football, voluntary work, travel). There is no cover letter or signature on a CV.

questions.stem: Where do you ask for a birth certificate (un acte de naissance)?
questions.explanation: Births, marriages and deaths are registered by the état civil of the mairie, which issues the certificates.

questions.stem: Since 6 November 2017, how do you apply for a driving licence in France?
choices: online, through the ANTS (now France Titres)
questions.explanation: Driving licences and vehicle registration papers moved fully online on 6 November 2017. The ANTS was renamed France Titres in 2024; its website is still ants.gouv.fr.

questions.stem: What is la carte Vitale?
choices: the card that shows you are covered by the national health insurance
questions.explanation: You show the carte Vitale at the doctor's or the pharmacy so the claim goes straight to the Assurance maladie and you are paid back faster.

questions.stem: What is la mutuelle?
questions.explanation: La mutuelle (la complémentaire santé) pays part of what the Assurance maladie doesn't. The State system is the Sécurité sociale / Assurance maladie.

questions.stem: Since 1 January 2016, what must private-sector employers in France do about complementary health insurance?
choices: nothing: it's up to each employee
offer it to employees and pay at least half
pay the whole cost for every employee
questions.explanation: Since 1 January 2016 every private-sector employer must offer a complémentaire santé and pay at least 50 % of its cost (DREES; service-public.fr). They may pay more.

questions.stem: A student wants help paying her rent. Which office does she contact?
questions.explanation: The CAF (Caisse d'allocations familiales) pays housing aid as well as family benefits. It decides on each person's situation.

questions.stem: What does a RIB show?
choices: your bank card number and code
your bank details, such as the IBAN and BIC
questions.explanation: Le relevé d'identité bancaire gives the account holder, the bank, the account numbers, the IBAN and the BIC. Never give your card number or code.

questions.stem: Read the letter. What is the problem with Grace's file?

image.alt: An invented letter from the Service Éducation of the Mairie de Saint-Aubin-les-Prés to Madame Grace Okafor, dated 2 November 2026, about enrolling her son Samuel in primary school. It says the file is incomplete and asks her to send, within fifteen days from the date of the letter, a proof of address less than three months old and the child's birth certificate or the livret de famille. For information she can contact the service from Monday to Friday, 9 h to 12 h.

choices: Samuel is too young for the school.
questions.explanation: Votre dossier est incomplet: she must send a proof of address and Samuel's birth certificate (or the livret de famille).

questions.stem: The letter is dated 2 November 2026 and gives "un délai de quinze jours à compter de la date de ce courrier". By about when must Grace send the documents?

image.alt: An invented letter from the Service Éducation of the Mairie de Saint-Aubin-les-Prés to Madame Grace Okafor, dated 2 November 2026, about enrolling her son Samuel in primary school. It says the file is incomplete and asks her to send, within fifteen days from the date of the letter, a proof of address less than three months old and the child's birth certificate or the livret de famille. For information she can contact the service from Monday to Friday, 9 h to 12 h.

questions.explanation: Fifteen days from 2 November is 17 November 2026 (a Tuesday). If in doubt, send the papers early.

questions.stem: What does "Nous vous prions de bien vouloir nous adresser …" mean in an official letter?
choices: We would like to visit you …
questions.explanation: Prier de here means to ask politely: nous vous prions de bien vouloir … = please kindly … . Adresser = to send.

questions.stem: Write the acronym for the Caisse d'allocations familiales: la ___
questions.explanation: La CAF, said as a word: "kaf". It is also written Caf.

questions.stem: Match each acronym to what it is.
choices: agency for ID cards, passports and licences
questions.explanation: CAF = family benefits; CPAM = the local health insurance office; RIB = your bank details; ANTS (now France Titres) = ID cards, passports and driving licences. Taxes are les impôts; the town hall is la mairie.

questions.stem: Which of these are done at a mairie (one with the right equipment, for ID cards)? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The mairie handles l'état civil (birth certificates, weddings) and, in equipped town halls, ID-card and passport applications. Driving licences are online (ANTS / France Titres), and the carte Vitale comes from the Assurance maladie.

questions.stem: Put the steps for a new identity card in order.
choices: Fill in the pre-application on the ANTS website
Hand in your documents and give your fingerprints at an equipped mairie (usually by appointment)
Receive a text message saying the card is ready
Collect the card yourself at the same mairie
questions.explanation: The online pre-application (optional, but it saves time) comes before your visit; at an equipped mairie your documents are checked and your fingerprints taken; you get a text message when the card is ready, and you collect it in person at the mairie where you applied.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je pense ___ il a raison."
questions.explanation: "Penser que" introduces an opinion, and "que" becomes "qu'" before a vowel: "Je pense qu'il a raison." "Que il" is never written. "Penser de" is only for asking someone's opinion of something, and "penser à" means to think about.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I don't agree with you"?
choices: Je ne suis pas d'accord avec toi.
Je n'ai pas d'accord avec toi.
Je ne suis pas d'accord à toi.
Je ne suis pas raison avec toi.
questions.explanation: "To agree" is "être d'accord", with "avec" + the person: "Je ne suis pas d'accord avec toi." French never uses avoir with d'accord, and "raison" goes with avoir (avoir raison = to be right).

questions.stem: Your friend asks: "Qu'est-ce que tu penses de ce film ?" Which answer is correct French?
choices: Je pense de ce film est long.
Je pense que de ce film.
Je le trouve un peu long.
questions.explanation: The question uses "penser de", but the answer doesn't: "Je le trouve un peu long" (or "Je pense qu'il est un peu long"). "Je pense à ce film" means the film is on your mind; it isn't an opinion.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu ___ raison, c'est une très bonne série."
questions.explanation: "To be right" is "avoir raison" in French: "tu as raison". English uses "be", which leads to the mistake "tu es raison". The opposite is "avoir tort".

questions.stem: Complete: "Les acteurs sont excellents. ___, l'histoire est un peu bête."
questions.explanation: "Par contre" (on the other hand) sets a second side against the first: good actors, a silly story. "Au contraire" would say the first statement is wrong, "donc" (so) gives a result that doesn't follow, and "selon" needs a noun after it (selon moi).

questions.stem: "Il a beaucoup révisé. Pourtant, il a raté l'examen." What does "pourtant" show?
choices: The second fact is the result of the first.
The second fact happened before the first.
The speaker agrees with the first fact.
The second fact is surprising after the first.
questions.explanation: "Pourtant" (yet, however) marks a surprise: after a lot of revision you expect him to pass, yet he failed. A result would be "donc" or "alors".

questions.stem: Which sentence means "It was raining, but we went out all the same"?
choices: Il pleuvait, mais on est quand même sortis.
Il pleuvait, mais quand même on sortis est.
Il pleuvait, quand même mais on est sortis.
Quand même il pleuvait, on est sortis.
questions.explanation: "Quand même" usually goes after the conjugated verb (here between "est" and the participle) or at the end: "on est quand même sortis" or "on est sortis quand même". The other orders aren't French.

questions.stem: What does "Je pense à mes vacances." mean?
choices: I think my holiday is good.
I have an opinion about my holiday.
I think that I'm on holiday.
questions.explanation: "Penser à" means to think about, to have something on your mind. An opinion uses "penser que" (Je pense que mes vacances seront super) or "trouver" (Je trouve mes vacances trop courtes).

questions.stem: Look at the TV guide. What is on at 21 h 40?

image.alt: An evening TV guide for Thursday on an invented channel: 19 h 00 les informations, 20 h 30 le documentaire, 21 h 35 la publicité, 21 h 40 la série Rue des Lilas, 22 h 30 l'émission de cuisine.

questions.explanation: At 21 h 40 the guide shows "Rue des Lilas", saison 2, épisode 5: "la série". The documentary is at 20 h 30, the news ("les informations") at 19 h 00 and the cooking programme ("l'émission de cuisine") at 22 h 30.

questions.stem: Which reply means "I don't think so"?
questions.explanation: "Je pense que non" (or "Je ne pense pas", "Je crois que non") means "I don't think so". "Que pas" isn't French, and "ne … que" means "only".

questions.stem: What does "Tu as regardé les informations hier soir ?" mean?
choices: Did you watch the adverts last night?
Did you read the newspaper last night?
Did you watch the news last night?
Did you watch the documentary last night?
questions.explanation: "Les informations" (les infos) is the news on TV or radio, always plural in this sense. Adverts are "la publicité", the newspaper is "le journal".

questions.stem: Complete the reply: "Ce documentaire était ennuyeux, non ? — ___ Il était passionnant !"
questions.explanation: "Au contraire" (on the contrary) rejects what the other person said and says the opposite: boring → gripping. "Tu as raison" and "Je suis d'accord" would agree that it was boring, which the next sentence contradicts; "par contre" adds a second side, it doesn't contradict.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Je trouve que ce magazine intéressant.
Je trouve de ce magazine intéressant.
Je trouve ce magazine est intéressant.
questions.explanation: "Trouver" can take a noun + an adjective directly: "Je trouve ce magazine intéressant." With "que" you need a full sentence with a verb: "Je trouve que ce magazine est intéressant."

questions.stem: Write the missing words: "À mon ___, cette émission est nulle. — Tu as ___ ! Elle est géniale !"
questions.explanation: "À mon avis" = in my opinion. The second speaker disagrees (elle est géniale), so: "Tu as tort" (you're wrong). "Tu as raison" would mean "you're right", which doesn't fit.

questions.stem: Put the words in order to ask "What do you think (of it)?"
questions.explanation: "Qu'est-ce que tu en penses ?" The pronoun "en" (of it) goes straight before the verb, as in lesson 7.

questions.stem: Match each contrast word with its meaning.
questions.explanation: "Mais" is the everyday "but"; "pourtant" marks a surprising contrast; "par contre" compares two sides; "quand même" means "all the same, even so". "On the contrary" is "au contraire".

questions.stem: Which sentences give an opinion in correct French? Select all that apply.
choices: Je trouve que ce film est trop long.
À mon avis, ce film est trop long.
Je pense ce film est trop long.
Selon moi, que ce film est trop long.
D'après moi, ce film est trop long.
questions.explanation: After "je trouve" and "je pense" you need "que" (never left out): "Je pense que ce film …". The openers "à mon avis", "selon moi" and "d'après moi" take no "que": the sentence simply follows.

questions.stem: Name the type of each numbered programme in this TV guide.

image.alt: An evening TV guide without the programme types. Numbered: the 19 h 00 slot with a news desk and the title Le journal du soir, the 20 h 30 slot with a fish and the title Les secrets des océans, a short 21 h 35 slot with a megaphone, and the 21 h 40 slot marked S2 · É5 with the title Rue des Lilas.

questions.explanation: 1 is the evening news ("les informations", with "Le journal du soir"), 2 a documentary about the oceans, 3 the short advert break ("la publicité", "la pub"), and 4 a series (season 2, episode 5).

questions.stem: Complete the suggestion: "Si on ___ au cinéma ce soir ?"
questions.explanation: The pattern for "how about…?" is "si on" + imparfait: "Si on allait au cinéma ce soir ?" The conditionnel never follows "si" ("si on irait" is wrong), and the passé composé would talk about the past.

questions.stem: What does "Si on allait au cinéma ?" mean?
choices: How about going to the cinema?
We used to go to the cinema.
We will go to the cinema.
questions.explanation: "Si on" + imparfait, said as a question, is a set pattern for suggestions: "How about…? Shall we…?" Even though "allait" is imparfait, it isn't about the past.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ça te dit ___ aller à l'exposition ?"
questions.explanation: "Ça te dit de" + infinitive = "Do you fancy …?". "De" becomes "d'" before a vowel: "Ça te dit d'aller …?"

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu as envie ___ sortir ce soir ?"
questions.explanation: "Avoir envie de" + infinitive = to feel like doing: "Tu as envie de sortir ?" "D'" is only for a following vowel (envie d'aller).

questions.stem: Complete the exclamation: "___ bonne idée !"
questions.explanation: "Quel" agrees with the noun, and "idée" is feminine: "Quelle bonne idée !" "Que" and "comme" are followed by a whole sentence (Que c'est beau !), not a noun.

questions.stem: Which exclamation is correct?
questions.explanation: Quel + noun takes no article: not "quelle une" (English "what a…!" misleads). "Que" and "comme" need a sentence: "Que la soirée était belle !", "Comme c'était beau !"

questions.stem: A friend asks: "Ça te dit, un concert samedi ?" Which reply refuses politely, with a reason?
choices: Désolé, je ne peux pas, je dois travailler. Une autre fois ?
questions.explanation: A polite refusal says sorry, gives a reason and often offers another time. A bare "Non." sounds cold; "Volontiers !" and "Pourquoi pas ?" accept.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je suis ravi ___ venir à ta fête."
questions.explanation: A feeling with être + adjective + de + infinitive: "Je suis ravi de venir", like "content de te voir", "désolé de ne pas pouvoir venir".

questions.stem: What does "On se retrouve devant le théâtre à 20 heures ?" mean?
choices: Did we meet in front of the theatre at 8 pm?
Shall we find the theatre at 8 pm?
Shall we meet in front of the theatre at 8 am?
Shall we meet in front of the theatre at 8 pm?
questions.explanation: "Se retrouver" is to meet up by arrangement, and the present with a question is a suggestion: "Shall we meet …?". 20 heures is 8 pm.

questions.stem: Paul says: "Je m'ennuie à la maison." What does he mean?
questions.explanation: "Je m'ennuie" (s'ennuyer) = I'm bored. "Ennuyeux" describes what bores you: "Je suis ennuyeux" would mean "I am a boring person". Having fun is "je m'amuse".

questions.stem: Look at the poster. Which showing can you no longer book?

image.alt: A poster for an invented play, Le Voyage de Lou, at the Théâtre des Tilleuls in Rouvigny. Séances: vendredi 20 h 30, stamped COMPLET; samedi 15 h et 20 h 30; dimanche 16 h. Tarifs: 18 €, tarif réduit 12 €, gratuit pour les moins de 12 ans.

questions.explanation: Friday's showing is stamped "COMPLET": sold out. The other showings (séances) have no stamp. The poster also advises booking: "Réservation conseillée".

questions.stem: Look at the poster again. How much does a 10-year-old pay?

image.alt: A poster for an invented play, Le Voyage de Lou. Tarifs: 18 €, tarif réduit 12 €, gratuit pour les moins de 12 ans.

questions.explanation: The poster says "gratuit pour les moins de 12 ans": free for under-12s. 12 € is the reduced price ("tarif réduit") and 18 € the full price.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu viens au restaurant avec nous ? — ___ : c'est à quelle heure ?"
questions.explanation: "Ça dépend" (it depends) leaves the answer open until the speaker knows more: here, the time. The other replies don't fit an invitation.

questions.stem: Write the one-word reply that means "gladly": "Tu viens avec nous au théâtre ? — Oui, ___ !"
questions.explanation: "Volontiers" = gladly, with pleasure. The final -rs is silent: [vɔlɔ̃tje].

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "What if we went to the theatre?"
questions.explanation: "Et si on allait au théâtre ?" The suggestion pattern is (et) si + on + imparfait, then the rest.

questions.stem: Choose the right form of quel for each exclamation.
questions.explanation: Quel agrees with the noun: le dommage (masculine) → quel; l'ambiance (feminine) → quelle; les costumes (masculine plural) → quels; les photos (feminine plural) → quelles. All four sound the same.

questions.stem: Which replies accept an invitation? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Volontiers", "Avec plaisir" and "Quelle bonne idée !" say yes. "Désolé, je ne peux pas" refuses, and "Une autre fois, peut-être ?" puts it off to another day.

questions.stem: Where are you going? Name each numbered place.

image.alt: A street at night with five buildings and no signs. Numbered: a building with two theatre masks, a large building with columns and music notes, a gallery with pictures in the window and a banner, a building with a film reel, and a building with a disco ball and music notes.

questions.explanation: The masks stand for the theatre, the columns and music for the opera, the pictures for an exhibition, the film reel for the cinema and the disco ball for a nightclub. "La séance" (a showing) and "le public" (the audience) aren't places.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je te montrerai les photos quand on se ___ en juin."
questions.explanation: After "quand" about the future, French uses the futur (lesson 13): "quand on se verra" (when we see each other). English uses the present ("when we see"), which leads to the mistake "quand on se voit".

questions.stem: Complete: "On voulait aller à la plage, mais il a plu. ___, on est restés à la maison."
questions.explanation: "Finalement" = in the end, after a change of plan. "Enfin" means "at last" or comes last in a list, so it doesn't fit a change of plan. "Lorsque" (when) needs a clause after it, and "malgré" needs a noun.

questions.stem: What does "Au bout d'une heure, le bus est arrivé." mean?
choices: For an hour, the bus arrived.
An hour ago, the bus arrived.
In an hour's time, the bus will arrive.
After an hour, the bus arrived.
questions.explanation: "Au bout de" + a length of time = after that time has passed. "An hour ago" is "il y a une heure"; "in an hour" is "dans une heure".

questions.stem: Complete: "___ la pluie, la fête était super."
questions.explanation: "Malgré" (despite) + a noun: "malgré la pluie". "Pourtant" and "quand même" are adverbs and can't take a noun like this; "lorsque" (when) needs a verb.

questions.stem: Complete: "Excuse-moi ___ répondre si tard."
questions.explanation: "Excuse-moi de" + infinitive (sorry for doing), "excuse-moi pour" + noun (excuse-moi pour le retard). "Pour répondre" would mean "in order to reply".

questions.stem: Your friend has to work all weekend on a long, difficult project. What do you write?
questions.explanation: "Bon courage !" is for something long or hard: hang in there. "Félicitations" is for a success, "Meilleurs vœux" for New Year or a special day, and "Bon appétit" before a meal.

questions.stem: Which closing suits an e-mail to your bank?
questions.explanation: "Cordialement" is the standard formal closing with vous. "Je t'embrasse" and "Bisous" are for family and close friends, "Amicalement" for friends and people you know well.

questions.stem: Who would you end a message to with "Je t'embrasse"?
questions.explanation: "Je t'embrasse" (lots of love) is a warm closing for family and close friends, with tu. It is not for colleagues, staff or teachers.

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT correct French?
choices: Lorsqu'il est arrivé, on a mangé.
Lorsque je suis rentré, il dormait.
questions.explanation: "Lorsque" means "when" only in a time clause; it never asks a question. "When are you arriving?" is "Quand est-ce que tu arrives ?". Note the elision "lorsqu'il".

questions.stem: Read Lisa's reply. "Salut Nora, merci beaucoup pour ton invitation ! Je suis vraiment désolée, mais je ne pourrai pas venir à ta fête samedi : je pars en Espagne avec mes parents pour l'anniversaire de ma grand-mère. On pourrait se retrouver la semaine prochaine ? Bises, Lisa" Why can't Lisa go to the party?
choices: She has to work on Saturday.
She's going to Spain for her grandmother's birthday.
questions.explanation: "Je pars en Espagne avec mes parents pour l'anniversaire de ma grand-mère": she is going to Spain for her grandmother's birthday. She also thanks Nora, says she is sorry and suggests another time.

questions.stem: Your friend tells you she has passed her driving test. What do you say?
questions.explanation: "Félicitations !" (or "Bravo !") congratulates someone on a success. "Bon courage" is for something still to come, "je regrette" is "I'm sorry" and "excuse-moi" is an apology.

questions.stem: What does "Je regrette de ne pas pouvoir venir." mean?
choices: I came, and I am sorry.
questions.explanation: "Regretter de" + infinitive = to be sorry to / that. The negative "ne pas" sits before the infinitive "pouvoir": I'm sorry not to be able to come.

questions.stem: Write the connector that means "in the meantime": "Le train a du retard. ___, on prend un café ?"
questions.explanation: "En attendant" (literally "while waiting") = in the meantime, meanwhile.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "Sorry for replying so late."
questions.explanation: "Excuse-moi de répondre si tard." Excuse-moi + de + infinitive; "si tard" (so late) comes after the verb.

questions.stem: What do you write in each situation?
left: Your friend has passed an exam.
Your friend has a job interview tomorrow.
It's the first week of January.
questions.explanation: "Joyeux anniversaire" for a birthday (A1), "Félicitations" for a success, "Bonne chance" before something where luck helps, "Meilleurs vœux" for the New Year.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct French? Select all that apply.
choices: Malgré la pluie, on est sortis.
Malgré il pleuvait, on est sortis.
Il pleuvait, mais on est quand même sortis.
Il pleuvait. Pourtant, on est sortis.
questions.explanation: "Malgré" takes a noun, not a clause (malgré la pluie, not malgré il pleuvait). "Quand même" and "pourtant" express the same contrast with a full sentence. "Merci pour" takes a noun; for a verb, say "Merci d'être venu(e) !".

questions.stem: Name each numbered part of Marc's message.

image.alt: Marc's e-mail to Julie without its tags. Numbered: Chère Julie; the paragraph telling what happened at the wedding; C'était une journée inoubliable, j'étais très ému; Je te montrerai les photos quand on se verra en juin; Je t'embrasse, Marc.

questions.explanation: 1 opens the message (Chère Julie), 2 tells the event in the passé composé with the scene in the imparfait, 3 gives feelings (c'était inoubliable, j'étais ému), 4 the plan in the futur (je te montrerai), and 5 closes it (Je t'embrasse, Marc).

questions.stem: In the DELF A2, how long do the three written parts (listening, reading, writing) take together?
questions.explanation: Listening 25 min + reading 30 min + writing 45 min = 100 minutes, 1 h 40, taken in one sitting. 1 h 20 is the DELF A1; 45 minutes is the writing part alone.

questions.stem: Léo scores 60/100 in the DELF A2, but only 4/25 in reading. What is his result?
choices: He fails: every part needs at least 5/25.
He passes: he has more than 50/100.
He passes, but must take reading again.
questions.explanation: You need 50/100 in total AND at least 5/25 in each of the four parts. Léo's 4/25 in reading is below the minimum, so he fails despite his total.

questions.stem: How does the DELF A2 speaking test run?
choices: 25 minutes, in the same sitting as the written parts
45 minutes, in a group of candidates
6 to 8 minutes with the examiner, after 10 minutes of preparation
questions.explanation: The speaking test is separate from the written papers: 10 minutes of preparation, then 6 to 8 minutes with the examiner, in three parts.

questions.stem: What are the two texts of the DELF A2 writing paper?
choices: an account of an event or experience, and a message with a purpose
a summary of an article and a formal complaint
two essays for and against an idea
questions.explanation: At A2 you write about an event or personal experience, and a message that invites, thanks, apologises, asks, informs or congratulates (often a reply). A form and a postcard are the DELF A1 tasks.

questions.stem: In the newer format, what kind of questions do the DELF A2 listening and reading parts use?
choices: open questions answered in full sentences
closed questions, mostly multiple choice with three options
true/false questions that you must justify
a written summary of each document
questions.explanation: Since the revision, the comprehension parts use only closed questions: mostly multiple choice with three options, plus some matching and true/false. Open answers and justified true/false belong to the older format.

questions.stem: What does "J'ai réussi le DELF A2 !" mean?
choices: I registered for the DELF A2.
I revised for the DELF A2.
questions.explanation: "Réussir" an exam = to pass it. "Passer" an exam = to take it, "s'inscrire" = to register, "réviser" = to revise.

questions.stem: Complete: "Elle ___ son diplôme en juin."
questions.explanation: "Obtenir" follows venir in the present (elle obtient) but takes avoir in the passé composé: "elle a obtenu". The participle is "obtenu".

questions.stem: Complete: "Vous ___ votre ville en quelques phrases."
questions.explanation: "Décrire" is conjugated like "écrire", with a v in the plural: nous décrivons, vous décrivez. (Its futur is "vous décrirez", with no v.)

questions.stem: Which of these is an A2 can-do statement?
choices: I can follow a fast radio debate about politics.
I can write a detailed essay with arguments for and against.
I can understand a long film without subtitles.
I can describe in simple terms what I did last weekend.
questions.explanation: A2 is about short, routine, everyday communication: describing your background, past experiences and plans in simple terms. Fast debates, detailed essays and long films are B2 or higher.

questions.stem: In a multiple-choice listening question, one option repeats words you heard in the recording. What should you remember?
choices: It is always the right answer.
It may be a trap: the right option often uses other words.
questions.explanation: Wrong options often reuse words from the document to tempt you; the right option often says the same thing in other words. Check the meaning, not the words.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je ___ quand le téléphone a sonné."
questions.explanation: An action going on when something else happened takes the imparfait ("je dormais"); the interruption takes the passé composé ("a sonné"). See the decision chart.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu as vu Marie ? — Oui, je ___ ai vue hier."
questions.explanation: "Marie" is a direct object (voir quelqu'un), so "la", which elides to "l'" before "ai": "je l'ai vue". The participle agrees with "la" (vue). "Lui" is indirect (à quelqu'un); "y" replaces à + place or thing.

questions.stem: Complete so that it means "I would like to come, but I have to work": "Je ___ venir, mais je dois travailler."
questions.explanation: "Would like" is the conditionnel: future stem "voudr-" + imparfait ending "-ais" = "je voudrais". "Je voudrai" (no s) is the futur, "I will want"; it sounds almost the same.

questions.stem: Write the nous form of "corriger" (to correct): "Nous ___ nos fautes."
questions.explanation: Verbs in -ger keep an e before -ons so that the g stays soft: nous corrigeons, like nous mangeons.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "I didn't read it again."
questions.explanation: "Je ne l'ai pas relu." In the passé composé the pronoun goes before avoir, and ne … pas surrounds the pronoun and the auxiliary (lesson 8).

questions.stem: Match each part of the DELF A2 with its time.
questions.explanation: Listening 25 min, reading 30 min, writing 45 min (1 h 40 together), speaking 6–8 min after 10 minutes of preparation.

questions.stem: Which statements about the DELF A2 are true? Select all that apply.
choices: Each of the four parts is marked out of 25.
You must pass the DELF A1 before you can take the A2.
The speaking test is taken separately from the written papers.
questions.explanation: Four parts of 25 points; each recording is played twice; the speaking test is separate. The pass mark is 50/100 (with 5/25 in each part), and the DELF levels are independent diplomas: you can register directly for the A2.

questions.stem: Name each numbered part of the DELF A2.

image.alt: The DELF A2 overview chart without the names of the parts. Numbered boxes: in the written papers, 25 min, 30 min and 45 min, each 25 points; in the speaking test, 10 min to prepare then 6 to 8 min, 25 points.

questions.explanation: The times identify the parts: 25 min is listening, 30 min reading, 45 min writing, and 6–8 min after preparation the speaking test. The DELF A2 has no separate grammar or translation paper.

questions.stem: What does the headline "Hausse des prix" mean?
choices: Prices are the same as last year.
questions.explanation: "La hausse" is a rise (from hausser; the usual verb is augmenter). A fall would be "Baisse des prix".

questions.stem: Which headline means "Le chômage baisse"?
questions.explanation: In the nominal style the verb "baisser" (to fall) becomes the noun "la baisse", followed by de + what falls: "Baisse du chômage" (de + le = du).

questions.stem: What is the noun of "fermer", as in "___ de la piscine cet été"?
questions.explanation: Fermer → la fermeture, like ouvrir → l'ouverture (-ure nouns are feminine). "Fermement" is an adverb (firmly), not a noun.

questions.stem: What does "Le voleur a été arrêté." mean?
questions.explanation: "A été" + participle is the passive: the thief undergoes the action. "Arrêter" (to stop) also means "to arrest". "Will be arrested" would be "sera arrêté".

questions.stem: Complete: "Deux personnes ont été ___ dans l'accident."
questions.explanation: In the passive the participle agrees with the subject, like an adjective. "Personne" is always feminine, so "deux personnes … blessées" (feminine plural), even if they are men.

questions.stem: Which passive sentence means the same as "On a arrêté le voleur"?
questions.explanation: The object of the active sentence (le voleur) becomes the subject, and the verb becomes être (a été) + participle. "S'est arrêté" means "stopped", and "est arrivé" means "arrived".

questions.stem: Which sentence is a passive?
questions.explanation: A passive in the passé composé has two auxiliaries: "a été" + participle. "Est partie", "est arrivé" and "sommes restés" are the ordinary passé composé of être verbs (active).

questions.stem: In a news item you read: "Le voleur serait un homme de 30 ans." What does it mean?
choices: The thief was a man of 30.
The thief will be 30 years old.
The thief is reportedly a man of 30.
The thief wants to be a man of 30.
questions.explanation: Journalists use the conditionnel for information they haven't confirmed: "serait" = is said to be, reportedly. This use is B1; just recognise it.

questions.stem: Read again the fait divers about the fire in the lesson. When did the firefighters arrive?
questions.explanation: "Les pompiers sont arrivés au bout de dix minutes": after ten minutes. 23 heures was roughly when the fire started ("il était environ 23 heures").

questions.stem: In a story about a theft, "La police a ouvert une enquête" means the police have opened…
questions.explanation: "L'enquête" here is an investigation. It can also be a survey, but an opinion poll is "un sondage"; a strike is "une grève"; the front page is "la une".

questions.stem: Write the headline noun for "arriver" (it ends in -ée): "___ du nouveau directeur lundi"
questions.explanation: Arriver → l'arrivée (feminine, -ée), like entrer → l'entrée. Headlines often leave out the article: "Arrivée du nouveau directeur".

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "The new mayor has been elected."
questions.explanation: "Le nouveau maire a été élu." Subject, then a été + the participle (élu, from élire). "Nouveau" goes before the noun.

questions.stem: Match each headline with the sentence it stands for.
choices: Les conducteurs de train font grève.
questions.explanation: Each headline noun stands for a verb: hausse → augmenter, baisse → baisser, grève → faire grève, ouverture → ouvrir. "Un musée ferme" would be "Fermeture d'un musée".

questions.stem: Which sentences are passives? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Passives are être + participle with the subject undergoing the action: a été fermé, seront publiés (futur of être), ont été blessées. "Elle est sortie" is the passé composé of sortir (active), and "On a publié" is active with on.

questions.stem: Name each numbered part of this front page.

image.alt: The front page of an invented newspaper, Le Courrier de Rouvigny, without tags. Numbered: the large headline about the tram, the date under the paper's name, a photo of a tram, a small box about a fire with two injured, and a sun and cloud with temperatures.

questions.explanation: 1 is the main headline (le titre), 2 the date, 3 the photo, 4 a short news item about an incident (le fait divers), and 5 the weather (la météo). There is no advert on this page.

questions.stem: How does part 1 of the DELF A2 speaking test (entretien dirigé) work?
choices: about 5 minutes on a topic you prepared
a role play in which the examiner plays a shop assistant
about 1 min 30 of questions about yourself, not prepared
questions.explanation: Part 1 is a short guided interview about you (family, work, hobbies), without preparation. The prepared talk is part 2 and the role play part 3.

questions.stem: In which part of the speaking test does the examiner play a role?
questions.explanation: In the "exercice en interaction" the examiner plays a role (a receptionist, a friend, a shop assistant) and you must reach a result together.

questions.stem: What does "Vous pouvez reformuler ?" ask the examiner to do?
choices: say it again in other words
questions.explanation: "Reformuler" = to rephrase. To hear the same words again, ask "Vous pouvez répéter ?".

questions.stem: Complete: "Tu habites à Paris ? — ___, j'habite en banlieue, à Montreuil."
questions.explanation: "En fait" (actually) corrects what the other person thought: not Paris itself, but a suburb. "En effet" would confirm ("indeed"), which contradicts the rest of the answer.

questions.stem: With the examiner, which word is a safer choice than the very informal "du coup"?
questions.explanation: "Du coup" (so, as a result) is very common in casual speech, but "donc" or "alors" is safer in an exam. "Ouais" and "bof" are informal too, and a string of "euh" sounds unprepared.

questions.stem: You hear "T'as vu ?". What is the standard form?
questions.explanation: In relaxed speech "tu" loses its u before a vowel: "t'as" = "tu as". Recognise it, but write and say "tu as" in the exam.

questions.stem: What does "C'est pas grave." mean?
questions.explanation: It is "Ce n'est pas grave" with "ne" dropped, as in most casual speech: "it doesn't matter, no problem". Keep "ne" in the exam.

questions.stem: In the role play, the examiner uses the word "trimestre" and you don't know it. What is the best thing to do?
choices: Ask in English what it means.
Ask: « Qu'est-ce que ça veut dire, trimestre ? »
questions.explanation: Asking for the meaning in French is a repair strategy, and examiners expect it at A2. Pretending, silence or English all break the conversation.

questions.stem: The instructions say "Donnez deux arguments." What should you do?
questions.explanation: "Un argument" in French is a reason that supports an opinion. A quarrel is "une dispute".

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Age takes avoir in French, with "ans": "J'ai 34 ans". "Je suis 34 ans" copies English and is one of the most common mistakes at the oral.

questions.stem: Write the verb: "Pardon, vous pouvez ___, s'il vous plaît ?" (say it again, the same words)
questions.explanation: "Vous pouvez répéter, s'il vous plaît ?" asks for the same words again. "Reformuler" asks for other words.

questions.stem: Put the three parts of the DELF A2 speaking test in order.
questions.explanation: First the guided interview about yourself (about 1 min 30), then the short talk (about 2 min), then the role play (about 3–4 min).

questions.stem: What do you say in each case?
left: You'd like it in other words.
questions.explanation: Répéter = say again; reformuler = say in other words; préciser = give more detail; "Pardon, je veux dire…" corrects yourself. "Du coup" is a filler meaning "so".

questions.stem: Which of these are fillers that buy you time to think? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Euh", "bon" and "en fait" fill a pause or start a sentence while you think. "Volontiers" (gladly) and "malgré" (despite) carry meaning.

questions.stem: Correct yourself: "Je suis allé à Lyon… pardon, je ___ dire à Lille."
questions.explanation: "Pardon, je veux dire…" (or "je voulais dire…") = sorry, I mean… It repairs a slip without stopping the conversation.

cards.back: Histoires ou contes du temps passé, avec des moralités (Paris, Claude Barbin, 1697), also called Contes de ma mère l'Oye. Eight prose tales, each with a moral in verse.

cards.front: How does Perrault's Petit Chaperon rouge end?
cards.back: The wolf eats the girl, and the story stops. A moralité in verse follows: beware of smooth-talking "wolves". No hunter, no rescue.
First edition of their Kinder- und Hausmärchen. A hunter (un chasseur) cuts the wolf open; the girl and her grandmother come out alive; the wolf's belly is filled with stones.

cards.front: « Tire la chevillette, la bobinette cherra. »
cards.back: Pull the little peg and the latch will fall. Chevillette = small wooden peg; bobinette = wooden latch; cherra = future of the old verb choir (to fall).

cards.front: « Ma mère-grand, que vous avez de grandes dents ! »
cards.back: "Grandmother, what big teeth you have!" Answer: « C'est pour te manger. » (Mère-grand = grand-mère, old.)
il -a, ils -èrent: il rencontra, ils rencontrèrent; il alla. -ger keeps e (il mangea), -cer takes ç (il commença).
-it / -irent: dit, fit, mit, prit, finit, s'ouvrit. -ut / -urent: fut, eut, voulut, put, sut. venir: vint / vinrent; tenir: tint.
Written: imparfait (background) + passé simple (events). Spoken: imparfait + passé composé. Il la dévora = il l'a dévorée.

cards.back: Passé simple (he said, he finished), not the present: look at the other verbs around them.
To be wary of, not to trust: Méfie-toi des inconnus ! (Be wary of strangers!)
Couplet = a verse of a song (the words change). Refrain = the chorus (the same words come back). Les paroles = the lyrics.

cards.front: Au clair de la lune: two grammar points
cards.back: Prête-moi, Ouvre-moi: affirmative imperative + moi (me → moi). Je n'ai plus de feu: ne … plus + de.

cards.front: Sur le pont d'Avignon: what is y?
cards.back: L'on y danse = people dance there; y = sur le pont (a place). L'on is an older, elegant on.
The pont Saint-Bénézet over the Rhône, 12th century; floods broke it; 4 of its 22 arches are left. The song (author unknown) became famous in 1853 through Adolphe Adam.
Words: Jean-Baptiste Clément, 1866. Music: Antoine Renard, 1868. Tied to the Paris Commune (May 1871). Public domain.

cards.front: Quand nous en serons au temps des cerises …
cards.back: Futur after quand for a future time: serons, seront, auront, sifflera. English uses the present ("when we get to").

cards.front: Imparfait or futur in a song?
cards.back: Imparfait to look back (memories, habits, nostalgia); futur to look forward (promises, hopes).

Édith Piaf (1915–1963); Georges Brassens (1921–1981, from Sète, guitar); Jacques Brel (1929–1978, Belgian); Barbara (1930–1997, piano, Göttingen 1964). Their songs are in copyright: name and discuss them, don't copy lyrics.
The Lumière brothers' first public screening for a paying audience, Salon indien of the Grand Café, boulevard des Capucines, Paris: ten films of under a minute each.
A magician who turned to film: studio at Montreuil (1897), camera tricks, Le Voyage dans la Lune (1902), about 500 films.
Planned for September 1939 (war); first held 20 September 1946; in May since 1952; Palme d'or since 1955.
France's national film awards, created by Georges Cravenne on the model of the Oscars; first ceremony 3 April 1976; trophy by the sculptor César.
VO = original language; VOST = original with French subtitles (sous-titres); VF = dubbed into French (doublé).
tourner un film = to shoot; réaliser = to direct (le réalisateur); le prix = the prize; un film muet = a silent film; jouer un rôle = to play a part.
The film is émouvant (moving), décevant (disappointing); the person is ému (moved), déçu (disappointed).

cards.front: Five parts of a short review
cards.back: Title and facts → short summary in the present (no ending) → points for, with reasons → points against → recommendation and a mark.
qui / que / où (un film qui fait du bien); plus … que, le meilleur … de; à mon avis, je trouve que, par contre; vraiment, complètement.
La librairie = bookshop (you buy); la bibliothèque = library (you borrow).
Madame, Monsieur, … Je vous prie d'agréer, Madame, Monsieur, l'expression de mes salutations distinguées. (Or simply Cordialement.)
Pourriez-vous me dire si la chambre est disponible ? Je voudrais savoir combien coûtent les charges.
Accueillir (like cueillir). The participle agrees with the direct object m' (Kate, feminine) because it comes before avoir.

cards.front: Ma famille me manque. / Tu me manques.
cards.back: With manquer, what you miss is the subject: I miss my family. / I miss you.

cards.front: le mal du pays / le dépaysement
cards.back: Le mal du pays = homesickness (avoir le mal du pays). Le dépaysement = the feeling of being far from home and your habits, pleasant or hard.
To get used to, to adjust to: je m'habitue à la ville; j'ai eu du mal à m'adapter.

cards.back: To take stock; to make progress; to say goodbye (for a long time).

cards.back: j'avais, je faisais, je prenais, j'allais (from nous avons, faisons, prenons, allons)
je mangeais, nous mangions; je commençais, nous commencions (e and ç only before a)

cards.back: nous étudiions, vous étudiiez (stem étudi- + -ions: two i's)

cards.back: imparfait: background (time, weather, place, people, feelings, what was going on, habits); passé composé: events that move the story on
Je dormais (imparfait) quand le téléphone a sonné (passé composé).
a verb, usually imparfait: Pendant que je faisais les courses, … (pendant + noun = during)

cards.back: background on that day / sums up a whole finished period (il a fait beau toute la semaine)

cards.back: me, te, se, nous, vous → le, la, les → lui, leur → y → en

cards.front: Je te le donne / Je le lui donne
cards.back: Columns 1 then 2 (person before thing); columns 2 then 3 (thing before lui, leur).
Il y en a. (y before en)

cards.front: Two pronouns in the passé composé
cards.back: The pair goes before the auxiliary: Je le lui ai dit. Je ne le lui ai pas dit.
The pair goes before the infinitive: Je vais te le montrer.
Donne-le-moi ! (affirmative command: direct object first, then the person)
Donnez-m'en ! (en last; moi → m' before en)
Statement order, before the verb: Ne me le donne pas !
Often stands for Je le lui ai dit: le is dropped before lui. Recognise it; write the full form.
flatshare / flatmate (informal: la coloc, le coloc)
stepfather or father-in-law / stepmother or mother-in-law
half-brother, half-sister (one parent in common); in speech also step-siblings. Plural les demi-frères.
blended family / single-parent family
pacte civil de solidarité: created by the law of 15 November 1999, for two adults of the same or different sexes

cards.front: Marriage for same-sex couples in France
cards.back: Law of 17 May 2013; first wedding in Montpellier on 29 May 2013
about 66 % "traditional", 25 % single-parent, 9 % blended
shared custody: the children live with each parent in turn

cards.front: Reciprocal verbs: agreement in the passé composé
cards.back: se = direct (rencontrer qqn): ils se sont rencontrés. se = indirect (parler à qqn): ils se sont parlé.

cards.front: Ils se sont écrit / plu / souri / téléphoné
cards.back: No agreement: écrire, plaire, sourire, téléphoner take à + person, so se is indirect.

cards.front: Elles se sont vues / mariées / disputées
cards.back: Agreement: se is direct (voir qqn), or the verb agrees with the subject (se marier, se disputer).
plus / moins / aussi + adjective + que: plus calme que, moins cher que, aussi grand que. The adjective agrees.
plus de / moins de / autant de + noun (+ que): plus de bruit, autant d'habitants.
verb + plus / moins / autant (que): Il travaille plus que moi. Tu manges autant que lui.
a stressed pronoun: plus grand que moi, que toi, que lui, qu'elle, que nous, que vous, qu'eux.
good → meilleur (adjective, agrees: une meilleure idée); well → mieux (adverb, never changes: il chante mieux). Never plus bon, plus bien.
pire or plus mauvais (adjective); plus mal (adverb). le pire = the worst.
le / la / les + plus / moins + adjective. After the noun the article comes twice: la ville la plus animée; before it once: la plus grande ville.
de: le plus grand musée de France, la rue la plus animée du quartier.
after the noun = clean (une rue propre); before it = own (ma propre chambre).
Strictly, une rivière flows into another river; un fleuve flows into the sea (la Seine, le Rhône). In speech, rivière is often used for both.
subject: a verb follows. l'appli qui marche. For people and things; never qu'.
object: a subject follows. le site que j'utilise; qu' before a vowel. Never left out (the film I saw = le film que j'ai vu).
place or time: la ville où j'habite, le jour où je suis arrivé (never le jour quand).

cards.front: qui or que? the quick test
cards.back: Cover the pronoun and look right: a verb → qui; a subject (je, tu, Marie…) → que.
The participle agrees with the antecedent: les photos que j'ai prises, la vidéo que tu as faite.
Puts one part in the spotlight: C'est Léa qui a le mot de passe. C'est ce site que j'utilise.

cards.front: Describing a thing you can't name
cards.back: C'est un truc qui sert à + infinitive … / C'est une machine qu'on utilise pour … / Ça sert à quoi ?
a mobile phone, and also short for l'ordinateur portable (laptop).
the one(s): masc. sing., fem. sing., masc. plural, fem. plural. They agree with the noun they replace.
+ -ci / -là (celui-ci), + de (celle de Paul = Paul's), + qui / que (ceux que j'ai achetés).
for things with no noun: ça (everyday), cela (careful, written), ceci (rare). Je voudrais ça. Ça me plaît.
le mien / la mienne / les miens / les miennes; le tien…; le sien… (agrees with the thing owned).
le nôtre, la nôtre, les nôtres; le vôtre…; le leur, la leur, les leurs. nôtre / vôtre with a circumflex.
la sienne: the pronoun agrees with clé (feminine), not with Paul.
C'est à moi / à toi / à Paul. = It's mine / yours / Paul's (everyday).
en + material, no article: en bois, en métal, en plastique, en cuir, en coton, en laine, en or, en argent (silver), en verre (glass).
feminine + -ment: douce → doucement, sérieuse → sérieusement, complète → complètement.
masculine ending in a vowel + -ment: vrai → vraiment, poli → poliment, facile → facilement.
-ant → -amment, -ent → -emment, both said "a-MAHN": couramment, évidemment, patiemment (but lent → lentement).
bon → bien, mauvais → mal, gentil → gentiment, précis → précisément. vite is already an adverb (adjective: rapide).
short common ones before the participle (j'ai bien dormi, il a vraiment aimé); -ment adverbs of manner usually after (il a parlé lentement).
Je m'ennuie (s'ennuyer). Je suis ennuyeux = I'm boring.
content = pleased (about something: content de te voir); heureux = happy (deeper).
angry; never changes: elle est en colère, ils sont en colère.
replaces de + noun: le livre dont je parle (parler de), l'outil dont j'ai besoin (avoir besoin de). B1 preview.
un ami dont le père est pilote; un roman dont j'ai oublié le titre (normal word order after dont).
The verb decides: no preposition → que; de → dont; a place or time → où; a verb follows → qui.
= what (the thing that). ce qui + verb: Ce qui me plaît, c'est …; ce que + subject: Ce que j'aime, c'est …

cards.front: Ce qui me plaît: why qui?
cards.back: me is an object pronoun, not a subject, so ce is the subject → ce qui.
never dont son père (→ dont le père); never dont j'en parle (→ dont je parle).
B1: la table sur laquelle j'écris, l'ami avec qui je travaille. At A2, où often works for places.
parler de, avoir besoin de, se souvenir de, avoir peur de, être fier de, se servir de, se passer de, se moquer de, avoir honte de, profiter de, hériter de.
le roman = novel (romance = une histoire d'amour); le personnage = character in a story (personality = le caractère).
Paris 2 103 778, Marseille 886 040, Lyon 519 127, Toulouse 514 819 (legal figures in force from 1 January 2026).
Paris 20 (1st–4th grouped as Paris Centre), Marseille 16, Lyon 9. le 11e = le onzième.
Métropole de Lyon (1 Jan 2015, about 1.4 million), Métropole du Grand Paris (2016, 131 communes, 7+ million), Aix-Marseille-Provence (2016, 92 communes, about 1.9 million).
Marseille about 240.6 km², Paris 105.4 km², Lyon 47.9 km²: Marseille is more than twice as big as Paris on the map.
Marseille, founded around 600 BC by Greek sailors from Phocaea (Phocée).
beaucoup plus, un peu moins, presque aussi … que, deux fois plus (de) … que, de loin (by far).
a space between groups of three digits (2 103 778), a comma for decimals (105,4 km²).
nickname (false friend). A surname is le nom de famille.

cards.front: Opinions vs facts in a guide
cards.back: Mark reputations: on dit que…, dit-on, pour beaucoup de Français, disent ses visiteurs.
nous present − -ons + -ant: parlant, finissant, prenant, faisant, mangeant, commençant.
être → étant, avoir → ayant, savoir → sachant.
en + present participle: en écoutant, en faisant. It never agrees.
while (Je mange en écoutant la radio), by (On apprend en pratiquant), when / on (En arrivant, j'ai vu Paul).
always the subject of the main verb. Two subjects → pendant que or quand.
I like reading = j'aime lire; before leaving = avant de partir; without saying = sans dire; I'm reading = je lis.
stresses that two things happen at the same time (often with contrast): Elle révise tout en regardant la télé.
the pronoun goes between en and the participle: en la parlant, en me levant.
je conduis, nous conduisons, ils conduisent; j'ai conduit; en conduisant.

cards.front: en même temps / à la fois
cards.back: at the same time; à la fois also = both: C'est à la fois simple et efficace.

cards.front: Futur simple: how to build it
cards.back: Infinitive + -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont (the present of avoir). -re verbs drop the e: prendre → je prendrai.
être ser-, avoir aur-, aller ir-, faire fer-, venir viendr-, devenir deviendr-, pouvoir pourr-.
vouloir voudr-, devoir devr-, savoir saur-, voir verr-, envoyer enverr-, recevoir recevr-; il faudra, il pleuvra.
je prévoirai (not "prévrai"): unlike voir (je verrai). Present je prévois, nous prévoyons; participle prévu.
je present + r: j'achèterai, j'appellerai, je jetterai, je paierai / payerai. préférer: je préférerai (1990: préfèrerai).
Futur proche: decided, near, everyday speech (je vais partir). Futur simple: predictions, promises, further ahead, writing (il fera beau, je t'appellerai). Often both are fine.
For a future action: Quand je serai grand, je serai pilote (When I grow up). For a habit, the present: Quand il pleut, je prends le bus.

cards.front: How sure? certainement, sûrement, probablement, peut-être
cards.back: From most to least sure. Sûrement usually = very probably. At the start: peut-être que (Peut-être qu'il viendra).
Future stem + imparfait endings -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient: je voudrais, tu pourrais, il serait, nous aimerions, vous devriez, ils auraient.
Pourriez-vous m'aider ? Est-ce que vous auriez une chambre ? Ce serait possible de payer par carte ? Je voudrais réserver …
Tu devrais + infinitive (you should). À ta place, je partirais (if I were you). Il faudrait + infinitive.
On pourrait + infinitive: On pourrait faire une excursion demain. (We could …)
ferai = I will do (futur); ferais = I would do (conditionnel). Test with nous: ferons / ferions.
A rental: une location de voiture = a car hire. "A location" = un endroit, un lieu.
complet (complète) = fully booked; disponible = available; compris = included (petit-déjeuner compris).
visiter + a place (visiter un musée); rendre visite à + a person (rendre visite à ma tante).
Si + present → present, futur or imperative. Si tu es fatigué, repose-toi. S'il fait beau, on ira à la plage. Never the futur after si (= if).
s'il, s'ils, but si elle, si on, si un ami.

cards.front: il ne faut pas vs tu n'es pas obligé de
cards.back: Il ne faut pas fumer = you must not smoke. Tu n'es pas obligé(e) de venir = you don't have to come.
Il vaut mieux + infinitive (no de) = it's better to: Il vaut mieux dormir. Il vaut mieux ne pas fumer.
conseiller à quelqu'un de + infinitive: Le médecin m'a conseillé de bouger.
Affirmative: pronoun after, with a hyphen (Prends-le. Repose-toi.). Negative: pronoun before (Ne le prends pas. Ne te repose pas.).
Like partir: je me sens, il se sent, nous nous sentons. Je me sens bien / mal. (sentir alone = to smell)
il pleut, il a plu, il pleuvait, il va pleuvoir, il pleuvra. The subject il never changes.
il fait beau, il a fait beau, il faisait beau, il va faire beau, il fera beau.
Il est important / nécessaire / interdit / possible de + infinitive. In speech: C'est important de trier.

cards.front: c'est important or il est important?
cards.back: Nothing after the adjective: only c'est (Trier ? Oui, c'est important.). With de + infinitive: both (il est is more formal).
je jette, nous jetons, je jetterai. je protège, nous protégeons, je protégerai (1990: protègerai).
Purpose: On trie pour recycler. J'éteins la lumière pour économiser l'électricité.
Since 1 Jan 2023: all packaging in the yellow bin (almost everywhere). Glass: bottle bank. Bin colours vary by town: check locally.
Real: si + present → futur (Si j'ai le temps, je viendrai). Imaginary: si + imparfait → conditionnel (Si j'avais le temps, je viendrais).
No conditionnel after si: Si j'avais (not "si j'aurais") le temps, je viendrais.
= à ta place (if I were you) + conditionnel: Si j'étais toi, je prendrais le train. Toi, not tu.
Answer with si + imparfait and the conditionnel: Si je gagnais au loto, j'achèterais une maison et je ferais le tour du monde.
A suggestion (How about going …?), lesson 22: si on + imparfait + ?, with no main clause and no conditionnel.
If I had known … (B1: si + plus-que-parfait + conditionnel passé: Si j'avais su, je serais venu). Recognise only.
5 numbers out of 49 and 1 lucky number out of 10: 1,906,884 × 10 = 1 chance in 19,068,840.
That would be great! (conditionnel of être). Also: Ce serait super !
1 Jan 2023: all packaging in the yellow bin (almost all of metropolitan France). 1 Jan 2024: every council must offer food-waste sorting.
To the bottle bank (la colonne à verre), not the yellow bin; lids separately.
Réduire → réutiliser → recycler → jeter (from best to least good).

cards.front: Plastic bags and the anti-waste law
cards.back: Single-use plastic checkout bags banned 1 July 2016. Loi AGEC, 10 Feb 2020: no destroying unsold non-food goods, sorting info on products, bonus réparation.
des vêtements d'occasion (never changes); des produits locaux (-al → -aux); des légumes bio (usually invariable).
vide-grenier: a street sale of people's old things (car-boot / yard sale). friperie: second-hand clothes shop.
le vélo en libre-service: Vélo'v in Lyon (2005), Vélib' in Paris (15 July 2007). le covoiturage = car-sharing.
Futur to predict (l'air sera plus propre), il faut / il ne faut pas for duties, il vaudrait mieux to suggest.
Verb gaspiller (to waste) → noun le gaspillage; le gaspillage alimentaire = food waste.
A mood used after certain expressions with que (il faut que, vouloir que) for actions needed or wanted, not stated as facts. B1: recognise it at A2.
ils present − ent + -e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent: ils partent → que je parte, que nous partions.
être sois, avoir aie, aller aille, faire fasse, pouvoir puisse, savoir sache.

cards.front: être and avoir in the subjunctive
cards.back: que je sois, tu sois, il soit, nous soyons, vous soyez, ils soient. que j'aie, tu aies, il ait, nous ayons, vous ayez, ils aient.

cards.front: Je veux partir or je veux que je parte?
cards.back: Same subject → infinitive: Je veux partir. Subjunctive only for someone else: Je veux que tu partes.
Il faut que tu fasses … → Tu dois faire … / Il faut faire … Both are correct.

cards.front: que je parle: present or subjunctive?
cards.back: For -er verbs the je, tu, il, ils forms look the same. The trigger (il faut que) tells you it is the subjunctive.
la colocation (la coloc), le / la colocataire, à tour de rôle (taking turns), c'est ton tour, le planning (rota), les tâches ménagères.
ne … pas (not), plus (no longer), jamais (never), rien (nothing), personne (nobody), aucun(e) + noun (not a single), nulle part (nowhere), que (only). Only one second word: never pas as well.

cards.front: Passé composé: where does the second word go?
cards.back: pas, plus, jamais, rien BEFORE the participle (je n'ai rien vu); personne, aucun, que, nulle part AFTER it (je n'ai vu personne).
Personne n'est venu. Rien ne marche. As the subject: ne straight after, no pas.
only (a restriction, not a negative): je n'ai que dix euros. The article stays: je n'ai que du pain.
not a single, no: + singular noun, agreeing with it: je n'ai aucune idée, aucun problème.
Merci de ne pas fumer. Ne pas (ne plus, ne jamais, ne rien) together before an infinitive.
personne = nobody (no article, with ne: Personne n'est là). la personne = a person, always feminine: deux personnes.
trade or profession; a job (employment: chercher un emploi); one position in a company (un poste de vendeur). La poste = the post office.

cards.front: The job hunt in five words
cards.back: l'offre d'emploi (advert) → postuler (apply) → la candidature (application: CV + letter) → l'entretien (interview) → embaucher (hire).
chaque + singular noun (chaque jour); chacun, chacune alone, singular verb (chacun a son livre).

cards.front: toute la journée / tous les jours
cards.back: the whole day / every day. Singular tout = the whole; plural tous, toutes = every, all.

cards.front: When is the s of tous pronounced?
cards.back: When tous is a pronoun (all of them): Ils sont tous là, "toos". Before a noun it is silent: tous les jours.
everyone, + singular verb: Tout le monde est là. (The whole world = le monde entier.)
several (no article: plusieurs fois), a few (quelques amis), some of a group (certains étudiants).
quelque chose d'intéressant, quelqu'un de sympa: de + masculine adjective (also rien de nouveau, personne d'important).
sometimes (= parfois) / a few times.

cards.front: French degrees in years after the bac
cards.back: BTS bac + 2; licence bac + 3; master bac + 5; doctorat bac + 8.
to take an exam; to pass it; to fail it (informal; formal: échouer à un examen).
dire / répondre / expliquer que + sentence. Que is never dropped and is repeated: Elle dit qu'elle est désolée et que ma carte est bloquée.
Il nous dit de patienter. dire / demander à quelqu'un de + infinitive.
si: Il demande si tu viens. si + il = s'il, but si elle.

cards.front: qu'est-ce que / qu'est-ce qui in an indirect question
cards.back: ce que (object): Dites-moi ce que vous voulez. ce qui (subject): Je ne sais pas ce qui se passe.

cards.front: Word order in an indirect question
cards.back: No est-ce que, no inversion, no question mark unless the whole sentence asks: Il demande où tu habites. Pourriez-vous me dire où est l'accueil ?
the time allowed, deadline (un délai de dix jours) / a delay, lateness (le train a du retard).
le compte, la carte bancaire (la CB), le distributeur (cash machine), retirer de l'argent, le virement (transfer), le code (PIN), le conseiller / la conseillère.
to let know, to warn; like venir but with avoir: je préviens, j'ai prévenu, je préviendrai. Préviens-moi !
because (everyday, answers Pourquoi ?); because (written, never with the cause first); as, since (first in the sentence: Comme il pleuvait, on est restés).
+ noun or pronoun: because of (bad result: à cause du retard) / thanks to (good result: grâce à toi).
donc (so), alors (so, spoken), c'est pourquoi (that's why, formal; spoken c'est pour ça que).
J'appelle pour réserver. pour + infinitive (same person); pour + noun = for. pour que + subjunctive is B1.

cards.front: avant de, sans, au lieu de
cards.back: + infinitive where English uses -ing: avant de signer, sans payer, au lieu de répondre.
indeed, in fact, that's right: it confirms or explains. Not "in effect".
fault, blame (ce n'est pas ma faute; une faute d'orthographe) / a mistake in general (une erreur sur la facture).
to get the wrong …: je me suis trompé de numéro, d'adresse.

cards.front: The usual order of a French CV
cards.back: coordonnées (état civil) → title → profile → expérience professionnelle → formation → langues → compétences → centres d'intérêt.
l'ordre antichronologique: most recent first, in the experience and education sections.
Optional (service-public.fr, checked November 2026). You don't have to give your family situation; an employer may only ask for information linked to the job (Code du travail L1221-6).
Gestion des réservations: date first, short noun phrases (accueil des clients, prise de commandes).
langue maternelle, bilingue, courant (fluent), bon niveau, notions (basics), or a CEFR level (français B2).
vous (the company), moi (you), nous (what you will bring + interview request); one page; formal closing.
Je me permets de vous adresser ma candidature pour le poste de … / Votre annonce a retenu toute mon attention.

cards.front: Formal closing of a cover letter
cards.back: Dans l'attente de votre réponse, je vous prie d'agréer, Madame, Monsieur, l'expression de mes salutations distinguées.
currently, now (not "actually" = en fait): Actuellement étudiant en tourisme, …

cards.front: Present, futur or conditionnel in a cover letter?
cards.back: Strengths in the present or futur (mon expérience sera un atout); the conditionnel for polite requests (je serais heureux de vous rencontrer).
town hall: état civil (birth certificates, weddings), school enrolment, ID cards and passports (equipped mairies only).
the State's office in each département: residence permits (titre de séjour), mostly online now. Driving licences and carte grise online since 6 November 2017.
the green card proving you are covered by the Assurance maladie; own card from 16; an app version exists. Show it at the doctor's and pharmacy.
private top-up health insurance. Since 1 January 2016 private-sector employers must offer one and pay at least half.
the regular doctor you declare to the Assurance maladie; without one you are usually paid back much less.
Caisse d'allocations familiales: family benefits and housing aid (les allocations).
relevé d'identité bancaire: your bank details (IBAN, BIC) for salary, benefits, direct debits. Never your card number or code.
15 digits: a 13-digit number (sex, year and month of birth, place of birth, order number) + a 2-digit key.

cards.front: Official letter: "dans un délai de quinze jours à compter de la date de ce courrier"
cards.back: within fifteen days from the date of this letter: count from the date on the letter, not from when you open it.

cards.front: Official letter: "Nous vous prions de bien vouloir nous adresser …"
cards.back: Please send us … (les pièces justificatives = the supporting documents).
je pense que (general), je trouve que (from experience), je crois que (less sure). Que is never left out: Je pense qu'il a raison.
à mon avis, selon moi, pour moi, d'après moi + the sentence: À mon avis, c'est trop long.
Qu'est-ce que tu en penses ? / Tu en penses quoi ? (informal) / Qu'est-ce que vous pensez de … ?

cards.front: penser à / penser de / penser que
cards.back: à = think about (Je pense à toi); de = opinion of, in questions (Qu'est-ce que tu penses de ce film ?); que = think that (Je pense qu'il est long).
Je pense que non. / Je ne pense pas. / Je crois que non. To go on: Je pense que ce n'est pas … (avoids the subjunctive).

cards.front: to agree / to be right / to be wrong
cards.back: être d'accord (avec) / avoir raison / avoir tort. Not "j'ai d'accord" or "je suis raison".
au contraire = on the contrary (you are wrong); par contre = on the other hand (a second side).
yet, however: a surprising contrast. Il a révisé. Pourtant, il a raté l'examen.
all the same, even so; after the verb or at the end: On est quand même sortis. / On est sortis quand même.
les informations / les infos (plural); le journal télévisé (le JT). One piece of news: une nouvelle.
A suggestion, "How about …?": Si on allait au cinéma ? Not about the past, no second half.
Ça te dit de + infinitive ? / Tu as envie de … ? / On pourrait … / Je te propose de …
Volontiers ! Avec plaisir ! Quelle bonne idée ! Pourquoi pas ? Ça marche ! (casual)
Désolé(e), je ne peux pas, je dois … + a reason + Une autre fois ? (C'est dommage !)
Agrees, no article: Quel dommage ! Quelle bonne idée ! Quels beaux costumes ! Quelles belles photos ! All said [kɛl].
Normal word order: Que c'est beau ! Comme il est drôle ! (not "Comme beau c'est")
Je suis ravi(e) de venir. Je suis content(e) de te voir. Je suis désolé(e) de ne pas pouvoir venir.
se retrouver = meet up by arrangement (On se retrouve à 8 h ?); rencontrer = meet for the first time, run into.
ennuyeux (ennuyeuse) = boring; je m'ennuie = I'm bored. "Je suis ennuyeux" = I am a boring person.

cards.front: New senses: l'entrée, la place, complet
cards.back: l'entrée = admission (L'entrée est gratuite); la place = seat, ticket (Il reste des places ?); complet = sold out.
passé composé = events; imparfait = the scene and feelings; futur = plans. On est allés au mariage. Il faisait beau. On se reverra en juin.
finalement = in the end, after a change of plan; enfin = at last, or last in a list.
= quand in a time clause, more written; lorsqu'il. Never for questions (Quand est-ce que … ?).
au bout d'une heure = after an hour; en attendant = in the meantime.
despite + noun: Malgré la pluie, on est sortis. (= Il pleuvait, mais on est quand même sortis.)
merci pour + noun (merci pour le cadeau); merci de + infinitive (merci de répondre vite); chunk: merci de m'avoir invité(e).
Excuse-moi de + infinitive (de répondre si tard); Excuse-moi pour + noun (pour le retard). Formal: Je vous prie de m'excuser.
Bonne chance = good luck (where luck helps); Bon courage = hang in there (something long or hard).
close: Bises, Je t'embrasse; friendly: Amicalement, À bientôt; formal: Cordialement.
Read the task, cover every point, match tu/vous, write at least the words asked for (60 in the sample papers), then check.
listening 25 min, reading 30 min, writing 45 min (1 h 40 together); speaking 6–8 min after 10 min of preparation. 25 points each.
50/100, with at least 5/25 in every part.
Two short texts: an account of an event or experience, and a message with a purpose (invite, thank, apologise, ask, inform, congratulate).
Closed questions: mostly multiple choice with three options, plus matching and true/false. Each recording is heard twice.
passer un examen = take it; réussir = pass it; obtenir le diplôme = get it.
like venir: j'obtiens, ils obtiennent, j'obtiendrai; but with avoir: j'ai obtenu.
décrire like écrire: nous décrivons, j'ai décrit; relire like lire: nous relisons, j'ai relu.
imparfait: scene, habits, what was going on; passé composé: a finished event. Je dormais quand le téléphone a sonné.
futur: stem + -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont; conditionnel: stem + -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient. je ferai / je ferais.
You manage short, routine everyday exchanges and can talk simply about your background, the past and your plans.
A headline noun for the action + de: Hausse des prix = les prix augmentent; Baisse du chômage = le chômage baisse.
-tion (arrestation), -ure (ouverture, fermeture), -ée (arrivée), -ment (changement), stem + e (baisse, hausse); gagner → victoire.
